Cook brown rice according to package directions, adding 5g smoked paprika to the cooking water for flavor and color.
Toast cashews in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until golden. Chop roughly.
Remove chicken from oven. Discard dried Ancho chilies. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.

To serve, place a mound of smoked paprika rice on each plate. Arrange one chicken thigh beside the rice. Distribute roasted eggplant cubes, corn kernels, and broccoli florets around the plate. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and toasted cashews.
notes: Adjust cayenne pepper to desired spice level. For a milder dish, reduce or omit.
If chicken is not fully submerged during braising, flip halfway through cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage and Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, vibrant Italian Sausage and Tomato Risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto flows naturally across the plate, showcasing its rich, fluid consistency, not stiff or mounded. Arborio rice, cooked to al dente perfection, is infused with the savory depth of browned, crumbled Italian sausage and the bright acidity of crushed tomatoes. Small, even diced onion pieces and minced garlic are visible, contributing to the dish's texture and color. A generous scattering of freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts into the warm rice, adding a golden hue and umami. Fresh, whole basil leaves are artfully placed on top, providing a verdant contrast and aromatic finish. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, allowing the dish to be the clear focal point. The plate rests on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a classic fork, creating an inviting, casual dining atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty artisan bread for soaking up the creamy risotto.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Crumble sausage into small pieces.
Dice the yellow onion into small, even pieces. Mince garlic cloves.
Warm chicken broth in a separate saucepan. Keep it hot at a simmer.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add crumbled sausage to the pan. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon and set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed by the rice.
Add crushed tomatoes to the rice. Stir well to combine.
Begin adding hot broth, one ladleful (about 125 ml) at a time. Stir constantly, allowing each addition of broth to be almost completely absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is al dente (tender with a slight bite in the center). The risotto should be creamy and fluid, not dry.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until butter and cheese are fully incorporated, creating a creamy consistency (mantecatura).
Stir in the cooked sausage. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Let risotto rest for 2 minutes before serving.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Chipotle Catfish with Cassava & Ginkgo Puree
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centered with purposeful negative space. A creamy, pale-yellow mound of smooth cassava and ginkgo puree forms the base. Resting atop the puree is a whole, golden-brown pan-seared catfish fillet, its surface exhibiting a delicate crust and flaky texture. A rich, glossy, reddish-brown chipotle sauce is artfully drizzled over the catfish and around the plate, creating fluid lines. Scattered over the sauce and puree are a few vibrant green fresh cilantro leaves, adding a pop of color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.

ingredients.name: Cassava, peeled and cut into 5cm chunks

instructions: Place cassava chunks in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until very tender. Drain well.
Add cooked cassava, ginkgo nuts, milk, butter, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper to a food processor. Process until smooth and creamy. Keep warm.
Pat catfish fillets dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine smoked paprika, 5g salt, and 1g black pepper. Rub seasoning mixture evenly over both sides of each catfish fillet.

Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Place seasoned catfish fillets in the hot skillet. Cook for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Remove from skillet and keep warm.
In the same skillet, add remaining 5ml vegetable oil. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, and broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.

Dissolve kudzu starch in 15ml cold water. Whisk dissolved kudzu starch into the simmering sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens to a glossy consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Spoon a generous portion of cassava & ginkgo puree onto the center of each plate. Place one cooked catfish fillet on top of the puree.
Drizzle a spoonful of chipotle sauce over the catfish and around the plate. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Pea Puree and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single seared beef medallion, golden-brown with a savory crust, rests elegantly on a swirl of vibrant green pea puree. Around the beef, perfectly roasted carrot batons, with their soft orange hue and slight caramelization, are artfully arranged alongside tender-crisp broccoli florets, showcasing their bright green color. A delicate dollop of creamy white garlic aioli sits beside the beef, ready to complement each bite. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, leaving ample negative space to highlight the balanced composition and natural colors of the ingredients. A scattering of fresh chopped parsley adds a final touch of verdant freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, evoking a modern bistro ambiance with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss carrot batons and broccoli florets with 30ml olive oil, 2 crushed garlic cloves, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, prepare pea puree. Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Add green peas. Cook for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender. Drain immediately.
Transfer cooked peas to a food processor or blender. Add a pinch of salt and a splash of water (15-30ml) if needed. Blend until smooth. Adjust consistency and seasoning. Keep warm.
Prepare garlic aioli. In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, 2 minced garlic cloves, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Season beef medallions generously with salt and pepper on all sides. Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place beef medallions in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes to finish cooking, if desired. Remove beef from skillet.
Transfer beef to a cutting board. Rest for 5-10 minutes. Resting is crucial.
To plate, spoon a generous swirl of pea puree onto each plate. Arrange 1 seared beef medallion next to the puree. Neatly place roasted carrot batons and broccoli florets around the beef.
Dollop or drizzle garlic aioli over the beef or beside it. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A rustic and inviting skillet dish featuring golden-brown chicken pieces nestled among tender, browned mushrooms in a rich, creamy, off-white sauce. The dish is generously speckled with vibrant green fresh parsley, creating a warm and comforting appearance. It's presented in a cast-iron skillet, ready to be served.

instructions.instruction: Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Cut into 1-inch pieces. Season the chicken with 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the seasoned chicken and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides and mostly cooked through. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.

Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the same skillet. Add the diced onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release their liquid and start to brown. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Sprinkle the flour over the onion and mushroom mixture, stir well and cook for 1 minute. Slowly pour in the chicken broth, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.

Reduce heat to low. Stir in the sour cream until fully incorporated. Return the cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir to coat the chicken and mushrooms in the creamy sauce. Heat gently for 2-3 minutes until everything is warmed through. Do not boil after adding sour cream to prevent curdling.
Taste and adjust seasoning with the remaining salt and pepper if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately, perhaps over rice or noodles.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Red Curry Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Thai Red Curry Chicken portion rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Succulent, browned chicken chunks are nestled among bright red bell pepper strips, translucent onion wedges, and halved cherry tomatoes. The rich, creamy red-orange curry sauce generously coats all ingredients, pooling slightly at the base. Fresh green Thai basil leaves are scattered over the top, providing a fragrant and colorful garnish. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate is presented on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a small white rice bowl filled with fluffy jasmine rice, a fork, and a spoon, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small dish of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies) on the side for added spice.
Traditionally eaten with a fork and spoon, using the fork to push food onto the spoon.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Add red curry paste. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is browned on all sides and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken broth. Stir well to combine with the paste.
Add palm sugar and fish sauce. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add kaffir lime leaves, red bell pepper strips, and onion wedges. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes and Thai basil leaves. Cook for 1 minute until basil wilts.
Remove kaffir lime leaves before serving. Serve hot with jasmine rice.
notes: Adjust red curry paste quantity to desired spice level.
Palm sugar can be substituted with brown sugar if unavailable.
traditional_techniques: Stir-frying curry paste to release aromatics.
Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors: spicy, sour, sweet, and salty.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Cherry Swirl Cheesecake
recipes.visual_description: A generous slice of Chocolate Cherry Swirl Cheesecake sits on a simple, round ceramic plate, its edges slightly imperfect, resting on a well-worn wooden dining table. The cheesecake presents a thick, dark brown chocolate biscuit crust, providing a sturdy base. Above, the creamy, off-white cheesecake filling is subtly swirled with ribbons of deep ruby red cherry compote, creating an inviting marbled effect. A few whole, glistening dark red cherries are casually placed on top of the slice, adding a fresh fruit accent. The texture is smooth and dense for the filling, contrasting with the crumbly crust. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. The scene is unpretentious, with a casual cloth napkin nearby, emphasizing homemade comfort.

ingredients.name: sour cream or full-fat plain yogurt

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Grease and line a 20 cm springform pan.
Crush biscuits finely. Mix with melted butter, cocoa powder, and 20g sugar. Press firmly into bottom of pan. Bake for 10 minutes. Let cool.
Combine pitted cherries, 50g sugar, and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until cherries soften and sauce thickens. Stir in lemon juice. Let cool.
Beat softened cream cheese and 150g sugar in a large bowl until smooth.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each. Stir in sour cream and vanilla extract. Add a pinch of salt. Do not overmix.
Pour half of the cream cheese mixture over the cooled crust. Spoon half of the cooled cherry compote in dollops over the filling.
Pour remaining cream cheese mixture over. Spoon remaining cherry compote on top. Swirl gently with a knife or skewer.
Place springform pan on a baking sheet. Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until edges are set but center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off oven. Leave cheesecake in oven with door ajar for 1 hour.
Remove from oven. Let cool completely on a wire rack. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rustic braised chicken thighs on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed. The chicken thigh, golden-brown from searing, is nestled amongst vibrant, tender chunks of roasted carrots, celery, and quartered Yukon Gold potatoes. The rich, savory turkey stock-based braising liquid forms a glistening, amber-hued pool around the ingredients, indicating its depth of flavor. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is inviting and hearty, showcasing the succulence of the chicken and the comforting warmth of the braised vegetables. The scene is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate and natural, even lighting from above, evoking a cozy yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the sauce.
A side of simple green salad with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add turkey stock, potatoes, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F).
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove herbs and bay leaf. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Korean Gochujang Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant single portion of Spicy Korean Gochujang Chicken Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Substantial 2.5 cm chicken chunks, seared to a dark golden-brown with visible charred edges, are coated in a glossy, rich reddish-orange gochujang sauce. They are mixed with bright orange julienned carrots and crisp-tender pieces of green and white napa cabbage. Vivid green 5cm spring onion pieces are scattered throughout. The stir-fry is arranged artfully next to a neat mound of fluffy white Basmati rice. A sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds garnishes the dish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table surface, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks resting beside the plate, and a small, simple white rice bowl nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a blurred, unobtrusive restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed short-grain rice (bap).
Traditionally accompanied by various banchan (small side dishes) such as kimchi or pickled radish.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm chunks.
In a large bowl, combine gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, honey, and rice vinegar. Whisk well to create the marinade.
Add chicken chunks to the marinade. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add marinated chicken to the hot wok in a single layer. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary.
Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add julienned carrots and chopped napa cabbage to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add spring onions. Toss everything together for 1 minute to combine and heat through.
Serve immediately with a side of steamed Basmati rice. Garnish generously with toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Roasted Pork Shoulder with Fermented Tomato-Onion Relish
recipes.visual_description: A substantial, golden-brown chunk of slow-roasted pork shoulder anchors the center of a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate. The pork skin is crispy, deeply caramelized. Tender, succulent meat beneath. Arranged around the pork are naturally textured, roasted butternut squash wedges, edges slightly charred, interiors soft. Robust, roasted potato chunks display a rustic, golden-brown crust. Quartered yellow onions and whole roasted garlic cloves are interspersed. A vibrant, jewel-toned mound of lacto-fermented tomato and red onion relish is placed artfully to one side, its bright red and translucent purple hues providing a fresh, zesty counterpoint. Plating is minimalistic, with ample white space, emphasizing pure beauty and natural textures. Setting features a light bamboo table, undyed linen napkin, soft natural lighting. Clean background with natural greenery. A single, refined portion is presented.

ingredients.name: Vegetable Scraps
ingredients.quantity: 100 g (e.g., carrot peels, celery ends, onion skins, for broth)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Relish: Dice tomatoes into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion. Combine tomatoes and red onion in a clean 500 ml jar. Dissolve 5 g non-iodized salt in 250 ml filtered water to make a brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small clean bag filled with brine to keep vegetables below liquid. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Store in refrigerator.
Prepare Pork Shoulder: Pat pork shoulder dry. Score the skin in a crosshatch pattern, being careful not to cut into the meat. Rub generously with sea salt and black pepper.

Roast Pork: Preheat oven to 160°C. Place pork shoulder, skin-side up, in a roasting pan. Add 100 ml water to the bottom of the pan to create steam and prevent drippings from burning. Roast for 2 hours.

Prepare Vegetables for Roasting: While pork roasts, peel and deseed butternut squash. Cut into large 4 cm wedges. Wash potatoes; cut into thick 4 cm chunks. Peel and quarter yellow onion. Peel garlic cloves.

Add Vegetables to Pan: After 2 hours, remove roasting pan from oven. Arrange squash wedges, potato chunks, yellow onion quarters, and garlic cloves around the pork in the pan. Drizzle vegetables with 30 ml olive oil, season with salt, pepper, and fresh rosemary sprigs if using.

Continue Roasting: Return pan to oven. Increase oven temperature to 180°C. Continue roasting for another 1 to 1.5 hours, or until pork is very tender and internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Crisp Skin (Optional): If pork skin is not crispy, increase oven temperature to 220°C for the last 15-20 minutes, watching carefully to prevent burning.
Rest Pork: Remove pork shoulder from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 15 minutes. This allows juices to redistribute.

Make Zero-Waste Broth: While pork rests, skim excess fat from roasting pan. Add 200 ml water, vegetable scraps, and any pork bones/trimmings to the pan. Simmer on stovetop for 15 minutes, scraping up any browned bits. Strain broth and reserve for future use.

Serve: Cut the rested pork shoulder into large, substantial chunks for serving. Arrange a chunk of pork on each plate alongside roasted squash wedges, potato chunks, and yellow onion. Spoon a generous amount of the fermented tomato-onion relish next to the pork. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Baked Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Mediterranean Baked Chicken and Vegetables is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, roasted chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is placed slightly off-center. Around the chicken, generous portions of roasted vegetables are casually arranged, some touching or slightly overlapping. There are thick, rustic wedges of roasted potato with tender interiors and slightly crisped edges. Bright green, tender-crisp broccoli florets are scattered amongst the other vegetables. Earthy, browned mushroom halves and translucent, sweet onion wedges add depth. Burst cherry tomatoes and soft, roasted whole garlic cloves are visible, their natural juices slightly released. The overall color palette is warm and natural, featuring golden browns, deep greens, and reds, with some charring on the edges of the vegetables. The textures are varied, from crispy chicken skin to soft vegetables. The dish is simply garnished with a small sprig of fresh oregano placed beside the chicken. The plate sits on a well-used, rustic wooden dining table. A casually folded, light-colored cloth napkin is placed next to the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, suggesting a cozy family kitchen atmosphere. The scene is unpretentious, highlighting the homely comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up juices.
Offer a simple green salad on the side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, potato wedges, broccoli florets, halved mushrooms, onion wedges, whole garlic cloves, and whole cherry tomatoes.
Drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Spread the mixture in a single layer on a large baking tray. Ensure chicken skin is facing up.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. Chicken should be golden brown and cooked through. Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.
Check chicken internal temperature with a meat thermometer. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust baking time based on chicken size and oven performance.
For crispier potatoes, pre-boil them for 5-7 minutes before roasting.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Lemon-Herb Velouté and Sautéed Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden brown with a slight crust, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. Beside it, a vibrant cluster of bright green broccoli florets, lightly sautéed, provides a contrasting texture and color. A generous pool of creamy, pale yellow lemon-herb velouté sauce artfully surrounds the chicken, its smooth texture evident. Freshly chopped green herbs, likely parsley and chives, are sprinkled over the chicken and sauce for a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard flatware placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its refined yet approachable presentation. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half juiced, half thinly sliced for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Bake chicken for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
While chicken bakes, blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender. Drain immediately and transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

In a separate pan, heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter over medium heat. Add blanched broccoli florets and minced garlic. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender and fragrant. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For the velouté, return the skillet used for chicken to medium heat (if not oven-safe, use a clean saucepan). Add remaining 30g butter. Once melted, whisk in 30g flour to create a roux. Cook roux for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in chicken stock until smooth. If using, deglaze with white wine first, then add stock. Bring to a simmer, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens to a coating consistency.
Remove velouté from heat. Stir in lemon juice, chopped parsley, and chives. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
To serve, place one chicken breast on each plate. Arrange sautéed broccoli florets beside the chicken. Spoon velouté generously over and around the chicken. Garnish with a thin lemon slice.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Blanching broccoli before sautéing helps maintain its vibrant color and tender-crisp texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Medley
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its skin is crisp and slightly blistered. Beside the chicken, vibrant green broccoli florets and tender-crisp green beans are artfully arranged, some exhibiting delicate charring from roasting. Scattered among the vegetables are plump, ruby-red cherry tomatoes, some slightly burst and caramelized. A light drizzle of pan juices glazes the ingredients, adding a subtle sheen. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. A fresh sprig of oregano and a bright yellow lemon wedge garnish the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's colors and textures. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful pan juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and dried oregano.
Trim green beans. Cut broccoli into florets. Halve cherry tomatoes if desired, or leave whole.
In a large bowl, toss broccoli florets, green beans, and cherry tomatoes with olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Arrange seasoned chicken thighs on a large baking sheet. Distribute the seasoned vegetables around the chicken.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip chicken thighs once.
Continue roasting for 10-15 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Vegetables should be tender-crisp with some charred edges.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the entire dish.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust roasting time based on chicken thigh size and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken with Roasted Vegetables and White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, sliced into thick, substantial medallions, takes center stage on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken boasts a golden-brown, crispy exterior and moist, white interior. Around the chicken, arrange a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables: bright red and yellow bell pepper chunks, softened red onion wedges with caramelized edges, tender-crisp green broccoli florets, and burst cherry tomatoes, creating a natural, organic composition. A rich, light brown pan sauce, glistening with olive oil and infused with garlic and herbs, is spooned generously over the chicken and vegetables. Scattered within the sauce are creamy white cannellini beans and dark, glossy Kalamata olives, adding textural contrast and depth. A sprig of fresh green parsley or basil leaves is placed artfully on top of the chicken or beside it. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits on the plate. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The setting includes standard silver flatware (fork and knife). Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background suggests a modern bistro with subtle, out-of-focus elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the flavorful sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut bell peppers into 2.5 cm chunks. Cut red onion into 2 cm wedges. Cut broccoli into small florets. Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice 3 garlic cloves. Mince 2 garlic cloves.

On a large baking tray, toss bell pepper chunks, red onion wedges, broccoli florets, and whole cherry tomatoes with 30ml olive oil, sliced garlic, rosemary sprigs, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crusty.
Remove chicken from skillet. Add minced garlic to the skillet, cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Deglaze with white wine (if using), scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Add chicken broth, bring to a simmer. Return chicken to skillet. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in drained cannellini beans and pitted olives into the skillet with the chicken. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Squeeze juice from half a lemon into the sauce. Stir in chopped fresh oregano or thyme.

Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions. Arrange roasted vegetables on plates. Place chicken alongside vegetables. Spoon sauce, beans, and olives over chicken and vegetables. Garnish with fresh parsley or basil and a lemon wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust roasting time for vegetables based on desired tenderness.
traditional_techniques: Pan-searing for browning and flavor development
Roasting vegetables to enhance sweetness and texture

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Rice Pudding with Roasted Sweet Potato Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Rice Pudding is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl on a light, reclaimed wood surface. The off-white, creamy pudding is gently mounded, highlighting its soft texture. A vibrant orange-gold roasted sweet potato puree, made from roasted and pureed 2cm sweet potato cubes, is artfully dolloped alongside or swirled in, offering color and smooth contrast. The dish is garnished with toasted rice grains for crunch and delicate, thin, crispy sweet potato skin ribbons, emphasizing zero-waste. The minimalistic plating focuses on natural beauty and contrasting textures. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is nearby. The clean, unobtrusive background includes subtle green foliage, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine rice and 500ml water in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat. Simmer until water is absorbed, about 10 minutes.
Transfer cooked rice to a clean, non-reactive container. Cover loosely. Let stand at room temperature for 24 hours for light fermentation and subtle tang.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash sweet potato. Do not peel.
Cut sweet potato into 2cm cubes. Save the skin trimmings for crisps.
Toss sweet potato cubes with olive oil and 15ml maple syrup. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 20-25 minutes until tender.
Blend roasted sweet potato into a smooth puree. Add a splash of plant milk if needed for consistency.
Wash sweet potato skin trimmings well. Pat dry. Toss with a tiny bit of olive oil and salt.
Bake skin trimmings on a separate tray at 180°C for 10-15 minutes until crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Add fermented rice, plant-based milk, 80ml maple syrup, vanilla, and salt to a pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Cook, stirring frequently, for 25-35 minutes until thickened and creamy.
Remove from heat. Let cool slightly. It will thicken further.
Spoon warm or chilled rice pudding into serving bowls. Dollop roasted sweet potato puree on top or swirl it in.
Garnish with sweet potato skin crisps. Optionally, sprinkle with toasted rice grains for extra crunch.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Chili with Rice and Beans
recipes.visual_description: A hearty bowl of classic beef chili, rich and deeply colored, is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chili, a thick, rustic stew, showcases tender chunks of seared beef, vibrant diced red and green bell peppers, dark sliced cremini mushrooms, and plump kidney beans, all suspended in a savory, tomato-based sauce. A hint of steam rises from the warm dish. The chili is generously spooned over a bed of fluffy white long-grain rice, which is neatly mounded on one side of the plate, allowing the chili to cascade slightly. A sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro adds a bright green contrast on top of the chili. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Beside the plate, a cotton napkin is neatly folded. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and warm tones of the food. A casual restaurant background with soft focus completes the scene, emphasizing the inviting and comforting nature of the meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas or tortilla chips on the side.
Offer shredded cheddar cheese, sour cream, or sliced jalapeños as optional toppings.

ingredients.name: Canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Season beef cubes (2.5 cm chunks) with salt and pepper. Brown beef in batches until seared on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion and diced bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is tender. Stir occasionally.
Add sliced mushrooms and drained kidney beans to the chili. Simmer for another 20 minutes, uncovered, allowing the chili to thicken slightly.

While chili simmers, prepare rice. Rinse rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 400ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Season chili with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot chili over a bed of cooked rice.
notes: For best flavor, prepare chili a day in advance and reheat. Flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust chili powder for desired spice level.
traditional_techniques: Slow simmering to tenderize tough cuts of beef

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Crispy Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a single portion of pan-seared chicken and crispy smashed potatoes on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cut into thick, irregular pieces, exhibits a deep golden-brown crust from searing, revealing tender white meat within. It is arranged naturally on one side of the plate. Beside it, the smashed potatoes are golden-brown and irregularly shaped, showcasing their crisp, craggy exteriors. A vibrant, glistening herb butter sauce, infused with finely minced garlic, rosemary, and thyme, is generously spooned over both the chicken and potatoes, adding a rich golden hue. Fresh green parsley sprigs are scattered for garnish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside it, under soft, natural lighting, creating a refined bistro ambiance.
instructions: Wash potatoes. Place in large pot. Cover with cold water. Add pinch of salt. Bring to boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to 75°C internal temperature. Transfer chicken to plate. Tent with foil. Rest 10 minutes.
While chicken rests, place drained potatoes on a clean surface. Gently smash each potato with a fork or potato masher to flatten, keeping it mostly intact.

Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter to the same skillet. Increase heat to medium-high. Add smashed potatoes in single layer. Cook 5-7 minutes per side until deeply golden and crispy. Remove potatoes. Keep warm.

Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 30g butter to skillet. Add minced garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to simmer. Cook 3-4 minutes, scraping up browned bits, until slightly reduced. Squeeze in lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Slice chicken breasts into two or three thick pieces across the grain (not fanned). Plate chicken alongside crispy smashed potatoes. Spoon herb butter sauce over chicken and potatoes. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken with Roasted Vegetables and White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Chicken with Roasted Vegetables and White Beans is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. The pan-seared chicken thigh, golden brown with visible herb specks, is positioned as the centerpiece, left as a whole piece. Around and partially underneath the chicken are vibrant, thick strips of roasted red and yellow bell peppers, creamy white cannellini beans, and rich diced tomatoes, all glistening with a savory sauce. Alongside, a generous serving of bright green, tender-crisp broccoli florets is arranged neatly. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and rich colors, reflecting a professional yet approachable modern bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread to sop up the flavorful sauce.
A simple green salad with a lemon-oregano vinaigrette makes a refreshing accompaniment.
Pair with a dry white wine such as a Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, black pepper, oregano, and smoked paprika.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add bell pepper strips. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, cannellini beans, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet. Ensure they are partially submerged in the sauce.
Cover skillet and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, toss broccoli florets with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C (392°F) for 10-15 minutes until tender-crisp.
Taste and adjust seasoning of the skillet sauce if needed.
Serve chicken and vegetable mixture directly from the skillet or portion onto plates. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve alongside roasted broccoli.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust spice levels of smoked paprika to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken Mole
recipes.visual_description: A single, bone-in chicken thigh is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is generously draped with a rich, dark reddish-brown mole sauce, showcasing its smooth, velvety texture. The sauce pools slightly around the chicken, revealing its depth and sheen. A light scattering of golden, toasted Panko breadcrumbs provides a textural contrast and visual crunch on top of the chicken and sauce. Fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves are artfully sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. The plate has appropriate negative space, allowing the dish to be the focal point. Beside the plate, a stack of warm, soft corn tortillas and a small bowl of fluffy white rice are placed, inviting a traditional Mexican dining experience. A simple wooden table surface and a casually placed cotton napkin complete the modern bistro setting, with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the mole.
Accompany with a side of white rice to soak up the sauce.
Offer pickled red onions or a simple fresh salsa on the side.
instructions: Toast dried Ancho and Guajillo chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Do not burn. Rehydrate chilies in hot water for 20 minutes. Remove stems and seeds.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Brown chicken thighs until golden on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add diced Roma tomatoes. Cook until tomatoes break down, about 8-10 minutes.
Add rehydrated chilies, toasted sesame seeds, toasted almonds, ground cumin, ground coriander, cinnamon stick, and whole cloves to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender. Add chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. Strain the mole sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot for a velvety texture. Discard solids.
Return browned chicken thighs to the pot with the strained mole sauce. Add unsweetened chocolate, salt, and sugar.
Simmer mole sauce with chicken over low heat for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and the sauce has thickened. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
While mole simmers, toast Panko breadcrumbs in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Taste and adjust seasoning of the mole. Remove cinnamon stick and whole cloves before serving.
Serve chicken hot, generously coated in mole sauce. Garnish with toasted Panko breadcrumbs and chopped fresh cilantro.
notes: For a deeper flavor, use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs.
Adjust chili quantity for desired spice level.
Straining the mole sauce through a sieve is crucial for an authentic, smooth texture.
traditional_techniques: Blending and straining ingredients for a smooth mole sauce

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef & Bean Skillet with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Beef & Bean Skillet with Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, savory beef and bean mixture forms the main element, featuring tender 3cm beef cubes alongside diced red and green bell peppers and quartered cremini mushrooms. The sauce is a deep, glossy reddish-brown from tomatoes and chili spices. Beside it, a neat mound of fluffy white long-grain rice. Fresh, vibrant green chopped coriander is sprinkled over the skillet. A bright yellow lime wedge rests on the plate's edge, ready to be squeezed. The setting includes a simple wooden table, with a stack of warm corn tortillas and a small bowl of salsa roja placed alongside the dish, enhancing the Tex-Mex feel. Natural, even lighting highlights the food's inviting colors and textures in a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping
Offer salsa roja or pico de gallo on the side
Accompany with a dollop of sour cream or guacamole
instructions: Rinse long-grain rice. Combine rice, chicken broth, and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef cubes in batches until seared on all sides. Remove beef from skillet and set aside.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the same skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook for 3-5 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Stir in chili powder, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Return browned beef to the skillet. Stir in diced tomatoes with their juice. Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 45-60 minutes, or until beef is very tender.
Stir in drained and rinsed kidney beans. Cook for an additional 5 minutes to heat through. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve the spicy beef and bean skillet mixture alongside the fluffy rice. Garnish each serving with fresh chopped coriander and a lime wedge.
notes: Adjust the amount of chili powder to suit your preferred spice level.
This dish can be prepared ahead of time; flavors deepen overnight.
traditional_techniques: Browning meat for depth of flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Aloo Matar Pulao
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Aloo Matar Pulao is mounded centrally on a round, clean white porcelain plate. The Basmati rice grains are distinct and fluffy, infused with a golden hue from turmeric and spices. Scattered throughout are vibrant green peas and tender, small-cubed potatoes (1.5 cm dice), lightly browned from cooking. Visible whole spices like a bay leaf and a small cinnamon stick are nestled within the rice. The dish is generously garnished with freshly chopped bright green cilantro leaves. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a small katori (metal bowl) holds a dollop of creamy raita, and a small metal spoon rests beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and warm colors of the dish. The background is softly blurred, maintaining a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt or cooling cucumber raita.
Offer Indian pickle (achar) and crisp papadum as accompaniments.
Traditionally served as part of a thali, a platter of various dishes.
instructions: Rinse Basmati rice thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. Soak rice in fresh water for 30 minutes. Drain well.
Peel potatoes and dice into 1.5 cm cubes. Slice onion thinly. Slit green chilies lengthwise.
Heat ghee or oil in a large pot or heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced onion. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Cook for 1 minute until raw smell disappears.
Add diced potatoes and green peas. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and garam masala. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the drained Basmati rice to the pot. Gently stir for 2 minutes to coat rice with spices.
Pour in 800 ml water and add salt to taste. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly with a lid. Cook for 15-18 minutes without opening the lid.
Turn off heat. Let the pulao rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Gently fluff the rice with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.
Serve hot with a lemon wedge.
notes: Adjust green chilies and red chili powder to your preferred spice level.
For best results, use aged Basmati rice.
The resting period allows the rice to fully absorb moisture and become fluffy.
traditional_techniques: Tadka (Tempering whole spices in hot oil/ghee)
Dum cooking (cooking rice on low heat in a sealed pot)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast Stuffed with Mushroom and Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-seared chicken breast, sliced diagonally in half, is centrally placed on a round, clean white porcelain plate. The chicken exterior is a rich golden-brown, showcasing a crispy texture. The revealed interior displays a generous, savory filling of finely diced earthy brown mushrooms, minced garlic, and green flecks of fresh herbs, bound with golden panko breadcrumbs. A small, glossy pool of light brown pan sauce is artfully spooned beneath one half of the chicken. A vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme rests gently on top of the chicken. The overall composition is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space around the dish. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. Standard silver fork and knife are neatly placed beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a softly blurred background hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Prepare filling: Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced mushrooms. Cook until softened and moisture evaporates, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat.
Combine filling: In a bowl, combine cooked mushrooms and garlic with panko breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, chopped parsley, and chopped thyme. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare chicken: Using a sharp paring knife, carefully cut a deep pocket into the thickest side of each chicken breast. Do not cut all the way through.
Stuff chicken: Divide mushroom-breadcrumb mixture evenly among the four chicken pockets. Use kitchen twine to tie the chicken breasts, or use toothpicks to secure the filling.

Sear chicken: Season outside of stuffed chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add stuffed chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown.

Finish in oven: Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Make pan sauce: While chicken rests, place skillet back on medium heat. Add white wine (if using) and deglaze, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes until slightly reduced. Stir in remaining 15g butter until melted and glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Serve: Slice each chicken breast diagonally in half to reveal the filling, or serve whole. Plate the chicken with a spoonful of the pan sauce. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig or a sprinkle of chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili-Crusted Chicken with Roasted Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-crusted, whole chicken breast is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Beneath and around it, a vibrant, rustic roasted tomato sauce, with visible softened tomato halves and slivers of garlic, pools naturally. The chicken, pounded to an even thickness before cooking, boasts a crisp, textured chili-breadcrumb crust. A few fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the sauce and chicken, adding color and freshness. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits alongside the chicken, ready to be squeezed. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting, a folded white cotton napkin, and modern silver flatware, embodying a refined yet approachable bistro style.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Place on the baking tray with smashed garlic cloves. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until softened and slightly caramelized.
While tomatoes roast, prepare chicken. Place each chicken breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound evenly to a thickness of about 1.5 cm.
Set up dredging stations: one shallow dish with flour seasoned with salt and pepper, one with whisked egg, and one with panko breadcrumbs mixed with minced red chilies.
Dredge each chicken breast first in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, allowing excess to drip off. Finally, coat thoroughly in the chili breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear breaded chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove roasted tomatoes and garlic from oven. Transfer to a small saucepan or a deep bowl. Gently mash with a fork or potato masher to create a rustic sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
Plate immediately. Spoon a generous amount of roasted tomato sauce onto each plate. Place a chili-crusted chicken breast on top of the sauce. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Gnocchi with Crispy Bacon and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, generous individual portion. Tender, pillowy potato gnocchi, lightly coated in a shimmering, savory sauce, form the base. Interspersed throughout are vibrant green, roasted broccoli florets, slightly charred at the edges for texture and depth of color. Crispy, golden-brown pieces of rendered bacon are scattered generously over the top, adding contrasting texture and rich aroma. A dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese provides a pale counterpoint, melting slightly into the warm gnocchi. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green, chopped fresh parsley. The arrangement is natural and inviting, not overly structured, with elements visually balanced. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra grated Parmesan cheese on the side.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast broccoli for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add diced bacon to the skillet. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered.
Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain. Keep rendered bacon fat in the skillet.
Add butter and remaining 15 ml olive oil to the skillet with bacon fat. Heat over medium heat.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cook gnocchi according to package directions in a separate pot of salted boiling water. Gnocchi floats when cooked.
Drain gnocchi. Add directly to the skillet with the broth mixture.
Add roasted broccoli and crispy bacon to the skillet.
Toss gently to combine.
Stir in half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately with fresh chopped parsley and remaining Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Pepper-Onion Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, subtly highlighting the natural textures of the ingredients. A single, golden-skinned pan-seared chicken thigh, perfectly cooked to a crisp, deep brown, sits slightly off-center. The chicken is a whole piece, showcasing its natural form and rich color. Adjacent to the chicken, a generous spoonful of vibrant Fermented Pepper-Onion Relish forms an organic mound. The relish features diced red bell peppers and red onions, their colors deepened and mellowed by fermentation, exhibiting a slight sheen from reduction. Beside these, a small, artfully arranged pile of vibrant green, lightly wilted seasonal greens provides a fresh contrast. The composition respects negative space, creating a clean, minimalist aesthetic. The table surface is light, natural wood with a subtle grain. An undyed linen napkin in a soft beige tone is casually placed. Lighting is soft, natural, and diffused, emphasizing the inherent beauty and texture of each ingredient. No ornate garnishes or excess elements are present; the focus remains purely on the food's natural appeal and sustainable preparation.

ingredients.name: Seasonal greens (e.g., spinach, Swiss chard, kale)

instructions: Ferment Bell Pepper & Onion:
Dice red bell peppers and red onions into 1.5 cm pieces.
In a clean jar, combine diced bell peppers and onions.
Dissolve 20g sea salt in 1 liter non-chlorinated water to make a 2% brine.
Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small clean bag filled with water to keep vegetables submerged.
Cover jar loosely with a lid or airlock.
Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily if using a tight lid.
Once fermented, store in refrigerator.
Prepare Relish:
Drain fermented bell peppers and onions, reserving a small amount of liquid.
Mince garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add drained fermented vegetables and minced garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in apple cider vinegar and honey (if using). Cook for another 2-3 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust tanginess with reserved fermentation liquid if needed. Set aside.
Cook Chicken:
Pat chicken thighs dry thoroughly with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with sea salt and black pepper on both sides.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden brown and crispy.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F).
Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Prepare Greens:
Wash seasonal greens.
In a separate pan, lightly sauté greens with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Plate Dish:
Place a portion of sautéed greens on each plate.
Arrange one pan-seared chicken thigh next to the greens.
Spoon a generous amount of fermented pepper-onion relish over or alongside the chicken.
notes: The fermentation process adds a complex tangy flavor and aids in food preservation.
Use any remaining fermented brine as a flavorful vinegar substitute in dressings or marinades.
Chicken bones and vegetable scraps from preparation can be used to make a flavorful stock, promoting zero-waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Potato and Mushroom Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of hearty potato and mushroom stew is presented in a simple, everyday ceramic bowl. The stew fills the bowl generously, with components touching and overlapping naturally. Visible elements include softened 2-3 cm potato cubes, browned quartered mushrooms, and vibrant green wilted chopped swiss chard leaves. A rich, reddish-brown broth coats the ingredients. The dish is garnished with a light sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, reflecting a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere with minimal clutter.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm cubes. Quarter mushrooms. Dice onion. Mince garlic. Remove Swiss chard stems. Chop chard leaves.
Heat oil in large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 5-7 minutes until soft.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in quartered mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and softened.
Add potato cubes, tomato paste, dried thyme, and smoked paprika. Stir to coat.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 15-20 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in chopped swiss chard leaves. Cook 3-5 minutes until chard wilts.
Season with salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef Goulash
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a dark oak table. The focus is a hearty portion of Hungarian beef stew. The beef is cut into 3cm chunks, appearing dark red and tender. Vibrant orange carrots are cut into 2cm rounds. Potatoes are 2cm cubes, absorbing the deep red sauce. The sauce is thick and glossy, colored intensely by sweet paprika. Red bell peppers are cut into 2cm squares. A single dollop of white sour cream is placed on the side. A sprig of fresh parsley is the garnish. A side of crusty rye bread rests on a small ceramic plate next to the bowl. Natural light creates soft shadows and highlights the rich textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Galuska or Nokedli dumplings
Accompany with pickled cucumbers or fermented cabbage
Provide thick slices of fresh rye bread for dipping
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Finely dice onions and mince garlic.
Cut carrots into 2cm rounds and potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Dice tomatoes and cut bell pepper into 2cm squares.
Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté onions until translucent and golden.
Remove pot from heat and stir in paprika and caraway seeds.
Add beef chunks and return to heat.
Sear meat for 5 minutes until browned.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and bell pepper.
Pour in beef stock and add bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots.
Simmer for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not boil the paprika over high heat to avoid bitterness.
The stew is even better when reheated the next day.
Ensure the beef is chuck or a similar braising cut for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of wide, golden pappardelle ribbons nested in a shallow white porcelain bowl. Large, 3cm tender chunks of braised beef are distributed naturally throughout the pasta, coated in a thick, mahogany-colored tomato sauce. The sauce has a glossy sheen and visible small bits of diced carrots and onions. The dish is topped with a light, airy snowfall of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. A small pinch of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the center. The bowl sits on a rustic light-wood bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural daylight illuminates the textures of the shredded beef fibers and the silkiness of the pasta ribbons.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of full-bodied red wine like Chianti
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread for 'fare la scarpetta'
Present in wide-rimmed pasta bowls
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the same pot. Sauté 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to release browned bits.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and herb sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Remove herb sprigs. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Boil salted water in a large pot. Cook pappardelle until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 60ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta with the ragu and reserved water over low heat for 1 minute.
Serve immediately with grated cheese.
notes: Ensure the beef is seared deeply for maximum flavor development.
If the sauce is too thick, add more pasta water during the finishing stage.
Chuck roast or shin are the best cuts for this long-braising method.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Caramelized Peaches and Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken with caramelized peaches and onions is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown roasted chicken thighs, moist and tender, are placed slightly overlapping. Alongside are vibrant, tender peach wedges, their edges subtly caramelized, and soft, deep purple-red caramelized red onion slices. Fresh green thyme sprigs are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The rich pan juices, a blend of savory chicken drippings, sweet peach nectar, and tangy balsamic, pool invitingly at the base of the chicken and vegetables. The plate maintains moderate negative space, showcasing the rustic appeal of the ingredients. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting textures and warm colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut peaches into 8 wedges each. Cut red onion into thick slices.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down (if applicable), for 4-5 minutes until golden brown. Flip and sear other side for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to skillet. Add red onion slices. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add peach wedges and fresh thyme sprigs to the skillet with onions. Cook for 3 minutes.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them among the peaches and onions.
Pour balsamic vinegar and chicken broth into the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken roasts, slice crusty bread. Toast lightly if desired.
Remove skillet from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken with roasted peaches and onions, drizzled with pan juices. Serve with crusty bread on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Beef Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Thai Basil Beef Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally piled with moderate negative space. Seared beef irregular chunks, rich brown and glistening with sauce, are nestled among bright green tender-crisp broccoli florets and thin orange carrot rounds. Translucent sautéed red onion slices and vibrant green Thai basil leaves are scattered throughout, adding color and texture. The glossy, savory sauce coats all ingredients, with visible flecks of minced garlic and chili. A small, separate white bowl of fluffy jasmine rice sits beside the main plate. Chopsticks rest beside the plate on a simple cotton napkin. The setting features a natural wooden table surface, illuminated by even, natural light from above, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer chili fish sauce (Prik Nam Pla) on the side for extra spice.
A fried egg, sunny-side up, is a traditional accompaniment.
instructions: Slice beef into 2 cm irregular chunks. Set aside.
Mince garlic and chilies together until a coarse paste forms. Set aside.
Cut carrot into thin rounds or julienne strips. Cut red onion into thick slices. Separate broccoli into small florets.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, and sugar. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add beef chunks to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add garlic and chili paste to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add onion slices and carrot rounds to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add broccoli florets to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return beef to the wok. Pour the prepared sauce over the beef and vegetables. Toss to coat evenly.
Add Thai basil leaves. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until basil wilts. Do not overcook.
Remove from heat immediately. Serve hot with jasmine rice.
notes: Use fresh Thai basil for authentic flavor; regular basil is not a substitute.
Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Beef Stock Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant portion presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, free-flowing mound of creamy, al dente beef stock risotto forms the base, its natural off-white hue subtly enriched by the stock. Resting prominently atop the risotto is a single, whole pan-seared chicken breast, its breadcrumb crust a vibrant, even golden-brown with visible crisp texture. Scattered artfully over the chicken and spilling onto the risotto are strands of deep amber, glistening caramelized onions, adding rich color and texture contrast. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded cotton napkin and polished standard flatware (fork and knife) are placed neatly beside the plate, completing a refined yet approachable modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth.
instructions: Halve the onion. Dice half for the risotto. Thinly slice the other half for caramelizing.
Heat 10 ml olive oil and 10 g butter in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onion. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes until deep golden brown and soft. Stir occasionally. Set aside.
In a separate large saucepan, heat 10 ml olive oil and 20 g butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the saucepan. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until edges become translucent.
Pour in white wine (if using). Stir until completely absorbed.

Add one ladle of hot beef stock to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 20-25 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and let rest for 2 minutes.
While risotto cooks, pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Place breadcrumbs on a shallow plate. Press each chicken breast firmly into the breadcrumbs to coat evenly on all sides.

Heat remaining 10 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add breaded chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Spoon creamy risotto onto the center of each plate. Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast partially on top of the risotto. Garnish with caramelized onions and chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Osso Buco
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Beef Osso Buco is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A large, rich brown beef shank, braised to a tender, falling-off-the-bone consistency, rests centrally. Its marrow bone is visible, indicating the authentic cut. A glossy, deep reddish-brown braising sauce, studded with finely diced carrots, celery, and onion, pools around the base of the shank. The beef exhibits a slight shimmer from its cooking juices, and the vegetables are soft but retain their form. A vibrant green gremolata, a finely minced mix of fresh parsley, lemon zest, and garlic, is generously sprinkled over the top of the beef, providing a fresh, bright contrast. Beside the Osso Buco, a generous, free-flowing mound of creamy, golden-yellow Saffron Risotto is artfully placed, its texture appearing rich and fluid. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple, light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard European flatware (fork, knife, spoon) are placed beside the dish. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the rich colors and textures of the food. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual, inviting restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served with Risotto alla Milanese (saffron risotto) or polenta.
Gremolata is an essential fresh garnish for authentic flavor.
Best enjoyed with a full-bodied red wine, such as a Barolo or Chianti.
instructions: Pat beef shanks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge shanks in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear shanks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove shanks from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared beef shanks to the pot. Ensure shanks are mostly submerged in liquid. If not, add a little more broth.
Cover pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender and falling off the bone. Turn shanks halfway through cooking.
While beef cooks, prepare the gremolata: finely chop parsley, mince remaining garlic, and finely grate lemon zest. Combine in a small bowl.
Once beef is tender, remove shanks from pot. Discard bay leaf and thyme sprigs. Skim any excess fat from the sauce.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning as needed. Simmer sauce briefly to reduce if desired, until slightly thickened.
Serve each beef shank on a plate with a generous spoonful of sauce. Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh gremolata. Serve immediately, traditionally with Saffron Risotto or polenta.
notes: For best results, prepare Osso Buco a day in advance. Flavors deepen overnight.
Ensure beef shanks are tied with kitchen twine if not already, to help them hold their shape during braising.

recipes.recipe_name: Brasato di Manzo con Verdure e Basilico
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Italian Brasato di Manzo is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Tender, dark brown 5-6 cm beef chunks are nestled amidst glossy, soft 2-3 cm carrot chunks and translucent, roughly chopped onions. The rich, deep red-brown braising liquid pools elegantly at the base of the dish. A generous scattering of vibrant, whole fresh basil leaves rests on top, providing a bright green contrast. A delicate sheen of extra virgin olive oil glistens on the surface. The overall presentation is rustic yet refined, showcasing the comforting, slow-cooked textures and warm colors of the dish. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface. Beside it, a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are neatly placed. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred background hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with creamy polenta or rustic crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.
Pair with a simple side salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 3 medium (approx. 200g), peeled and cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge beef in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add chopped onions and carrots to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce wine by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Add bay leaf and rosemary sprig.
Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid. Bring mixture to a gentle simmer.
Cover pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf and rosemary sprig from the pot. Discard.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Stir in chopped fresh basil just before serving. Garnish with whole basil leaves.
