ingredients.name: Seasonal Root Vegetables (e.g., carrots, parsnips), cut into chunks

instructions: Prepare Kohlrabi Kraut: Wash and thinly slice kohlrabi. Discard tough outer layers. In a large bowl, massage kohlrabi with 10g sea salt until water releases. Pack tightly into a clean jar. Press down to submerge kohlrabi in its own liquid. Seal loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.
Prepare Chicken Brine: In a large pot, combine 1 litre water, 60g sea salt, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Bring to a simmer until salt dissolves. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Brine Chicken: Submerge chicken thighs in cooled brine. Ensure chicken is fully covered. Refrigerate for 2-4 hours. Remove chicken from brine. Pat very dry with paper towels. Discard brine.

Prepare Preserved Lemon Crumble: Preheat oven to 180°C. Tear stale bread into small pieces. In a bowl, combine bread pieces, diced preserved lemon, chopped parsley, thyme leaves, minced garlic, and 15ml olive oil. Toss to combine. Spread on a baking tray. Bake for 10-15 minutes, until golden and crispy. Set aside.

Sear Chicken: Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear for 2 minutes on the flesh side.

Roast Vegetables: Add seasonal root vegetable chunks to the skillet around the chicken. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender-crisp. Remove chicken and vegetables from skillet. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

Make Pan Sauce: Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken stock to deglaze, scraping up any browned bits. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half. Whisk in butter until melted and sauce slightly thickens. Season to taste.

Plate Dish: Place one brined chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange roasted vegetables alongside. Add a generous spoonful of kohlrabi kraut next to the chicken. Sprinkle preserved lemon crumble over the chicken and vegetables. Spoon pan sauce over the chicken and vegetables. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Banana Gnocchi with Cocoa Mozzarella Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Banana Gnocchi with Cocoa Mozzarella Sauce is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown, pan-fried banana gnocchi, irregularly shaped, are artfully mounded on one side of the plate. Beside them, a nest of light yellow, buttered tagliatelle pasta is neatly arranged. A rich, creamy cocoa mozzarella sauce, with a light tan hue, is generously spooned over the gnocchi, partially coating the pasta and pooling gently around the base. The sauce exhibits a smooth, glossy texture. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green chives provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness over the gnocchi and sauce. The dish sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Peel bananas. Cut into thick chunks. Boil or steam banana chunks until very soft, about 10-15 minutes.
Drain bananas. Mash thoroughly with a fork or potato masher until smooth. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine mashed banana, plain flour, and the whole egg. Add a pinch of salt. Mix until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
Lightly flour a clean surface. Divide dough into 4 portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, about 2 cm thick.
Cut each rope into 2 cm pieces to form gnocchi. Gently press each piece with a fork tines for ridges, if desired.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Carefully drop gnocchi into boiling water in batches. Cook until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon.

In a separate large frying pan, melt 20g of butter over medium heat. Lightly whisk the egg white. Dip each cooked gnocchi lightly in egg white, then place in the hot butter. Pan-fry gnocchi until golden brown and slightly crispy on all sides. Set aside.
For the sauce: In a saucepan, melt remaining 30g butter over medium heat. Whisk in 20g of the flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth and thickened. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Reduce heat to low. Stir in shredded mozzarella until melted and smooth. Add hot chocolate powder, a pinch of salt, and black pepper. Stir well to combine. The sauce should be creamy with a subtle cocoa hue.
Cook tagliatelle according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Toss lightly with a small knob of butter.

To serve: Place a portion of buttered tagliatelle on a white porcelain plate. Arrange a generous serving of golden banana gnocchi beside the pasta. Spoon the warm cocoa mozzarella sauce generously over the gnocchi, allowing some to pool on the plate. Garnish with fresh chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic Mushroom Orzo Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A generous, mounded portion of Spicy Garlic Mushroom Orzo Pilaf is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The pilaf has an inviting golden-brown hue with visible tender, sautéed mushroom slices, distinct grains of al dente orzo, and fluffy rice. Flecks of vibrant red from thinly sliced chili are interspersed throughout, contrasting with the earthy tones. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, roughly chopped fresh coriander leaves scattered over the top. Two bright yellow-green lime wedges are placed artfully beside the pilaf, ready to be squeezed. The overall presentation is natural and abundant, not overly sculpted. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a set of dark, polished chopsticks laid parallel to the plate and a folded light grey cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background, ensuring the focus remains entirely on the food.
instructions: Rinse basmati rice thoroughly under cold water. Drain well.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic. Thinly slice red chilies.
Heat neutral cooking oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Add diced shallots to the same pot. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add orzo pasta and rinsed rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to lightly toast the grains.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice and orzo are tender. Do not stir excessively during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff the pilaf with a fork. Stir in cooked mushrooms, soy sauce, and sesame oil. Squeeze juice from one lime into the pilaf. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Roughly chop fresh coriander. Cut the remaining lime into wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Tuna and Mango Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Mexican Tuna and Mango Rice Bowl is presented in a deep, rustic, hand-painted ceramic bowl with earthy tones. The base of the bowl holds a generous bed of fluffy, white cilantro-lime rice, its individual grains distinct and lightly glistening. On one side of the rice, thick, seared yellowfin tuna chunks are nestled, showing a lightly browned, seasoned crust and a tender, opaque interior. Adjacent to the tuna, a vibrant, colorful salsa composed of diced bright yellow mango, crisp red and yellow bell peppers, and finely minced red onion is piled casually. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered over the salsa and rice, adding a pop of freshness. The components touch and slightly overlap, creating a natural, inviting arrangement. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table, revealing natural grain and minor imperfections. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed next to the bowl. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a comfortable, lived-in family dining atmosphere. A whole lime cut into wedges and a small, traditional Mexican-style spoon rest nearby, suggesting a complete, authentic meal experience.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Combine rice with 600 ml water or broth in a saucepan. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed. Remove from heat, let stand covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
While rice cooks, prepare the salsa. Dice mangoes into 1 cm cubes. Dice bell peppers into 1 cm cubes. Mince red onion finely. Roughly chop half the cilantro.
In a medium bowl, combine diced mango, bell peppers, red onion, and chopped cilantro. Squeeze juice from one lime over the mixture. Season with salt and pepper. Stir gently to combine. Set aside.
Prepare the tuna. Pat tuna steaks dry. Mince garlic. In a small bowl, combine cumin, chili powder, salt, pepper, and minced garlic. Rub this spice mixture evenly over both sides of the tuna steaks.

Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add tuna steaks. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for well-done, or less for medium-rare, until cooked to your preference and opaque throughout. Do not overcook. Remove from pan and let rest for a few minutes. Slice tuna into thick chunks.
Finely chop the remaining cilantro. Squeeze juice from the second lime into the cooked rice. Add chopped cilantro. Fluff the rice with a fork, ensuring lime and cilantro are evenly distributed.

To assemble bowls, divide the cilantro-lime rice among four serving bowls. Top each portion of rice with the seared tuna chunks. Spoon a generous amount of mango-bell pepper salsa next to the tuna. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Seared Tuna with White Beans and Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Skillet Seared Tuna with White Beans and Greens is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. Two thick chunks of pan-seared yellowfin tuna display a light golden-brown crust and slightly pink interior. They are nestled among creamy white cannellini beans and vibrant green, wilted spinach. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes are scattered throughout, some slightly burst, adding juicy pops of color. Diced red onion and minced garlic are visible within the mixture. Fresh, chopped green parsley garnishes the dish. The components are casually arranged, naturally touching, creating an inviting, unpretentious appearance. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light, with a plain cloth napkin and simple fork and knife, reflecting a homely kitchen.
instructions: Pat tuna fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear tuna fillets 2-3 minutes per side, until light golden-brown and cooked to desired doneness. Remove tuna from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced red onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes, drained cannellini beans, dried oregano, and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add fresh spinach to the skillet. Cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Return seared tuna fillets to the skillet, nesting them into the bean and spinach mixture. Cook 2 minutes to heat through.
Season the dish with additional salt and pepper to taste. Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra flavor, add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the garlic.
Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Shrimp Pasta with Sun-dried Tomato and White Wine
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous portion of golden-hued linguine is coiled naturally in the center, forming an inviting mound. The pasta strands are glistening, coated in a light, emulsified sauce that hints at white wine, garlic, and sun-dried tomato. Scattered artfully over and around the pasta are succulent, plump pink shrimp, some whole, some halved, exhibiting a gentle sear. Bright crimson slivers of sun-dried tomato are interspersed, providing vibrant color contrast. A delicate shower of finely chopped fresh green parsley and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese garnish the top, adding freshness and texture. The overall composition is clean, professional, and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio.
Serve a simple green salad as a side.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes in oil, drained and thinly sliced

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 500 ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add shrimp. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcrowd. Remove shrimp from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add sliced sun-dried tomatoes to the skillet. Sauté 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze skillet, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until wine reduces slightly.
Add 250 ml reserved pasta water to the skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet. Toss to coat. Add grated Parmesan cheese. Toss until sauce thickens and coats pasta. Add more pasta water gradually if needed for desired consistency.
Return cooked shrimp to the skillet. Toss gently to combine and heat through.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Tuscan Beef Farfalle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Tuscan Beef Farfalle is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl on a simple wooden table. The rich, deep red tomato ragu coats al dente farfalle pasta, interspersed with tender, braised beef chunks and vibrant halved cherry tomatoes. Quartered artichoke hearts and borlotti beans are visible, adding texture and color. A generous sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh basil and freshly grated Parmesan cheese garnishes the top. The dish is arranged naturally, allowing the ingredients to mingle. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s warmth and rustic elegance, with a softly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the sauce.
Pair with a robust Tuscan red wine, such as Chianti or Brunello.
Enjoy as a hearty family meal, a centerpiece for convivial dining.

ingredients.name: Borlotti beans, canned, drained and rinsed

instructions: Pat beef short ribs dry. Cut into 4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook for 8-10 minutes until softened. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly reduced.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and cherry tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Once beef is tender, gently shred some beef chunks if desired, leaving others whole. Stir in borlotti beans and quartered artichoke hearts. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook farfalle pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Add drained pasta to the beef ragu. Toss to combine. Stir in most of the fresh basil.
Serve hot in shallow bowls. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Tortilla with Chorizo and Caramelized Onions
recipes.visual_description: A thick wedge of Spanish Tortilla rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The exterior is a rich golden-brown, lightly seared. The interior reveals distinct layers of thinly sliced, tender potatoes and translucent caramelized onions, interspersed with small, reddish-orange diced chorizo. The eggs are set firm but still moist. A small sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley is placed delicately on top. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a silver fork are beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rustic elegance and inviting textures. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.
Accompany with crusty bread and a simple green salad.
Offer a small bowl of olives or cured meats on the side.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (floury type like Russet or Maris Piper)

instructions: Peel potatoes. Slice thinly into 2-3 mm rounds.
Peel onions. Slice thinly into half-moons.
Heat olive oil in a 24 cm non-stick oven-safe pan over medium-low heat.
Add potato slices and onion slices to the oil. Ensure they are submerged. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes.
Potatoes and onions should be very tender but not browned. Drain excess oil, reserving 2 tablespoons in the pan. Transfer potatoes and onions to a large bowl.
In the same pan, add diced chorizo. Cook over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until crispy and fat renders. Remove chorizo with a slotted spoon, add to the potato-onion mixture.
Crack eggs into the bowl with potatoes, onions, and chorizo. Add salt. Mix gently to combine.
Pour egg mixture back into the pan with the reserved oil. Spread evenly. Cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes.
Edges should set. Place a large plate over the pan. Invert the tortilla onto the plate. Slide tortilla back into the pan, uncooked side down.
Cook for another 5-10 minutes until golden brown and firm. Internal temperature should be 75°C if chorizo is raw.
Slide tortilla onto a clean serving plate. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a good quality olive oil for authentic flavor.
The slow cooking of potatoes and onions is key to tenderness.
Ensure the pan is truly non-stick for easy flipping.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Fricassée with Green Peas and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thick, irregularly cut chunks of golden-brown pan-seared chicken are nestled within a rich, creamy sauce. Vibrant green peas and earthy sliced cremini mushrooms are generously interspersed, adding color and texture. The sauce, a light cream color, coats all elements, showing its velvety consistency. A generous sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley provides a bright green garnish over the top. The overall presentation is organized yet naturally flowing, with moderate negative space around the main dish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the inviting colors and textures of the Fricassée.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with crusty bread or rice to soak up the sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge in flour.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken until golden brown, 4 minutes per side. Remove chicken.
Add shallots to pan. Sauté 2 minutes. Add garlic and mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until tender.
Pour in white wine. Scrape pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half, 3 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to simmer. Return chicken to pan.
Cover. Cook on low heat 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken. Stir heavy cream and peas into sauce. Simmer 3 minutes.
Slice chicken into thick pieces. Return to pan with sauce.
Stir in parsley. Adjust seasoning.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Braised Chicken with Peppers and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, home-cooked Spanish-style braised chicken dish is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Two large, bone-in chicken pieces, deeply seared to a rich golden-brown, are nestled centrally. Thick strips of vibrant red and yellow bell peppers, softened but still holding their shape, are scattered generously around and over the chicken. Diced onion pieces and whole black olives are interspersed throughout the rich, savory, reddish-brown braising liquid that pools at the bottom of the plate. The chicken skin shows a crisp texture, while the meat appears tender and falling off the bone. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley adds a final touch of color. The dish sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, slightly wrinkled cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen light, suggesting a relaxed family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.
Serve alongside simple steamed white rice or patatas a lo pobre (poor man's potatoes).
Enjoy with a glass of robust Spanish red wine.
instructions: Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add bell pepper strips to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender.
Return chicken pieces to the pot. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Add pitted olives. Cover the pot.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Pea and Mint Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken has a beautiful, golden-brown seared crust, showcasing its tender interior. Beside it, a vibrant, smooth mound of bright green pea and mint puree adds a striking color contrast. The puree is artfully spooned, maintaining a soft, organic shape. A few blanched, bright green asparagus spears are arranged naturally beside the chicken, adding textural interest. A light sprinkle of fresh microgreens or chopped chives garnishes the chicken and puree. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A cotton napkin and standard flatware are placed beside the plate. The composition is clean, balanced, and inviting, with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken breasts in skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until golden-brown.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken cooks, melt 30g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add frozen peas and chicken stock to the saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes until peas are tender.
Drain most liquid from peas, reserving a few tablespoons. Transfer peas, shallots, garlic, fresh mint, remaining 30g butter, lemon zest, and half the lemon juice to a blender.
Blend until smooth and vibrant puree forms. Add reserved liquid as needed for desired consistency. Season with salt, pepper, and remaining lemon juice to taste.
If using, blanch asparagus in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain.
Rest cooked chicken breasts for 5 minutes before plating.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chili Chicken with Egg Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Crispy Chili Chicken with Egg Fried Rice is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The plate is moderately filled, leaving appropriate negative space. Golden-brown, irregularly shaped crispy chicken chunks are piled neatly on one side of the plate. The chicken pieces are visibly crunchy, showcasing their fried texture. Adjacent to the chicken, a generous portion of fluffy Egg Fried Rice forms a bed, displaying vibrant specks of yellow scrambled egg, bright green peas, and finely diced orange carrots against the white rice grains. The rice has a slight sheen from the stir-frying process. A small, simple white ceramic dipping bowl containing the reddish-orange chili mayo is placed on the plate, slightly to the side of the chicken. The entire dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly chopped vibrant green scallions over both the chicken and the rice, adding a pop of fresh color. The setting features a simple light-colored wooden table surface. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, creating soft shadows that highlight the textures of the food. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Place in a bowl.
Add 10ml soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, 5g grated ginger, 5g minced garlic, and 2g white pepper to chicken. Mix well. Marinate for 20 minutes.
In a separate bowl, whisk cornstarch, flour, baking powder, 2g salt, and cold water to form a smooth batter.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep pot to 175°C.
Dip each marinated chicken chunk into the batter, ensuring full coating. Let excess drip off.
Carefully place battered chicken into hot oil. Fry in batches to avoid overcrowding.
Fry for 4-5 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack to drain excess oil. Season lightly with salt.
For fried rice, heat 30ml vegetable oil in a clean wok over high heat.
Add remaining 10g minced garlic and white parts of green onions. Stir-fry briefly until fragrant.
Add diced carrots and frozen peas. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Push vegetables to one side. Pour beaten eggs into the empty side of the wok. Scramble eggs quickly until cooked.
Add cold jasmine rice to the wok. Break up any clumps. Stir-fry vigorously, mixing rice, vegetables, and eggs.
Add remaining 30ml soy sauce and 2g white pepper. Continue stir-frying for 3-4 minutes until rice is heated through and slightly toasted. Stir in sesame oil.
For chili mayo, combine mayonnaise, chili oil, remaining 10ml soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sugar in a small bowl. Whisk until smooth.
Serve crispy chicken chunks alongside egg fried rice. Garnish with chopped green parts of green onions. Offer chili mayo on the side for dipping.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of hearty beef and potato soup is presented in a clean, round white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The rich, reddish-brown broth is filled with tender 2-3 cm beef chunks, creamy 1.5 cm potato cubes, and vibrant diced carrots and celery. The beef exhibits a deep, seared brown exterior. The soup’s surface is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley, offering a vibrant color contrast. An optional swirl of off-white crème fraîche or sour cream provides a creamy accent. The plating is organized but not overly arranged, maintaining a professional yet approachable aesthetic. Standard silver flatware (fork and spoon) rests beside the bowl on a folded cotton napkin. The setting features natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting restaurant-style atmosphere in the background, subtly out of focus to highlight the dish. The entire bowl is visible with appropriate negative space, showcasing the dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Pair with a glass of medium-bodied red wine.

ingredients.name: Crème fraîche or sour cream (optional garnish)

instructions: Cut beef into 2-3 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, creating a roux.
Gradually whisk in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Ensure beef is submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is very tender. Internal temperature of beef should reach 75°C (167°F).
Add 1.5 cm potato cubes to the pot. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Stir in Dijon mustard.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and an optional dollop of crème fraîche or sour cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy Chicken and Broccoli Risotto is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale, creamy yellow, flows naturally within the bowl. Diced, golden-seared chicken pieces (2 cm cubes) are visibly integrated, alongside vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets and flecks of deep amber caramelized onion. A small, elegant swirl of bright white lemon-herb mayonnaise rests on top, providing a contrasting color and texture. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan. The setting is a modern bistro, with the bowl placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork and a crisp cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the dish while suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Stir occasionally.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to the pot with onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to toast rice kernels.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.
Heat chicken broth in a separate saucepan; keep it simmering.
Begin adding hot broth to the rice, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 20-25 minutes.
While risotto cooks, steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Drain well.
When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente, stir in cooked chicken and broccoli florets.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and half of the Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until creamy and fluid. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Grate lemon zest. In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise with half of the chopped parsley and lemon zest. Mix well.
Serve risotto immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish each serving with a small dollop or swirl of lemon-herb mayonnaise, remaining Parmesan cheese, and a sprinkle of fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Beef and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Beef and Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a harmonious blend of rich colors and textures. Tender, slow-cooked beef chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, are interspersed throughout the reddish-brown short-grain rice. Diced red bell pepper and onion are visible, adding vibrant color and soft texture. The dish maintains a slightly saucy, moist consistency, characteristic of traditional Spanish rice dishes, not dry or molded. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh contrast and aroma. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. The setting features a modern bistro aesthetic with natural, even lighting. Traditional Spanish flatware is placed alongside the plate, and a small side plate with a few green olives complements the authentic cultural presentation. The overall composition is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space, highlighting the robust, home-style elegance of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the flavorful sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar as a fresh accompaniment.
Serve alongside a small bowl of marinated olives.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 3-4 cm chunks

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Season beef chunks with salt and pepper. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in smoked paprika and saffron threads (if using). Cook for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until beef is very tender.

Stir in rice. Bring mixture back to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 18-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is cooked and liquid is mostly absorbed. Do not overcook; the rice should be slightly al dente and the dish should remain moist.
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The consistency of the rice dish should be moist, not dry, similar to a risotto but with individual grains. Adjust broth quantity if needed during cooking.
For best flavor, use good quality beef chuck that benefits from slow cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef short ribs is elegantly plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Rustic, fork-tender chunks of dark brown beef are piled generously atop a creamy, vibrant golden-yellow polenta base. The rich, deep red-brown braising sauce coats the beef, pooling slightly around the polenta. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh Italian parsley provides a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is organic and inviting, with appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Traditional silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are neatly placed beside the plate, all under soft, natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's warmth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread for dipping.
A glass of robust red wine.
Finish with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
instructions: Pat beef short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear ribs until deeply browned on all sides. Remove ribs.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of pot. Simmer 5 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared short ribs to the pot. Ensure ribs are mostly submerged. Cover.
Transfer to preheated oven at 160°C. Braise 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove ribs from pot. Discard herbs. Skim fat from sauce.
Shred beef from bones using two forks. Discard bones. Return shredded beef to sauce. Simmer sauce 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, prepare polenta: Bring water or broth to a boil in a separate pot. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, 20-30 minutes, until creamy and tender.
Stir butter and grated Parmesan into polenta. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle creamy polenta onto plates. Top with generous portions of braised beef and sauce.
Garnish with fresh chopped Italian parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Braising time can vary based on rib size and oven.
This dish can be made ahead; flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Mushroom Skillet with Fresh Basil and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A modest, single portion of Hearty Beef and Mushroom Skillet is presented in an everyday ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. A mound of fluffy white long-grain rice serves as the base. The rich, savory beef and mushroom mixture is spooned generously over it. Beef is cut into 2 cm cubes, deeply browned and tender. Sliced cremini mushrooms are visible, browned and savory. The sauce is glossy, deep brown, coating ingredients beautifully. Vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh basil is scattered throughout. Components are naturally arranged, touching and overlapping, conveying a comforting, homemade appearance. A simple fork is placed casually beside the bowl. A plain, light-colored cloth napkin is nearby. Warm, natural kitchen light illuminates the scene, suggesting a relaxed family dining atmosphere.
instructions: Rinse rice. Combine rice with 600ml water in a saucepan. Bring to boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand 10 minutes, covered. Fluff with fork.
Pat beef cubes dry. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Remove beef from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to skillet. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to skillet. Cook until tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Return seared beef to skillet. Pour in beef broth and soy sauce. Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover. Cook 15-20 minutes, or until beef is tender.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 30ml water to make a slurry. Stir slurry into simmering skillet. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens, about 2 minutes.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in roughly chopped fresh basil.
Ladle hearty beef and mushroom mixture over cooked rice in individual everyday ceramic bowls. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Breaded Chicken Cutlets
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown breaded chicken cutlet occupies the center of a round, off-white ceramic plate. The cutlet, pounded thin and pan-fried, exhibits a crisp, textured surface from the panko breadcrumbs, flecked with small pieces of green parsley and hints of minced garlic and onion. Its irregular, organic shape sits casually on the plate. A small, natural portion of fluffy mashed potatoes is nestled beside the cutlet, and a scattering of vibrant green steamed green beans provides a fresh color contrast. The plate is set on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone rests nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft kitchen light, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family dinner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Mashed potatoes
Steamed green beans
Simple garden salad
instructions: Pound each chicken breast to an even 1 cm thickness. Place between plastic wrap. Use a meat mallet.

Set up a breading station. Place flour in a shallow dish. Whisk eggs in a second shallow dish. Combine breadcrumbs, minced onion, minced garlic, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper in a third shallow dish. Mix well.
Dredge each chicken cutlet in flour, shaking off excess.
Dip floured chicken into whisked egg, ensuring full coating. Let excess drip off.
Press chicken firmly into breadcrumb mixture. Coat completely. Ensure breadcrumbs adhere well.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Oil should be about 1 cm deep.
Carefully place 2 chicken cutlets into hot oil. Do not overcrowd pan.
Fry for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove cooked cutlets. Place on a wire rack over paper towels to drain excess oil.
Repeat with remaining cutlets. Serve hot.
notes: Pounding chicken to even thickness ensures even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Green Pea Salad with Spiced Indian Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean, white round porcelain plate, centrally mounded with a balanced, organic arrangement. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes and vibrant green blanched peas form the core, interspersed with fresh, roughly torn basil leaves. Finely diced pickled jalapenos are scattered throughout, adding small flecks of pale green and a hint of tang. Delicate, thin shavings of Parmesan cheese are lightly draped over the top, catching the light. A glistening, golden-hued vinaigrette, subtly spiced with cumin and red chili flakes, coats all ingredients, revealing tiny spice particles. The composition is fresh, colorful, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, emphasizing a contemporary yet approachable dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing side dish with grilled meats or curries.
Can be accompanied by light flatbreads like naan or roti for scooping.
instructions: Halve cherry tomatoes. Set aside.
Blanch green peas in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain immediately and refresh in ice water. Drain well. Set aside.
Finely mince garlic. Finely dice pickled jalapeno chilies.

For the dressing, combine olive oil, lime juice, jalapeno pickling liquid, minced garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, red chili flakes, black salt, sugar, salt, and black pepper in a small bowl. Whisk until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine halved tomatoes, blanched peas, and diced pickled jalapenos.
Pour dressing over vegetables. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Roughly tear fresh basil leaves. Add to the salad. Toss again.
Shave Parmesan cheese using a vegetable peeler or grate finely.
Serve salad immediately. Garnish with Parmesan shavings.
notes: This salad offers a modern fusion of Indian spices with Western ingredients. The pickled jalapenos and Parmesan cheese provide unique tangy and savory notes not traditionally found in Indian salads, creating a balanced and intriguing flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Roasted Tomato & Garlic Pasta with Pickled Jalapeño and Basil
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant individual portion of rigatoni pasta, generously coated in a rich, rustic roasted tomato and garlic sauce, is artfully mounded in the center of a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The sauce features tender, halved roasted cherry tomatoes and soft, caramelized whole roasted garlic cloves, showcasing their rich red and golden-brown hues. Bright green fresh basil leaves, roughly torn, are generously scattered throughout and on top, providing a striking color contrast and aromatic freshness. Thin, translucent slices of pickled jalapeño are strategically placed to add a pop of vibrant green and a tangy counterpoint. A fine dusting of grated Parmesan cheese lightly blankets the dish. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, presented on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and a fork, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread for dipping
Pair with a light green salad dressed with a simple vinaigrette
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Place cherry tomatoes and whole garlic cloves on a baking sheet.
Drizzle with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tomatoes burst and garlic is tender and caramelized.
While tomatoes roast, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
Transfer roasted tomatoes and garlic to a large skillet or pot. Mash gently with a fork to create a rustic sauce.
Add dried chili flakes and vegetable broth to the skillet. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add cooked rigatoni to the sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually.
Stir in half of the fresh basil leaves, roughly torn, and half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve immediately in individual portions. Garnish each plate with remaining fresh basil, pickled jalapeño slices, and a sprinkle of grated Parmesan.
notes: For extra depth, a splash of red wine can be added to the sauce before the vegetable broth.
Adjust chili flakes to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken Thighs with Herbs and Lemon
recipes.visual_description: A single, homely portion of baked chicken is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate with a subtle, imperfect glaze. The plate holds two golden-brown, crisped chicken thighs, cooked whole and skin-on, nestled among a generous serving of roasted vegetables. Scattered around the chicken are tender potato wedges, thick carrot chunks, and soft onion wedges. Smashed garlic cloves, lightly browned, and wilted sprigs of fresh rosemary and thyme add earthy green and dark brown tones. A few bright yellow lemon slices are tucked into the arrangement. The dish has natural, organic shapes, with components touching and overlapping slightly, creating a comforting, unpretentious composition. Colors are warm browns, golden yellows, and muted greens, reflecting natural cooking. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, soft kitchen light, suggesting a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. A simple folded cloth napkin and standard metal fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Quarter the small potatoes. Peel carrots and cut into thick chunks. Cut onion into wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
In a large roasting pan, combine potatoes, carrots, onion, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Drizzle with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange vegetables in an even layer in the roasting pan. Place seasoned chicken thighs, skin-side up, over the vegetables.

Slice half of the lemon into rounds. Tuck lemon slices among the chicken and vegetables. Squeeze the juice from the remaining half lemon over everything. Drizzle remaining 30 ml olive oil over the chicken.
Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Remove from oven. Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Rosemary Potatoes and Garlic Green Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a crisp exterior, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, presented whole, exhibits a slight sheen from the pan sauce. Beside it, a cluster of irregularly cut, roasted potato wedges displays a rustic, golden-brown crust and a dusting of green rosemary flecks. Vibrant green beans, tender-crisp, are neatly arranged, showcasing their natural shape and a subtle garlic glaze. A rich, glossy pan sauce, the color of amber, is artfully drizzled over the chicken and potatoes, creating a sophisticated sheen. A small sprig of fresh rosemary provides a final aromatic and visual accent. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Fresh rosemary
ingredients.quantity: 3 sprigs, finely chopped, plus 1-2 small sprigs for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss potato wedges with 30ml olive oil, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Flip halfway through.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch green beans for 3 minutes. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain again.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts.
Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Rest for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Remove from heat. Whisk in 30g unsalted butter until melted and sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
In a separate pan, melt 30g butter over medium heat. Add blanched green beans and sauté for 2-3 minutes until heated through.
Plate rested chicken breast. Arrange roasted potato wedges and sautéed green beans alongside. Drizzle pan sauce over chicken and potatoes. Garnish with a small fresh rosemary sprig.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Lemon Herb Chicken and Rice Soup is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The golden, clear broth holds evenly distributed white chicken cubes, tender white rice grains, and vibrant green broccoli florets. The diced chicken pieces are plump and cooked through. The rice is soft, and the broccoli florets are small and tender-crisp, retaining their bright color. The soup is garnished with a generous sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley and dill, adding bursts of fresh color and aroma. A thin, bright yellow lemon slice rests delicately on the bowl's rim. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its freshness and warmth against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Stir in rice and chicken broth. Bring soup to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes.
Add broccoli florets. Continue simmering 5-7 minutes, uncovered, until broccoli is tender-crisp and rice is cooked. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove soup from heat. Stir in fresh lemon juice, chopped parsley, and chopped dill. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into individual bowls. Garnish each bowl with a thin lemon slice.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato and Chili Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Penne pasta, coated in a vibrant, rustic red-orange sauce, is neatly arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The roasted cherry tomatoes, some halved and slightly burst, are visibly integrated into the sauce, along with thin slices of garlic and red chili. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered over the top as a garnish, providing a color contrast. The pasta has a tender, al dente texture. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh colors and inviting textures. The overall presentation is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread (pane) for dipping into the sauce.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss cherry tomatoes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast tomatoes for 20-25 minutes, until softened and slightly burst.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook penne according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add thinly sliced garlic and thinly sliced chili. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add roasted tomatoes and dried oregano to the skillet. Gently mash some tomatoes with a spoon to create a saucier consistency.
Add 120 ml vegetable broth (or some reserved pasta water) to the skillet. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add drained penne to the skillet with the sauce. Toss well to coat.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a tablespoon at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.
For a deeper flavor, a splash of red wine can be added after sautéing garlic and chili, before adding tomatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Massaman Beef Curry
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, tender 4cm chunks of braised beef and 3cm cubes of golden potato submerged in a rich, glossy, orange-brown curry sauce. The sauce shows a thin layer of aromatic oil on the surface. Whole shallots and roasted peanuts are scattered throughout. The beef is served as whole chunks, showing a deeply caramelized exterior and moist interior. A single cinnamon stick and star anise pod rest on top for visual appeal. The curry is presented in a deep, traditional ceramic bowl placed on a dark wood table. A side of fluffy jasmine rice in a separate small bowl and a garnish of fresh cilantro sprigs complete the composition. The setting includes a clean cotton napkin and brass spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with Thai cucumber relish (Arjad)
Use a traditional ceramic spoon and fork
instructions: Cut beef into 4cm chunks.
Peel potatoes and cut into 3cm cubes.
Heat 200ml coconut milk in a heavy pot until oil separates.
Add curry paste and fry 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add beef chunks and sear 5 minutes to coat.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and stock.
Add cinnamon, star anise, and cardamom.
Simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add potatoes and whole shallots.
Simmer 30 minutes until beef and potatoes are tender.
Stir in palm sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind paste.
Add roasted peanuts and serve.
notes: Ensure the coconut milk 'cracks' to release its oil for an authentic flavor base.
Do not over-stir once potatoes are added to keep their shape intact.
Adjust tamarind and palm sugar to balance the sour-sweet profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Soybean & Root Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty soybean and root vegetable stew in a simple ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew is rich brown from miso, filled with tender, pale green shelled soybeans, vibrant orange carrot chunks, and soft white potato chunks. A few wilted dark green spinach leaves are visible on top. The broth is thick and savory, lightly coating the ingredients. The stew is arranged naturally, filling the bowl without overcrowding, with some ingredients slightly overlapping. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl, and a simple white cloth napkin is casually placed. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice on the side
Offer a small dish of kimchi or pickled daikon
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add carrot and potato chunks. Stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable broth and soy sauce. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
Stir in frozen shelled soybeans and miso paste. Cook for 5-7 minutes until soybeans are heated through and miso is dissolved.
Stir in sesame oil and chopped spinach. Cook until spinach wilts, about 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Serve hot.
notes: This stew is excellent for meal prepping and tastes even better the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Carrot Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, fluid carrot risotto forms a natural mound in the center, its pale orange hue punctuated by vibrant, finely diced orange carrot pieces. A perfectly pan-seared salmon fillet, skin-side up and golden-crisp, rests atop the risotto, its flaky pink flesh visible on the sides. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the salmon and risotto, adding a fresh contrast. The risotto maintains a soft, flowing consistency, not stiff or mounded into a perfect circle. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. A standard set of silver flatware (fork and knife) is neatly arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the textures and colors. The background is slightly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro or casual restaurant atmosphere, with minimal, unobtrusive elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Risotto is typically served as a 'primo piatto' (first course) in Italy, but often as a main course in casual settings.
instructions: Keep beef stock warm in a saucepan over low heat.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 20g butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and finely diced carrots. Sauté 3 minutes.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are slightly translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add one ladle of warm beef stock. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed. This takes about 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in remaining 40g butter and grated Parmesan. Stir vigorously for 1 minute (mantecatura). Season with salt and pepper.
While risotto cooks, pat salmon fillets dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon skin-side down. Cook 4-5 minutes until skin is crisp.
Flip salmon. Cook 3-4 minutes until cooked through.
Serve risotto immediately. Place a salmon fillet on top of each serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Simmered Pork and Soybeans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Japanese Simmered Pork and Soybeans is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic donburi bowl. Tender, glossy pork belly cubes, with their distinct layers of rich fat and lean meat, are nestled alongside plump, dark brown soybeans. The dish is coated in a glistening, savory-sweet, amber-brown sauce. Thin, translucent rounds of ginger are visible among the ingredients. The dish is garnished with bright green, thinly sliced diagonal pieces of scallion, offering a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm wooden dining table. Adjacent to the main bowl is a smaller, simple ceramic bowl of perfectly steamed white rice, and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests beside the donburi. Lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice as a staple accompaniment.
Can be accompanied by a small dish of tsukemono (Japanese pickled vegetables).

ingredients.name: Dashi stock (or water + 1 tsp dashi powder)

instructions: Rinse dried soybeans. Soak in plenty of water overnight (at least 8 hours). Drain.
Place soaked soybeans in a large pot. Cover with fresh water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until very tender. Drain well.
Cut pork belly into 3-4 cm cubes.
Place pork belly cubes in a pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil over high heat. Boil for 5 minutes to remove impurities. Drain pork, rinse under cold water, and pat dry.
In a clean large pot, combine dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar. Add thinly sliced ginger. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add blanched pork belly cubes and cooked soybeans to the simmering liquid. Ensure ingredients are submerged. If not, add a little more water or dashi.

Place a small lid (otoshibuta) directly on top of the ingredients, or cover the pot loosely. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until pork belly is very tender and the liquid has reduced slightly and thickened.
Remove from heat. Let the dish rest for 10-15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Serve hot in individual bowls. Garnish each serving with thinly sliced green onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Bell Pepper Chicken & Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Bell Pepper Chicken & Rice is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, leaving generous white space around the dish. A base of earthy brown rice forms a natural mound in the center. Diced, pan-seared chicken chunks, cooked to a golden-brown, are nestled atop the rice. Alongside, vibrant julienned bell peppers, both sautéed (softened, slightly charred edges) and quick-pickled (crisp, bright red and yellow), are artfully arranged, showcasing their natural colors and textures. A scattering of finely chopped fresh green onion and a few delicate cilantro leaves provide a subtle, fresh green accent. The composition is clean and unfussy, emphasizing the pure beauty of each ingredient. The plate rests on a light-colored, reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating a calm, eco-conscious ambiance with a hint of green from a blurred plant in the background. The entire plate is visible.
instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Bell Peppers: Halve one bell pepper (e.g., yellow). Remove seeds and membrane. Julienne into thin strips. In a small saucepan, combine 250 ml water, 250 ml white vinegar, 15 g salt, and 10 g sugar (optional). Bring to a boil, stirring until salt and sugar dissolve. Place julienned bell pepper strips in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over peppers. Ensure peppers are submerged. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to marinate. These can be prepared days in advance.

Cook Brown Rice: Rinse 250 g brown rice under cold water until water runs clear. In a medium saucepan, combine rinsed rice with 500 ml vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Prepare Chicken: Dice 600 g boneless, skinless chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.
Prepare Aromatics and Remaining Bell Peppers: Mince 3 garlic cloves. Dice 1 small onion. Halve the remaining bell pepper (e.g., red). Remove seeds and membrane. Cut into 2-3 cm chunks.

Cook Chicken and Vegetables: Heat 15 ml neutral cooking oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is browned on all sides and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add diced onion and bell pepper chunks. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften and begin to caramelize. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.

Combine and Finish: Return cooked chicken to the pan with the sautéed vegetables. Add 60 ml soy sauce, 30 ml rice vinegar, 15 ml maple syrup (if using), and 5 ml toasted sesame oil. Stir well to coat all ingredients. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing sauce to slightly reduce and coat the chicken and vegetables.

Serve: Divide cooked brown rice among four bowls. Top each serving with the chicken and bell pepper mixture. Garnish generously with freshly chopped cilantro or parsley and thinly sliced green onion. Serve immediately with a side of the quick-pickled bell peppers.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Gnocchi, and Pasta with Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Creamy Chicken, Gnocchi, and Pasta with Sun-Dried Tomatoes rests on an off-white, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, centered on a well-used wooden dining table. Thick chunks of seared golden-brown chicken are nestled amongst plump, lightly pan-fried gnocchi and al dente penne pasta. All components are generously coated in a rich, creamy, pale orange sauce, punctuated by vibrant crimson-red roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes and wilted dark green spinach leaves. A light sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese and a few fresh torn basil leaves adorn the top, adding a touch of freshness. The dish forms a natural, slightly mounded shape, inviting and comforting. A simple fork and knife with traditional Italian design lie casually beside the plate on a casually draped linen napkin. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's comforting textures and inviting colors. The background remains uncluttered, focusing on the homely, lived-in atmosphere of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil or parsley, for garnish
Water, for cooking pasta and gnocchi

instructions: Cut chicken breasts into thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and roughly chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile, cook gnocchi and penne pasta in separate pots of salted boiling water according to package directions. Drain well.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Add cooked gnocchi and pasta. Add fresh spinach. Toss gently until spinach wilts and all ingredients are coated in the sauce.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil or parsley.
notes: For extra flavor, you can pan-fry the gnocchi in a separate pan with a little olive oil until golden before adding to the sauce.
Ensure the sauce is simmering gently; do not boil rapidly once cream is added to prevent splitting.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (using onion and garlic as an aromatic base)

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Cherry Gastrique and Wild Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A whole, roasted chicken thigh, its skin crisped to a golden-brown, is positioned prominently. Beside it, a neat mound of fluffy wild rice pilaf, showcasing its varied grain textures. A vibrant, glossy cherry gastrique, rich with tender red cherries, is artfully spooned over the chicken and around the plate, forming pools of deep crimson. A light sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley garnishes the dish, adding a fresh color contrast. The plating is balanced and elegant, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with traditional flatware
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken.
Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 190°C. Roast 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan, rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.

In a medium saucepan, combine wild rice blend and 700ml chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 40-45 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
While rice cooks, drain excess fat from chicken pan, leaving 15ml. Add diced shallots to pan. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute more.
Add red wine vinegar and sugar to pan. Bring to a simmer, scraping up browned bits. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Add pitted fresh cherries and 100ml chicken broth to pan. Simmer 5-7 minutes, until cherries soften and sauce thickens slightly.
Remove pan from heat. Whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until melted and sauce is glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in fresh thyme.
Spoon wild rice onto the center of each plate. Place a roasted chicken thigh beside the rice. Spoon cherry gastrique generously over chicken and around the plate. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Pork and Bean Chili with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic ceramic bowl is filled with a mound of fluffy white rice, generously topped with rich, dark red chili. The chili is thick and hearty, showcasing tender chunks of slow-cooked pork, plump kidney beans, and visible flecks of diced green bell pepper and onion. A few drops of vibrant red hot sauce are visibly drizzled over the chili, adding a pop of color and promising a spicy kick. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Beside it, a simple, everyday fork and spoon rest on a plain, textured cloth napkin. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen setting. The background is slightly blurred, showing hints of a lived-in kitchen, perhaps a simple water glass. The entire plate is shown, displaying a single, generous individual portion, filling the bowl adequately without overcrowding.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra hot sauce on the side for individual spice preference.
instructions: Prepare pork: Cut pork shoulder into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Brown pork: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add pork cubes in batches. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pot. Cook until softened, 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Build flavor: Stir in chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Combine: Return browned pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, drained and rinsed kidney beans, and broth. Stir well. Add hot sauce.
Simmer chili: Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 1.5 to 2 hours, until pork is very tender. Stir occasionally.

Cook rice: While chili simmers, prepare rice. Rinse white rice. Combine rice and water in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15-18 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Finish chili: Taste chili. Adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or more hot sauce.
Serve: Ladle cooked rice into bowls. Spoon generous portions of hot chili over rice. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to personal spice preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Bell Pepper and Orange Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A generous, free-flowing portion of creamy, pale yellow risotto occupies the center of a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto has a fluid consistency, not stiff. Scattered across the top are vibrant roasted bell pepper pieces, cut into irregular, rustic 2cm chunks, showcasing rich reds and yellows. A fine sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley adds a pop of color. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and knife on a crisp white cotton napkin. The setting features soft, natural, even lighting from the side, with a subtly blurred, inviting restaurant background. The plate is not overcrowded, allowing for ample negative space to highlight the dish.

ingredients.name: Grated Parmesan cheese (or vegetarian hard cheese)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve and deseed bell peppers. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skin is blistered.
Remove peppers from oven. Transfer to a bowl. Cover tightly with cling film. Let steam for 10 minutes. Peel off skins. Dice bell peppers into 2 cm chunks. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the grains. Rice should be slightly translucent at the edges.
If using, pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot vegetable broth to the rice. Stir continuously. Wait until broth is almost fully absorbed before adding the next ladle.
Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. This process takes about 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Finely zest the orange. Squeeze 2 tablespoons of orange juice. Stir zest and juice into the risotto.
Fold in the diced roasted bell peppers. Stir gently to combine.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and grated cheese until melted and fully incorporated. The risotto should be fluid and creamy.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish each portion with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pea & Turkey Arancini with Quick-Pickled Radish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of three golden-brown, perfectly spherical arancini is artfully placed on a light cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate. The arancini, approximately 5 cm in diameter, are arranged organically, allowing ample negative space. Their exterior is crisp with visible breadcrumb texture. A few vibrant green whole peas and small pieces of turkey are visible where the arancini are broken or slightly exposed. Beside the arancini, a small, vibrant pile of thinly sliced, quick-pickled red radishes adds a pop of fuchsia, glistening slightly from the pickling liquid. A scattering of fresh, bright green pea shoots provides a delicate, natural garnish. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The background is minimalist and softly blurred, with a hint of natural light filtering in. The overall composition is clean, simple, and celebrates the natural beauty and sustainable ethos of the ingredients.
instructions: Cook turkey: Heat a pan. Add ground turkey. Cook until browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Break into small pieces. Drain excess fat.
Cook peas: Blanch green peas in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain. Mash half of the peas roughly. Keep the other half whole.
Prepare arancini mixture: In a large bowl, combine cooked rice, cooked turkey, mashed peas, whole peas, and grated cheese. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Form arancini: Take small portions (approx. 50-60g) of the mixture. Form into uniform balls.

Bread arancini: Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with breadcrumbs. Roll each arancini in flour, then dip in egg, then coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs. Press gently to adhere crumbs.
Fry arancini: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 170°C. Fry arancini in batches for 4-6 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature is hot. Drain on paper towels.
Quick-pickle radish: In a small bowl, combine thinly sliced radishes, rice vinegar, water, and sugar. Let sit for at least 15 minutes.
Plate arancini: Arrange arancini on a plate. Garnish with quick-pickled radish and fresh pea shoots.
notes: This recipe utilizes leftover cooked rice, promoting zero-waste.
Stale bread can be used to make fresh breadcrumbs.
The quick-pickled radish adds a bright, acidic counterpoint to the rich arancini.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Lemon-Dill Sauce and Roasted Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of pan-seared salmon rests on an everyday ceramic plate. The salmon fillet is golden-brown with a crispy skin, showcasing its natural, flaky texture. Beside the salmon, a pile of vibrant green roasted asparagus spears is casually arranged. A glossy, pale yellow lemon-dill sauce is drizzled generously over the salmon. A fresh lemon wedge and a small sprig of fresh dill garnish the dish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table in a homely family kitchen. Standard silver flatware (fork and knife) is placed beside the plate.
