recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Chicken & Corn Rice is presented on a clean, round, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. A generous mound of fluffy, light brown rice, subtly flecked with diced red tomato, forms the base. Two substantial, golden-skinned chicken chunks rest naturally on top of the rice, showcasing their tender texture and rich color, without being sliced or fanned. Alongside, a vibrant heap of fresh corn kernels and diced red tomato salsa, lightly glossed with fermented hot sauce, adds a pop of yellow and red. Scattered fresh green basil leaves provide a final aromatic touch and color contrast. The composition is minimalist and organic, with ample negative space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting, creating an eco-conscious, inviting ambiance. The entire plate is visible, emphasizing the dish as the centerpiece.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden and crispy. Flip and sear other side briefly. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Slice mushrooms. Roughly chop 2 garlic cloves. Add mushrooms and chopped garlic to the skillet. Sauté until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Pour in beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce heat to medium.

Return chicken to the skillet. Pour in 250ml chicken stock. Cover. Simmer for 25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside to rest. Keep braising liquid in skillet.
While chicken cooks, prepare corn and tomatoes. Cut corn kernels from cobs. Reserve cobs for stock. Dice 2 tomatoes. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Thinly slice fresh chili.

In a medium saucepan, combine rice, 500ml chicken stock, diced tomatoes, and minced garlic. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.
For the corn and tomato salsa, combine corn kernels, remaining diced tomato, and sliced chili in a small bowl. Stir in fermented hot sauce. Season with salt.
Once chicken is rested, cut each thigh into 2-3 large chunks. Do not slice thinly or fan out.
Stir chopped basil into the cooked rice. Taste and adjust seasoning.
To serve, spoon a portion of rice onto each plate. Arrange chicken chunks on top of the rice. Spoon the corn and tomato salsa alongside the chicken.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sirloin with Rosemary Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Pan-Seared Sirloin with Rosemary Butter is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The beef sirloin steak, a thick, whole piece, is centrally placed. It boasts a rich, deep golden-brown crust from searing, with a visible glossy sheen from the rosemary butter baste. A small, neat mound of halved roasted baby potatoes, golden-brown and slightly crispy, is arranged beside the steak. Four to five vibrant green asparagus spears, tender-crisp, are neatly placed alongside the potatoes. A small pool of clarified rosemary-garlic butter pan sauce is artfully spooned over a portion of the steak and potatoes, creating a rich, reflective highlight. A single fresh rosemary sprig rests delicately on the side of the plate near the steak, adding a touch of vibrant green. The overall color palette is rich with browns, golds, and vibrant greens. The textures are a mix of crispy, tender, and smooth. Moderate negative space ensures a professional, uncluttered presentation. The plate rests on a simple light-colored wooden or laminate table surface. Standard silver flatware (fork and knife) is positioned neatly beside the plate. A folded light-colored cotton napkin is placed adjacent. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating soft shadows. The background is a subtly blurred, warm-toned modern bistro interior, suggesting a relaxed but refined dining atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and halve baby potatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until tender and golden-brown.
Pat beef sirloin steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place steaks in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. A deep brown crust should form.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter, whole rosemary sprigs, and smashed garlic cloves to the pan.
Tilt the pan slightly. Spoon the melted butter mixture over the steaks continuously for 2-3 minutes, basting thoroughly.
Remove steaks from pan. Transfer to a cutting board. Rest for 5-7 minutes. This allows juices to redistribute.
While steaks rest, blanch or steam asparagus spears until tender-crisp, about 2-3 minutes. Drain well.
To serve, place one whole pan-seared sirloin steak on each plate. Arrange roasted baby potatoes and blanched asparagus alongside.
Spoon the pan sauce from the skillet over the beef and potatoes. Garnish with a fresh rosemary sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Layer Cake with Lime Curd and Toasted Meringue
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Coconut Layer Cake with Lime Curd and Toasted Meringue is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The slice reveals distinct, uniform layers: a light, fluffy coconut cake base, a vibrant, pale yellow layer of smooth lime curd, and a second cake layer, all crowned with a generous, artfully swirled topping of glossy white Italian meringue. The meringue features subtle golden-brown peaks, achieved by light torching. The top of the meringue is scattered with golden-brown toasted desiccated coconut flakes and a fine dusting of bright green lime zest, providing textural contrast and a pop of color. The cake's sides are lightly coated with the meringue. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver dessert fork placed neatly beside it. In the slightly blurred background, the remaining whole cake, showing its full meringue-covered form, sits on a minimalist cake stand. Natural, even lighting highlights the cake's textures and colors, creating a professional and inviting presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 15 cm round cake pans. Line bottoms with parchment paper.
Cream softened butter and 200g sugar in a stand mixer until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix in vanilla.
Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with coconut milk. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Fold in 50g desiccated coconut.
Divide batter evenly between prepared pans. Bake 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare Lime Curd: Zest 2 limes. Juice all limes to yield 60ml. In a saucepan, whisk egg yolks, 75g sugar, lime zest, and lime juice.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens. It should coat the back of a spoon. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter cubes until melted and smooth. Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill until firm, at least 2 hours.
Prepare Coconut Meringue: Toast 30g desiccated coconut in a dry pan over medium-low heat until golden. Set aside.
Combine 150g sugar and 45ml water in a small saucepan. Heat over medium-high heat until syrup reaches 115°C (soft ball stage). Use a candy thermometer.
While syrup cooks, begin whipping egg whites in a clean stand mixer bowl until soft peaks form.

Once syrup reaches 115°C, slowly pour hot syrup in a steady stream into whipping egg whites. Continue whipping on high speed until meringue is glossy, thick, and holds stiff peaks. Beat until bowl is cool to the touch.
Assemble Cake: Level cooled cake layers with a serrated knife if needed.
Place one cake layer on a serving plate. Spread chilled lime curd evenly over the top.
Place second cake layer on top of curd.
Spread or pipe coconut meringue over top and sides of the cake. Create decorative swirls or peaks.
Garnish with toasted coconut flakes and fresh lime zest. Serve immediately or chill briefly.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti all'Amatriciana with Crispy Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spaghetti all'Amatriciana is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, reflecting a modern bistro aesthetic. The al dente spaghetti is neatly twirled, coated generously in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. Scattered over the pasta are golden-brown, crispy bacon lardons, providing textural contrast. Freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese forms a snowy mound atop the dish, with a few delicate green basil leaves offering a pop of color. The sauce is thick enough to cling to the pasta but still appears moist and inviting. The overall composition is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, beside a standard silver fork and a neatly folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its appetizing colors and textures against a subtly blurred restaurant background, suggesting a casual yet refined dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with extra grated Pecorino Romano cheese.
A glass of dry red wine, such as a Lazio Cesanese or a Sangiovese, complements the dish beautifully.

ingredients.name: Peeled whole tomatoes (canned, San Marzano preferred)

instructions: Cut bacon into 1 cm lardons. Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add bacon lardons.
Cook bacon until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat in skillet.
Finely dice the red onion. Mince the garlic cloves.
Add diced onion to the skillet with bacon fat. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Crush peeled whole tomatoes with your hands into the skillet. Stir well. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
While sauce simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add spaghetti.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water before draining.
Add drained spaghetti to the skillet with the sauce. Add reserved pasta water gradually, tossing until sauce emulsifies and coats the pasta.
Return crispy bacon lardons to the pasta. Toss to combine.
Grate Pecorino Romano cheese. Serve immediately, topped with more grated Pecorino and a sprig of fresh basil or parsley.
notes: For authentic Amatriciana, use guanciale (cured pork jowl) instead of smoked bacon. Pancetta is also a suitable alternative.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Tomato and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned braised chicken thigh rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, with its crispy, golden-brown skin, is nestled in a pool of rich, glossy, deep red-brown tomato and herb sauce. The sauce clings to the chicken and showcases tender pieces of diced onion and tomato. Scattered over the chicken and sauce are vibrant green flecks of fresh chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, hinting at a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded white cotton napkin lies beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the dish's comforting textures and colors. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down first, until deep golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, beef stock, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the liquid. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot and reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from the pot and set aside. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce the sauce, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly to a desired consistency, about 5-10 minutes.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning if needed. Return chicken to the pot or spoon sauce over chicken on individual plates.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Dark Beer Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty European beef and dark beer stew is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The stew features generous, tender chunks of braised beef, rustic quartered potatoes, and whole cremini mushrooms, all suspended in a rich, glossy, dark brown gravy. The beef shows a deep, caramelized crust from initial searing. The potatoes are slightly softened but hold their shape. A scattering of bright green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant contrast against the deep brown and off-white tones. The stew has a comforting, rustic appearance with a professional finish. It is served on a simple wooden table. A white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's texture and color, creating an inviting and authentic casual dining scene. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space around the bowl, emphasizing the warmth and richness of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 4 cm cubes
Carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks
Celery stalk, cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry. Toss with flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced smoked bacon. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Add beef to the pot in batches. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Return seared beef and cooked bacon to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add quartered potatoes and mushrooms to the pot. Continue simmering, covered, until beef and potatoes are tender, about 45-60 minutes more.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Season stew with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Rigatoni with Roasted Potatoes and Smoked Cheddar Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Rigatoni with Roasted Potatoes and Smoked Cheddar Tomato Sauce is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish is mounded, showcasing rigatoni pasta tubes coated in a rich, deep red tomato sauce, interspersed with tender, golden-edged roasted potato small cubes. A generous, bubbly layer of melted, golden-brown smoked cheddar cheese forms a crisp crust over the top. Scattered fresh green chopped parsley provides a vibrant color contrast. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, with a softly blurred restaurant-style background. The scene is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing the comforting, rustic appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm small cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes. Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 125 ml pasta water.
While pasta cooks, finely chop onion and mince garlic. Heat remaining 45 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn garlic.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring sauce to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Grate smoked cheddar cheese.
Add cooked rigatoni and roasted potato cubes to the tomato sauce. Stir to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Transfer mixture to a 23x33 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe pot. Sprinkle grated smoked cheddar evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes. Cheese should be melted and bubbly. The top should be golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Chop fresh parsley. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Coca-Cola & Cocoa Braised Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of Coca-Cola & Cocoa Braised Chicken on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, dark brown braised chicken thigh, with a glossy, reduced sauce coating its surface, sits prominently atop a smooth, pale cream turnip puree. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. Beside it, a neat mound of fluffy white basmati rice, subtly flecked with bright green chopped parsley. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. Colors are natural and appealing: deep brown from the chicken and sauce, creamy off-white from the turnip, and bright green from the fresh parsley garnish. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the professional yet approachable plating.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear for another 3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Dice onion into small cubes. Mince garlic. Add onion to the pot, sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in vodka. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until vodka nearly evaporates.
Whisk together Coca-Cola, cocoa powder, ketchup, brewed tea, and chicken stock. Pour into the pot. Add bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.

Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure liquid partially covers chicken. Cover pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 170°C (340°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
While chicken braises, peel turnips. Cut turnips into 2cm chunks. Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet at 200°C (400°F) for 25-30 minutes, until very tender.
Transfer roasted turnips to a food processor or blender. Add whole milk, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Process until smooth and creamy. Adjust consistency with more milk if needed. Keep warm.
Cook rice according to package instructions. Fluff with a fork. Stir in half of the chopped parsley.

Remove braised chicken from the pot. Discard bay leaf. Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Reduce sauce over medium-high heat on the stovetop until slightly thickened, about 5-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

To serve, spoon a generous portion of creamy turnip puree onto the center of each plate. Place one braised chicken thigh on top of the puree. Spoon reduced Coca-Cola & cocoa sauce over the chicken. Serve herbed rice alongside. Garnish with remaining fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Medley
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spicy Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Medley is presented on a simple, cream-colored ceramic plate with natural imperfections. Roasted golden-brown chicken chunks (4-5cm) are nestled among tender-crisp broccoli florets and creamy white cauliflower florets, all coated in a vibrant reddish-orange spicy garlic glaze. Bright yellow corn kernels are scattered throughout, adding pops of color. The arrangement is natural and casual, with components touching and slightly overlapping. A light scattering of fresh chopped parsley adds a touch of green. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A casually placed cloth napkin and sturdy everyday flatware complete the homely, lived-in atmosphere of a family kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 4-5cm chunks. Pat dry.
Cut broccoli and cauliflower into small florets.
Mince garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, broccoli, cauliflower, 45ml olive oil, 3g salt, 1g black pepper, and 3g smoked paprika. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 20 minutes.
While roasting, prepare the spicy garlic sauce. In a small bowl, combine remaining 15ml olive oil, minced garlic, hot sauce, remaining 2g salt, and 2g smoked paprika.
After 20 minutes, remove tray from oven. Stir vegetables. Pour the spicy garlic sauce over the chicken and vegetables. Toss gently to coat.
Add corn kernels to the tray.
Return to oven. Roast for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to taste for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Tuscan Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Pasta rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The dish features golden-brown roasted chicken chunks, vibrant green broccoli florets, and tender-crisp cauliflower florets, all mixed loosely with al dente penne pasta. A light, savory pan sauce coats the pasta and vegetables. Torn fresh basil leaves are scattered over the top, adding a pop of green. The chicken chunks are rustic and substantial, not fanned. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting. A simple metal fork is placed beside the plate. In the background, a casually placed linen napkin and a small bowl of grated Parmesan cheese complete the homely, inviting scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Offer crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the sauce.
Serve with a glass of light red wine, like Chianti, for adults.
Provide extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm thick chunks. Place on the baking tray.
Cut broccoli and cauliflower into small florets. Add to the baking tray with chicken.
Peel and thinly slice garlic cloves. Scatter over chicken and vegetables.
Drizzle 45 ml olive oil over everything. Season generously with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and vegetables are tender-crisp and slightly browned.
While roasting, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 125 ml pasta water.
Remove chicken and vegetables from the oven. Transfer to a large mixing bowl.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Add reserved garlic slices from the baking tray (if any stuck to the tray) and cook for 30 seconds. Pour in chicken broth and reserved pasta water. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the broth. Add roasted chicken and vegetables. Toss to combine.
Tear fresh basil leaves and stir into the pasta. Season with more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately. Garnish with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For extra flavor, you can add a pinch of dried oregano or red pepper flakes to the chicken and vegetables before roasting.
Ensure vegetables are spread in a single layer on the baking tray for optimal roasting and browning.

recipes.recipe_name: Adobo Chicken and Pork with Creamy Chipotle Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Adobo Chicken and Pork with Creamy Chipotle Beans is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The base is a generous bed of smooth, dark purplish-black creamy chipotle black beans. On top are artfully arranged, rustic chunks of rich, deep reddish-brown adobo-braised pork (4 cm cubes) and chicken (4 cm chunks). The meats are tender, exhibiting a glistening, savory surface. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, bright green coriander leaves provides a fresh counterpoint. Beside the plate, two warm, folded corn tortillas are neatly stacked. A small, simple white ramekin holds bright pink pickled red onions. The setting is a natural wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin, under soft, natural lighting, evoking a modern bistro with authentic Mexican elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges on the side for a squeeze of freshness.
Accompany with a small dish of pickled red onions or salsa fresca.
instructions: Prepare chiles. Remove stems and seeds from ancho and guajillo chiles. Place in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let soak for 20 minutes until softened.

Make adobo sauce. Drain softened chiles. Transfer to a blender. Add half of the onion, 4 garlic cloves, cumin, oregano, cloves, vinegar, diced tomatoes, and 250 ml chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve if desired for a smoother sauce.

Sear pork. Cut pork shoulder into 4 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork cubes until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot.
Sear chicken. Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Sear chicken chunks in the same pot until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.

Braise meats. Pour adobo sauce into the pot. Bring to a gentle simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Return seared pork to the pot. Ensure pork is mostly submerged. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 1.5 hours.

Add chicken to braise. Add seared chicken chunks to the pot with the pork. Continue to simmer covered for another 30-45 minutes, or until both pork and chicken are very tender. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

Prepare creamy chipotle beans. While meats braise, dice remaining half onion and mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Heat a small amount of oil in a separate saucepan. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.

Cook beans. Add rinsed black beans, selected chipotle chiles (chopped) and adobo sauce, and remaining 500 ml chicken broth to the saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.

Blend beans. Transfer half of the bean mixture to a blender. Blend until creamy and smooth. Return blended beans to the saucepan. Stir to combine with the remaining whole beans. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.
Serve. Ladle creamy chipotle beans onto individual plates. Arrange generous portions of braised adobo pork cubes and chicken chunks over the beans. Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust chipotle quantity to your preferred spice level.
traditional_techniques: Rehydrating dried chiles to create a sauce base

recipes.recipe_name: Butter Chicken with Roasted Cauliflower
recipes.visual_description: A single, inviting portion of Butter Chicken with Roasted Cauliflower is presented in a clean, white porcelain dinner bowl. The vibrant, reddish-orange curry sauce, rich and velvety, envelops succulent, seared chicken chunks (3-4 cm). Tender, roasted cauliflower florets (3-4 cm), exhibiting delicate charring on their edges, are thoughtfully arranged alongside the chicken within the sauce. A generous sprinkle of bright green fresh coriander leaves garnishes the dish, providing a striking color contrast and freshness. The bowl is positioned on a simple, natural wooden table surface. Alongside, a small, elegant white bowl holds fluffy basmati rice, and a piece of warm, golden-brown naan bread rests nearby. A neatly folded white cotton napkin completes the simple, professional restaurant-style setting. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm and authentic Indian dining experience without being cluttered.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fluffy Basmati rice.
Serve with warm Naan bread for scooping.
Offer a side of cooling Raita (yogurt dip).
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Cut cauliflower into 3-4 cm florets.
Toss cauliflower florets with 1 tbsp vegetable oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly charred.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 30g butter to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in garam masala, turmeric, cumin, coriander, and chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to layer spices.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Soak cashews in hot water for 10 minutes. Drain cashews. Blend cashews with 50ml water until very smooth to form a paste.
Add cashew paste to the tomato mixture. Stir well.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in remaining 30g butter and heavy cream. Simmer for 2 minutes. Do not boil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt.
Serve butter chicken alongside roasted cauliflower. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.
notes: For CHICKEN: Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) - minimum safe temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Vanilla Celebration Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Classic Vanilla Celebration Cake rests on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The slice reveals two layers of light, airy vanilla sponge separated by a generous layer of creamy white vanilla buttercream. The top and sides of the slice are also coated in buttercream, with a few rustic swirls. In the background, the remaining whole cake, lightly frosted with more rustic swirls, sits on a wooden cake stand on a well-used wooden dining table. The table features a casually placed, folded beige linen napkin and a plain fork. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The colors are natural: golden-brown cake, off-white buttercream. The focus is on the inviting texture and homemade appeal of the cake.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 15cm round cake tin. Line base with baking paper.
Beat 150g butter and 150g caster sugar in a bowl until pale and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time. Beat well after each addition.
Stir in 1 tsp vanilla extract.
Fold in 150g self-raising flour gradually until just combined.
Add 2 tbsp milk. Mix gently.
Pour batter into prepared tin. Smooth top.
Bake 25-30 minutes. Cake is done when a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool in tin for 10 minutes. Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.
For buttercream: Beat 100g softened butter in a clean bowl until soft.
Gradually add 200g icing sugar. Beat until smooth.
Stir in 1 tsp vanilla extract and 1-2 tbsp milk. Beat until light and fluffy.
Once cake is completely cool, slice horizontally into two even layers.
Spread half the buttercream on the bottom layer.
Place top layer on. Spread remaining buttercream over top and sides of the cake.
Decorate simply as desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Pasta with Toasted Garlic Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. A generous portion of rigatoni pasta, coated in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce, forms a central mound. Tender, golden-brown chicken medallions, sliced into thick chunks, are artfully arranged atop and around the pasta, showcasing their juicy interior. Sautéed cremini mushrooms are interspersed throughout the sauce, adding earthy tones. The dish is crowned with a scattering of golden, crispy panko breadcrumbs, providing a textural contrast. Vibrant green fresh basil leaves are generously torn and sprinkled over the entire dish, adding a fresh aroma and pop of color. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese completes the plating. The composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space around the food. Standard silver flatware, a fork and knife, are placed neatly beside the plate, and a folded white cotton napkin rests nearby. The background is clean and subtly blurred, maintaining a modern bistro ambiance, illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting that highlights the food's natural colors and textures.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions or chunks.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain pasta.

In the same pan, add remaining 30ml olive oil. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add 3 cloves minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Add crushed tomatoes, halved cherry tomatoes, chicken broth, and red pepper flakes (if using) to the pan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10-12 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.

While sauce simmers, heat a small dry pan over medium heat. Add panko breadcrumbs. Toast 3-4 minutes until golden. Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 1 clove minced garlic and 15g grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Add most of the chopped basil and remaining 35g grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water until desired consistency.

Divide pasta among 4 plates. Arrange sliced chicken over pasta. Top with toasted garlic breadcrumbs. Garnish generously with fresh basil. Serve immediately with extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of creamy Garlic Mushroom Risotto is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The risotto is free-flowing and naturally arranged, showcasing its luscious, fluid consistency. Specks of finely chopped fresh green parsley are scattered over the top, along with a light dusting of freshly grated white Parmesan cheese. The warm, inviting colors of the dish – golden-beige rice, earthy brown mushrooms, and vibrant green parsley – are illuminated by soft, natural kitchen lighting. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple metal spoon. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin is nearby, contributing to the homely, comfortable atmosphere of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto should be enjoyed at its peak creaminess.
Pair with a glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking.
Offer crusty bread to sop up any extra sauce.
instructions: Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan. Keep it simmering over low heat.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil and 20g butter over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until tender and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladle of simmering broth to the rice. Stir constantly until broth is absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring continuously, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
Risotto is ready when rice is al dente and creamy. It should be fluid, not dry.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 40g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. This is 'mantecatura'.
Stir vigorously until butter and cheese are fully incorporated and risotto is creamy.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The key to creamy risotto is constant stirring and adding broth gradually.
Ensure broth is hot when adding to avoid cooling the rice.
Adjust garlic quantity to personal preference for a stronger or milder flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Maple-Mustard Glazed Turkey Breast with Crab & Mango Relish and Thyme Mash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Maple-Mustard Glazed Turkey Breast is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. The roasted turkey breast, cut into thick, substantial medallions, exhibits a golden-brown, slightly caramelized crust and a moist, tender interior. It is placed prominently on the plate. Beside the turkey is a creamy, smooth mound of mashed potatoes, speckled with fine green flecks of fresh thyme. Adjacent to the turkey, a vibrant mound of diced orange-yellow mango and white lump crab meat, interspersed with tiny red chili pieces, forms the relish, adding a burst of color and texture. A light, glossy red wine pan sauce is subtly drizzled over the turkey. The composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate, accompanied by standard, clean flatware. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the main subject.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Season turkey breast with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear turkey breast for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
In a small bowl, whisk together maple syrup, Dijon mustard, brown sugar, and beer to make the glaze. Brush half of the glaze over the seared turkey.

Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast turkey for 20-25 minutes, brushing with remaining glaze halfway through, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest turkey for 10 minutes before slicing into thick medallions or chunks.

While turkey roasts, peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Place potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes until fork-tender.
Drain potatoes. Return to hot pot. Add butter, milk or cream, and 10g chopped fresh thyme. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
For the relish, peel and dice mango into small cubes. In a bowl, gently combine diced mango, lump crab meat, minced red chili, and lime or lemon juice. Season with a pinch of salt.
Deglaze the turkey pan with red wine over medium heat, scraping up browned bits. Simmer until slightly reduced to create a light pan sauce.

To plate, place a generous mound of creamy thyme mashed potatoes on one side of a clean white plate. Arrange thick turkey medallions or chunks beside the mash. Spoon a portion of the vibrant crab and mango relish next to the turkey. Drizzle the red wine pan sauce over the turkey. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Chicken Meatballs in Tomato Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rustic Pork and Chicken Meatballs rests in a shallow ceramic bowl, bathed in a rich, vibrant red tomato basil sauce. The meatballs are irregularly shaped, showcasing a homemade quality, and are golden-brown from searing before simmering. They are arranged naturally, some partially submerged, others peeking out. The sauce is thick with visible specks of minced garlic and finely diced onion, and bright green ribbons of fresh basil are scattered generously over the top. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese creates a delicate white contrast. The plate is an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic, with a subtle rim. It sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table. A simple fork and knife are placed beside the bowl. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a family dining area.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cooked spaghetti, penne, or other pasta.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread (pane casereccio) for dipping.
instructions: Mince 2 cloves of garlic. Dice the onion. Chop fresh basil, reserving some for garnish.
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, ground chicken, 2 minced garlic cloves, egg, breadcrumbs, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into 16-20 meatballs, about 4-5 cm in diameter.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear meatballs in batches until browned on all sides. Remove meatballs and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add sugar, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Stir well. Bring sauce to a simmer.

Return browned meatballs to the sauce. Ensure meatballs are mostly submerged. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until meatballs are cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
Stir in most of the chopped basil. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Dijon Herb Sauce and Gluten-Free Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cut into thick medallions, is positioned on one side of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A neat, moderate portion of gluten-free penne pasta is arranged beside the chicken. A rich, golden-brown Dijon herb sauce is generously drizzled over the chicken and lightly coats the pasta. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley and chives are scattered over the chicken and pasta as a garnish. The chicken exhibits a beautiful golden-brown sear, contrasting with its tender, cooked interior. The penne is al dente, with distinct ridged texture. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, reflecting a modern bistro ambiance. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant setting without distracting from the food.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs
Dry white wine or apple cider vinegar (optional)

instructions: Cook gluten-free penne according to package directions. Drain. Keep warm.
Pat chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced shallot to the same skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute more.
Deglaze with white wine or apple cider vinegar if using. Scrape up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in chicken stock and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Simmer 1-2 minutes to heat through.
Stir in butter, if using, until melted. Stir in fresh parsley and chives.
Serve chicken immediately with gluten-free penne. Spoon sauce over chicken and pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Horseradish Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of pan-seared chicken with horseradish cream sauce is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken breast is a whole, golden-brown piece, prominently placed, with a generous, creamy white horseradish sauce spooned over its surface and pooling around its base. The sauce has a smooth, rich texture. Alongside the chicken, vibrant green roasted asparagus spears are neatly arranged, showcasing their tender-crisp texture and slight char. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with the golden chicken, rich white sauce, and bright green vegetables creating a balanced composition. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, reflecting a modern bistro setting. Standard silver flatware is placed beside the plate, and a crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, focusing all attention on the professionally plated meal.

ingredients.name: Dry white wine or chicken broth

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil and half of the butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Cook for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside to rest.
While chicken cooks, toss asparagus spears with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet at 190°C (375°F) for 8-12 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Return skillet to stovetop over medium heat. Add remaining butter. Sauté diced shallot until softened, about 2-3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with white wine or chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in heavy cream and prepared horseradish. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return rested chicken breasts to the skillet, coating them in the horseradish cream sauce.
Serve chicken immediately with horseradish cream sauce spooned over and roasted asparagus spears arranged alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Dijon Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Creamy Dijon Chicken Pasta rests on an off-white ceramic plate, centrally placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The pasta, penne, is coated in a rich, creamy, pale yellow sauce. Golden-brown seared chicken breast thick chunks are nestled among the pasta, showing a slightly crispy exterior from pan-frying. Wilted green spinach leaves are visible throughout, adding a touch of color. Diced onion and minced garlic are subtly integrated into the sauce. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley garnishes the dish, providing a vibrant contrast. The arrangement is natural and comforting, with components touching and slightly overlapping. A simple fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate on a folded cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, evoking a cozy family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add penne pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120 millilitres of pasta water.
Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15 millilitres olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 millilitres olive oil to the skillet. Add diced yellow onion. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard, heavy cream, and chicken broth. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes until spinach wilts.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the skillet. Add cooked pasta. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly with the sauce. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Chop fresh parsley. Serve pasta immediately, garnished with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sardines with Nectarine-Annatto Salsa and Vegemite Couscous
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate on a simple wooden bistro table. A single portion of fluffy, vegemite-infused couscous forms a gently mounded base. Three pan-seared sardine fillets, skin crisped to golden-brown, are artfully arranged as whole pieces on top of and beside the couscous. A generous spoon of vibrant nectarine-annatto salsa, featuring small diced firm-ripe nectarines and finely diced red onion, is draped over the sardines and spills onto the couscous. The salsa's bright orange-red hue contrasts beautifully. Fresh, finely chopped parsley is scattered as a verdant garnish. The composition is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate, under natural, even light, with a soft bistro background.
instructions: Prepare annatto oil: Combine 100ml olive oil and annatto seeds in a small saucepan. Heat gently over low heat for 5-7 minutes. Do not boil. Strain oil into a small bowl, discard seeds. Let cool.

Prepare nectarine-annatto salsa: Dice nectarines into small cubes. Finely dice the red onion. Finely chop 20g of the parsley. In a bowl, combine diced nectarines, red onion, chopped parsley, 2 tablespoons of the prepared annatto oil, and juice from half a lime. Season with salt and pepper. Stir gently. Set aside.
Prepare vegemite couscous: In a medium bowl, dissolve vegemite in the hot vegetable broth. Add couscous. Stir well. Cover and let stand for 5 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.

Sear sardines: Pat sardine fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Place sardine fillets skin-side down in the hot oil. Sear for 2-3 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Flip and cook for 1 minute on the flesh side. Cook in batches if necessary.

Plate the dish: Spoon a portion of the vegemite couscous onto each plate, forming a gentle mound. Arrange 3-4 seared sardine fillets as whole pieces on top of and beside the couscous. Spoon a generous amount of nectarine-annatto salsa over the sardines and couscous. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley sprigs or finely chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Gâteau Mangue-Érable, Coulis de Vin Rouge et Croustillant de Crabe
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Gâteau Mangue-Érable is centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The cake slice is golden-brown on the exterior, revealing a moist, light crumb with subtle specks of mango within. A delicate, glossy pool of ruby-red Red Wine Coulis is artfully drizzled alongside the cake, with a tiny, fresh thyme sprig placed on its edge. Perched delicately on top of the cake slice is a small, irregular piece of Caramelized Crab Crisp, a golden, translucent shard with visible strands of finely shredded, caramelized crab meat. A tiny, precise dot of the deep amber Maple-Mustard-Turkey Drizzle is placed strategically on the plate, separate from the main cake. The entire presentation maintains moderate negative space. The table setting is a modern bistro style with a simple wooden surface. A silver dessert fork rests beside the plate on a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of strong espresso.
Offer a digestif like Cognac or Armagnac after the meal.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter
ingredients.quantity: 150 g, melted, plus extra for greasing

ingredients.name: Roasted turkey stock
ingredients.quantity: 50 ml, highly reduced to a glaze

instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
Sift flour, potato starch, and baking powder into a bowl. Add granulated sugar and brown sugar. Whisk to combine.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, maple syrup, beer, and mango puree.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Fold in melted butter.
Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Bake 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in pan 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.

For Red Wine Coulis: Combine red wine, 20g brown sugar, thyme sprigs, and chili flakes in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and simmer until liquid is reduced by half and slightly syrupy. Strain and cool.

For Caramelized Crab Crisp: Spread dried shredded crab meat thinly on a parchment-lined baking sheet. In a small saucepan, combine 80g granulated sugar and 30ml water. Heat over medium-high heat without stirring until sugar dissolves and caramelizes to a golden amber. Quickly pour caramel over the crab meat. Spread thinly. Let cool completely and harden. Break into small, irregular pieces.
For Maple-Mustard-Turkey Drizzle: In a very small bowl, whisk reduced turkey stock with remaining 30g maple syrup and Dijon mustard until smooth. Set aside.
notes: Ensure crab meat is very dry before making the crisp for best results.
The turkey stock reduction should be very concentrated for a subtle umami note.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Bake is presented on a rustic, matte ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features golden-brown roasted chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, nestled among a medley of vibrant, caramelized vegetables. Thick-cut potato wedges and chunky carrot slices show tender, slightly browned edges. Bright green broccoli florets are interspersed with quartered mushrooms, substantial bell pepper chunks, and sweet halved cherry tomatoes, all coated in a light herb seasoning. Melted, bubbly shredded cheese forms a comforting golden crust over parts of the dish. The overall arrangement is casual and inviting, as if served directly from a family kitchen. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and natural colors of the home-cooked meal.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 250g, peeled and cut into 2 cm thick slices

ingredients.name: Dried herbs (e.g., oregano, thyme, rosemary blend)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, carrot slices, onion wedges, bell pepper chunks, broccoli florets, quartered mushrooms, and minced garlic.
Drizzle vegetables with olive oil. Add dried herbs, salt, and black pepper. Toss well to coat.
Place seasoned vegetables in a single layer in a large baking dish (approx. 25x35 cm).
Season chicken thighs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Nestle chicken thighs among the vegetables in the baking dish.
Pour chicken broth over the vegetables.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the baking dish. Stir vegetables gently.
Continue baking for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender.
Remove dish from oven. Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven and bake for 5-7 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and lightly golden.

recipes.recipe_name: Nectarine, Burrata, and Arugula Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant composition. A bed of fresh, bright green arugula forms the base. Juicy nectarines, sliced into 1 cm wedges, are artfully arranged across the greens, displaying soft orange and red hues. Creamy white burrata, torn into irregular, luscious pieces, is nestled amongst the fruit and greens, its soft texture contrasting with crisp arugula. Toasted, roughly chopped pistachios are scattered, adding crunch and light green. Fresh basil leaves are thoughtfully placed for deeper green and aroma. A light vinaigrette is evenly drizzled, enhancing natural colors. The presentation is fresh, inviting, and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, natural lighting, and a cotton napkin, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Slice nectarines into 1 cm thick wedges. Discard pits.
Prepare dressing. Whisk olive oil, white balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Set aside.
Toast pistachios in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes. Stir often. Let cool. Roughly chop.
Arrange arugula on a large serving platter or individual plates.
Artfully arrange nectarine slices over arugula.
Tear burrata into irregular pieces. Place evenly among nectarines.
Scatter chopped pistachios and fresh basil leaves over the salad.
Drizzle dressing evenly over the entire salad just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sardines with Beer-Chocolate Glaze and Grapefruit-Fennel Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown, crisp-skinned seared sardines are arranged naturally on the plate, their whole forms visible. A dark, glossy beer-chocolate glaze is subtly drizzled over the sardines. Beside them, a vibrant pile of thinly sliced fennel and ruby-red grapefruit segments provides fresh contrast. The fennel is cut into very thin slices, and grapefruit into neat segments. Bright green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the ingredients. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a cotton napkin and traditional flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish in a casual restaurant setting.
instructions: Rinse sardines. Pat them dry thoroughly. Season generously with salt and pepper.

In a small saucepan, combine beer and honey or maple syrup. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce liquid by half, about 8-10 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in chopped milk chocolate until melted and smooth. Season with a pinch of salt. Keep warm.

Segment grapefruits over a bowl to catch juice. Squeeze membranes to extract remaining juice. In a medium bowl, combine grapefruit segments, thinly sliced fennel, and very thinly sliced red onion. Add 30ml olive oil and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place sardines in a single layer, skin-side down. Sear for 2-3 minutes until skin is crisp and golden. Flip carefully. Cook for another 1-2 minutes until cooked through. Cook in batches if needed.

Divide grapefruit-fennel salad among four plates. Arrange 3-4 seared sardines per plate on top of or beside the salad. Drizzle beer-chocolate glaze over the sardines. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure sardines are very fresh for best flavor. The beer-chocolate glaze is intended to be savory, with the chocolate adding depth and richness, not sweetness. The grapefruit and fennel salad provides a crucial acidic and fresh counterpoint to the richness of the sardines and glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Nectarine & Chickpea Salad with Preserved Lemon Dressing
recipes.visual_description: The Nectarine & Chickpea Salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. Thin wedges of ripe nectarine are artfully scattered amidst vibrant baby spinach. Whole chickpeas and small diced cucumber cubes add textural contrast. Halved cherry tomatoes contribute deep red, complementing translucent, thinly sliced quick-pickled red onion. Freshly chopped mint and parsley leaves are integrated. The preserved lemon dressing lightly coats each component. The arrangement is organic, creating a harmonious mound with negative space, emphasizing a clean, minimalist aesthetic. The plating focuses on sustainable, ingredient-forward presentation. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed natural linen napkin, and soft, diffused natural lighting. A minimalist background hints at natural elements, maintaining focus on the fresh, wholesome dish.

ingredients.name: Nectarines
ingredients.quantity: 2 ripe, firm, sliced into thin wedges

ingredients.name: Chickpeas
ingredients.quantity: 1 x 400 g can, rinsed and drained

instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Red Onion: In a small heatproof bowl, combine 120 ml apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and 2 g salt. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Add thinly sliced red onion. Submerge completely. Let steep for at least 15 minutes while preparing other ingredients.

Make Preserved Lemon Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, finely minced preserved lemon rind (discard pulp), 15 ml apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, and Dijon mustard. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Assemble Salad: In a large mixing bowl, combine nectarine thin wedges, rinsed chickpeas, small diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, baby spinach, roughly chopped mint, and roughly chopped parsley.
Dress and Serve: Drain the quick-pickled red onion. Add the pickled onion to the salad. Pour the preserved lemon dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe promotes zero-waste by utilizing full ingredient potential and minimizing food scraps. Adjust sweetness of dressing to nectarine ripeness.

recipes.recipe_name: Confit Salmon, Horseradish Espuma, Beetroot Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Confit Salmon, Horseradish Espuma, and Beetroot Puree is presented on a round, matte white bone china plate. A vibrant, deep purple beetroot puree forms a graceful, organic swipe across the plate. A perfectly cooked, flaky salmon fillet, its skin lightly crisped, rests artfully on the puree. Adjacent to the salmon, a cloud of pristine white horseradish espuma is delicately piped, creating an ethereal contrast. A single, small sprig of fresh green dill is precisely placed atop the salmon, adding a pop of verdant color. The arrangement is minimalist and asymmetric, with abundant negative space. The plate sits on a polished light grey marble surface, accompanied by a crisply folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's textures and forms against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Wash beetroots. Wrap each beetroot in foil. Roast for 60-90 minutes until tender. Let cool slightly. Peel roasted beetroots. Dice into small cubes. Blend with butter and apple cider vinegar until smooth. Season with salt. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky puree. Keep warm.

For the horseradish espuma, finely grate fresh horseradish. Bring cream to a simmer in a small saucepan. Add grated horseradish. Steep for 15 minutes off heat. Strain cream through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract flavor. Discard solids. Season cream with salt and white pepper. Pour into a culinary siphon. Charge with one N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm in a bain-marie or warm water bath.

For the confit salmon, pat salmon fillets dry. Season generously with salt and white pepper. Place fillets in a small oven-safe dish. Pour olive oil over salmon to fully submerge. Ensure skin is submerged. Bake at 120°C for 20-25 minutes. Salmon internal temperature should reach 50°C. Carefully remove salmon from oil. Transfer to a wire rack to drain excess oil. Gently crisp the skin with a blowtorch or hot pan if desired.

To plate, create a sweeping arc of beetroot puree on one side of a large plate. Carefully place a confit salmon portion beside the puree. Pipe a generous dollop of horseradish espuma next to the salmon. Garnish with a small, delicate dill sprig on the salmon. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti with Crab, Garlic, Chili, and Lemon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spaghetti with Crab, Garlic, Chili, and Lemon is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table surface. The spaghetti is neatly coiled into a soft nest, showcasing its golden hue. Generous flakes of tender, white lump crab meat are distributed throughout the pasta and gently mounded on top, highlighting its delicate texture. Thinly sliced, lightly golden garlic pieces and vibrant red chili flakes are visibly interspersed, adding color and texture. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast, and a dusting of finely grated white Parmesan cheese melts into the warm pasta. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the pasta, ready to be squeezed. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, with moderate negative space. The table setting includes standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin placed to the left of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml of pasta cooking water before draining.

While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and chili flakes. Cook gently for 3-4 minutes until garlic is fragrant and lightly golden. Do not brown the garlic.
Add lump crab meat to the skillet. Gently warm through for 1-2 minutes. Do not break up the crab too much.
Add the drained spaghetti to the skillet with the crab mixture. Pour in 150ml of reserved pasta water. Add lemon juice, lemon zest, and half of the grated Parmesan cheese.
Toss vigorously to combine, allowing the sauce to emulsify. Add more pasta water, 30ml at a time, if needed to achieve a silky sauce consistency.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley. Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, topped with remaining grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Beef Short Ribs with White Bean Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Beef Short Ribs is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two generous, dark brown, fork-tender beef short rib chunks are nestled atop a smooth, creamy off-white mound of white bean puree. The beef boasts a rich, slightly glossy surface from the braising liquid. A deep amber-brown, glossy reduction of the braising sauce is artfully drizzled around the beef and puree. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green chives provides a contrasting color and fresh texture. The plate features moderate negative space, showcasing a professional yet approachable presentation. The setting includes a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and standard polished flatware, all under soft, natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Pat beef short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Dredge lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in dark beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Return short ribs to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Liquid should almost cover the ribs.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly and transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While beef braises, prepare white bean puree. In a saucepan, combine drained cannellini beans with 125 ml of the hot braising liquid (skimmed from the pot) and butter. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Mash beans roughly with a fork or use an immersion blender for a smoother puree. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Once beef is tender, remove ribs from the pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids and herbs.
Skim any excess fat from the braising liquid. Bring to a boil over high heat and reduce until it thickens to a glossy sauce consistency, about 10-15 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning of the sauce. Reheat short ribs gently in a little sauce if needed.
To plate, spoon a generous portion of white bean puree onto the center of each white porcelain plate. Place 1-2 pieces of braised short rib on top of the puree.
Drizzle the rich, reduced braising sauce around and over the short ribs. Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Zaatar Feta Baked Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Zaatar Feta Baked Chicken rests on a simple, round ceramic plate with a natural, rustic edge. Two whole, golden-brown boneless chicken thighs are arranged slightly overlapping, topped with generously melted and lightly golden feta cheese. Dark green zaatar flecks are visible on the chicken, and a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the top. The plate sits on a well-worn, light wooden dining table, evoking a cozy family kitchen. A small, rustic bowl of fluffy rice pilaf and a piece of warm pita bread are casually placed nearby. A simple, off-white cloth napkin lies beside the plate. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a comforting and appetizing atmosphere, with minimal background elements to focus on the hearty dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with rice pilaf and warm pita bread.
Often accompanied by a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with salt and black pepper.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise and zaatar. Mix well.
Spread the mayonnaise-zaatar mixture evenly over each chicken thigh.
Place chicken thighs in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove from oven. Crumble feta cheese evenly over the chicken.
Return to oven. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and feta is lightly golden.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Potato Bake with Garlic Cheese Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A generous square portion of the Hearty Beef and Potato Bake sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The top layer features a rich, golden-brown crust of melted Gruyère cheese, bubbling and slightly crisp. Below the crust, tender, thinly sliced potato rounds are visible, interspersed with succulent, dark brown beef chunks. A creamy, pale yellow garlic cheese sauce peeks through the layers, indicating a moist interior. The overall presentation is robust and comforting. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the corner of the bake, adding a touch of vibrant green. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, creating a casual bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth and 2 thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot and transfer to oven. Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Beef should shred easily. Remove beef, shred into smaller chunks. Discard thyme.
Increase oven temperature to 190°C.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes into 3 mm rounds. Use a mandoline if possible.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in milk and cream. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and 150 grams of grated Gruyère. Stir until cheese melts and sauce is smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Lightly grease a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Arrange a layer of potato slices in the dish. Top with a layer of shredded beef. Pour some cheese sauce over the beef.
Repeat layers: potato, beef, sauce, until all ingredients are used, ending with a potato layer.
Sprinkle remaining 50 grams of Gruyère over the top layer.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly. Insert a knife to check potato tenderness.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Tomato-Cashew Chicken with Coconut Rice
