recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Tomato-Cashew Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. Tender, pan-seared chicken breast, cut into large irregular chunks, is generously coated in a rich, vibrant reddish-orange sauce. The sauce, creamy and glossy, shimmers with hints of tomato and coconut, dotted with crushed cashews. Beside the chicken, a neat, fluffy mound of fragrant coconut rice glistens, its pure white contrasting with the sauce. Freshly chopped green spring onion and a few whole toasted cashews adorn the chicken, adding fresh color and textural crunch. A small lime wedge rests on the plate's edge. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light grey cotton napkin and simple polished silver flatware, bathed in soft, natural lighting, creating an inviting, professional presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with fresh lime wedges for a bright finish.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until clear. Combine rice and 250 ml coconut milk in a saucepan. Add 250 ml water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand 10 minutes, covered. Fluff with a fork.
Cut chicken breast into large irregular chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Finely chop onion, garlic, and ginger. Coarsely chop 50 g cashews. Keep remaining 50 g cashews whole for garnish.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the skillet. Add chopped onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened. Add chopped garlic and ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, sriracha hot sauce, brown sugar, soy sauce, and chopped cashews to the skillet. Stir well. Pour in remaining 150 ml coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the sauce. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer 10-12 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in fresh lime juice. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Thinly slice spring onion for garnish. Lightly toast whole cashews in a dry pan for garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Roasted Lamb Shoulder with Celery Root Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-roasted lamb shoulder is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A central, creamy mound of pale off-white celery root puree forms the base. Rustic, pull-apart chunks of golden-brown lamb, showcasing a tender, moist interior, are deliberately placed atop the puree. Beside the lamb, vibrant green roasted celery batons are neatly arranged, displaying a slight char and tender-crisp texture. A glossy, dark amber reduction sauce is artfully drizzled over the lamb and around the plate. A few fresh parsley leaves are scattered for a touch of bright green. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard modern flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a minimal, soft-focus background suggesting a casual bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat lamb shoulder dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb on all sides until deeply browned, about 5-7 minutes total. Remove lamb from pot.
Add whole garlic head (cut in half horizontally), minced garlic, rosemary, and thyme to the pot. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Return lamb to pot. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Roast for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until lamb is fork-tender.
While lamb roasts, prepare celery root puree: Peel celery root. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Place celery root in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 15-20 minutes until very tender.
Drain celery root well. Return to hot pan to dry briefly.
Add butter and milk to celery root. Mash or blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Cut celery stalks into 5 cm batons. Toss with remaining 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread celery batons on a baking sheet. Roast in oven during the last 20 minutes of lamb cooking, or separately at 180°C for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Remove lamb from oven. Transfer lamb to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Rest 15 minutes.
Skim excess fat from pan juices. Reduce pan juices over medium heat until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes.
To serve: Spoon celery root puree onto plates. Arrange chunks of lamb shoulder on top. Place roasted celery batons beside the lamb. Drizzle with pan reduction sauce. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Thyme Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked whole, is surrounded by a generous pool of creamy, earthy mushroom and thyme sauce. Sliced cremini mushrooms and finely diced onions are visible within the rich, off-white sauce. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting, refined casual dining presentation. The scene is uncluttered.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and fresh thyme leaves. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Heat through for 1-2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously coated with a rich, creamy mushroom sauce. The sauce features irregularly sliced, deeply browned cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots, creating a rustic yet refined texture. Bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and sauce, adding a fresh color contrast. The chicken breast shows a crisp exterior and a tender interior. A small pool of sauce surrounds the base of the chicken. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A single portion, balanced and appealing.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan.
Add sliced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add irregularly sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the pan. Turn to coat with sauce.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Lamb and Celery Stew
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, generous serving of Hearty Lamb and Celery Stew fills a deep, matte cream-colored ceramic bowl. Thick, fall-apart chunks of braised lamb are prominently featured, interspersed with large-diced carrots, potatoes, and tender celery pieces. All ingredients are enveloped in a glossy, dark brown, thick gravy. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh chopped flat-leaf parsley garnishes the top. The bowl rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table. Beside it, a simple, sturdy silver fork. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family dinner. The plating is natural and unpretentious, emphasizing comforting sustenance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Enjoy with a simple green salad on the side.

ingredients.name: Lamb shoulder or leg
ingredients.quantity: 800 g, cut into 4 cm thick chunks

instructions: Pat lamb chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove lamb and set aside.
Add chopped onion, celery, and carrots to the pot. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir constantly for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid is reduced by half.
Return lamb to the pot. Add beef or lamb broth, diced tomatoes, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours, or until lamb is nearly tender.
Add diced potatoes to the pot. Stir gently. Ensure potatoes are submerged. Add a little water if needed.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 25-30 minutes, or until lamb is very tender and potatoes are cooked through.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Browning the lamb thoroughly adds depth of flavor to the stew.
Adjust the thickness of the gravy by simmering longer or adding a cornstarch slurry if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken & Sundried Tomato Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken & Sundried Tomato Tagliatelle is presented in a clean, white, shallow porcelain bowl. The al dente tagliatelle is neatly coiled, forming a gentle mound. Thick, pan-seared chicken breast medallions, exhibiting a golden-brown crust, are arranged on top. The rich, reddish-orange sundried tomato sauce generously coats the pasta and chicken. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered for contrast and aroma. A light dusting of grated Parmigiano-Reggiano finishes the dish. Elements are arranged naturally, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, with a silver fork and knife beside the bowl. A folded white cotton napkin completes the casual bistro aesthetic. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
Enjoy with a glass of dry Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add shallot to the skillet. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce wine by half, about 2 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chopped sundried tomatoes, and chicken broth. Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Let sauce gently simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While sauce simmers, cook tagliatelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Slice seared chicken breasts into thick medallions. Return chicken medallions to the simmering sauce. Cook for 2-3 minutes to heat through.

Drain pasta, reserving 125ml of pasta water. Add drained tagliatelle directly to the sauce. Add butter, grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, and chopped fresh basil. Toss pasta with sauce until well coated. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired consistency.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish with additional fresh basil leaves and a sprinkle of Parmigiano-Reggiano.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust red pepper flakes to personal preference for spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Szechuan Noodle Bowl with Seared Calf Liver and Crispy Salt Cod
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Szechuan Noodle Bowl is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface. The base consists of golden-yellow Hokkien noodles, glossed with a rich, savory Szechuan sauce, with patches of melted, gooey taco cheese woven throughout, creating a comforting, inviting texture. Thick, pan-seared calf liver chunks, exhibiting a deep brown crust and tender interior, are arranged atop the noodles. Scattered over the dish are small, golden-brown pieces of crispy salt cod, adding a contrasting texture and salty counterpoint. Beside the liver, a vibrant dollop of diced star fruit salsa, showcasing its characteristic five-point star shape, provides a fresh, tart accent with hints of green and yellow. The dish is garnished generously with bright green sliced spring onions and fresh coriander leaves, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the centerpiece. A simple cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl, and the scene is lit with natural, even lighting, conveying a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Desalinate salt cod: Rinse cod under cold water. Submerge in a bowl of cold water. Refrigerate for 24-36 hours. Change water every 6-8 hours. Drain and pat dry.
Prepare star fruit salsa: Cut star fruit into small dice. In a small bowl, combine diced star fruit, 15ml raspberry vinegar, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Cook Hokkien noodles: Boil noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Toss with 5ml sesame oil to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Prepare noodle sauce: In a small bowl, combine Szechuan sauce, soy sauce, and remaining 10ml sesame oil. Mix well.

Cook salt cod: Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Flake desalinated cod into small pieces. Fry until golden brown and crispy. Remove and drain on paper towels. Set aside.

Cook calf liver: Season liver pieces with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml vegetable oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Sear liver for 2-3 minutes per side, until browned and cooked to desired doneness. Remove liver from pan and slice into thick chunks. Set aside.

Assemble noodles: Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the pan (add a little more oil if needed). Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add cooked Hokkien noodles and noodle sauce to the pan. Toss to coat evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes until heated through.

Plate the dish: Divide hot noodles among 4 serving bowls. Top each noodle portion with a generous amount of shredded taco cheese. The heat from the noodles will melt the cheese. Arrange seared calf liver chunks on top of the cheese and noodles.
Garnish: Sprinkle crispy salt cod over the liver and noodles. Spoon a portion of star fruit salsa beside the liver. Garnish with sliced spring onions and fresh coriander. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of slow-braised beef ragu is presented on an everyday, off-white ceramic pasta bowl, showcasing its rustic Italian charm. The rich, deep reddish-brown ragu, featuring tender, shredded beef chunks and finely diced carrots and celery, generously coats wide, golden pappardelle noodles. The pasta is naturally intertwined with the sauce, creating a hearty, flowing mound in the center of the bowl. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano adds a creamy white accent and subtle texture. A few small, fresh thyme leaves are casually scattered on top for a touch of green. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Alongside, a simple fork and spoon with classic design are placed on a casually folded beige linen napkin. The background shows a hint of a relaxed family kitchen atmosphere, with warm, cozy lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a robust Italian red wine.

ingredients.name: Beef chuck, cut into 4-5 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches if needed. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced carrots and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until wine is mostly reduced.
Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender and easily shredded.
Remove beef from the pot. Shred the beef using two forks. Discard herb sprigs and bay leaves.
Return shredded beef to the sauce. Stir well. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook pappardelle according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss with a generous amount of beef ragu.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: Four vibrant bell peppers, halved lengthwise, are baked until tender, holding their shape on a rustic ceramic baking dish. Each half is generously filled with a hearty, rustic mixture of cooked white rice and brown lentils, mixed with diced red onion, minced garlic, and diced mushrooms. The rich red of the crushed tomatoes and the fresh green of chopped basil, oregano, and parsley are visible within the filling. A golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted mozzarella cheese and crisp breadcrumbs tops each pepper. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, with an everyday ceramic plate. A casually folded cloth napkin and simple cutlery complete the homely, comforting scene. Natural, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the modest, satisfying portions, highlighting the dish's inviting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in any remaining sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced mushrooms. Cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in rinsed lentils and rice. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, until most liquid is absorbed and lentils/rice are partially cooked.
Stir in chopped basil, oregano, parsley, and grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the filling generously into each bell pepper half.
Top each filled pepper with shredded mozzarella and breadcrumbs.
Add 100 ml water to the bottom of the baking dish to prevent sticking.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until peppers are tender and cheese is golden and bubbly.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Macadamia-Crusted Chicken with Savory Peanut Butter Chocolate Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Macadamia-Crusted Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three thick, golden-brown chicken medallions, boasting a visibly crunchy macadamia crust, are artfully arranged slightly off-center. A rich, dark brown savory peanut butter chocolate sauce is generously spooned beside and partially over the chicken, creating a glossy pool. The sauce exhibits a smooth, thick texture. A vibrant sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives or cilantro provides a contrasting green pop on top of the chicken and sauce. The composition emphasizes natural shapes and moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and subtle, even natural lighting. The overall presentation is professional, approachable, and highlights the dish as the centerpiece.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. If breasts are very thick, slice each horizontally to create two thinner cutlets, or pound to even thickness.
Set up a dredging station: Place kamut flour on one plate, beaten egg on a second, and crushed macadamia nuts on a third.
Dredge each chicken piece in kamut flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Press firmly into crushed macadamia nuts to coat completely.

Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Sear crusted chicken for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Keep warm.
For the sauce: In the same skillet, add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in chicken broth, peanut butter, soy sauce, and rice vinegar. Bring to a simmer, whisking until smooth.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in chopped milk chocolate until melted and sauce is smooth. Stir in kewra water.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. Sauce should be savory with subtle sweetness and floral notes.
To serve, slice each chicken breast into thick medallions. Arrange on plates. Spoon generous amounts of sauce over and around the chicken. Garnish with fresh cilantro or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet aux Champignons et Oignons Perlés
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Poulet aux Champignons et Oignons Perlés is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface. Golden-brown seared chicken thighs, presented as whole pieces, are nestled in a rich, glossy brown sauce. Earthy brown sautéed mushroom quarters and tender, caramelized pearl onions are generously distributed around the chicken. A sprinkle of vibrant fresh chopped parsley provides a pop of green against the savory hues. The composition is balanced, allowing for moderate negative space around the central dish. Traditional French flatware is neatly placed beside the plate. A cotton napkin and a subtle restaurant-style background enhance the casual yet refined bistro atmosphere under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with simple steamed potatoes or roasted small potatoes.
Accompany with a light green salad with a vinaigrette dressing.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, cook lardons over medium heat until crispy. Remove lardons with a slotted spoon; set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.

Add olive oil to the pot if needed. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot fat for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 3-5 minutes. Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Add pearl onions to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until lightly caramelized. Add quartered mushrooms; cook for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer; cook for 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid. Cover the pot.
Simmer gently for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken and thyme sprigs. Stir in butter until melted and sauce is slightly thickened. Return cooked lardons to the sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef with Fermented Tomato-Onion Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of tender, dark brown, irregular chunks of slow-cooked beef is centered on a round, matte, off-white ceramic plate. Large, rustic chunks of roasted root vegetables (carrots, parsnips) are naturally arranged around the beef, showcasing their caramelized edges. A vibrant, rustic dollop of reddish-orange fermented tomato-onion relish sits beside the beef. A rich, glossy braising liquid pools subtly at the base. Ample negative space emphasizes the natural beauty and textures. A few fresh parsley leaves are scattered sparingly. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, beside an undyed linen napkin. The background is clean, minimalist, with a soft-focus hint of green foliage. Soft, natural diffused lighting highlights textures. The scene conveys an eco-conscious, serene, and organic aesthetic.
instructions: Dice the large onion and 2 garlic cloves finely. Chop tomatoes into small pieces.
Combine chopped tomatoes, diced onion, and garlic in a clean jar. Add 15g salt. Mix well.
Press down to submerge vegetables in their own liquid. Cover jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until tangy. Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat beef chuck dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef.
Add 2 medium onions (roughly chopped) and 4 garlic cloves (smashed) to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Reduce by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Ensure beef is mostly submerged.
Bring to a simmer. Cover tightly.
Transfer to preheated oven. Cook for 2.5-3 hours, until beef is fork-tender.
Add root vegetables (large chunks) to the pot during the last 45-60 minutes of cooking. Cook until tender.
Remove beef, thyme, and bay leaf. Skim fat from braising liquid. Reduce liquid slightly if desired. Season to taste.
Shred or cut beef into large chunks.
notes: Source local, seasonal ingredients when possible.
Use vegetable scraps to make homemade beef stock for a zero-waste approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Tom Kha Gai (Thai Coconut Chicken Soup)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Tom Kha Gai is presented in a deep, glossy white ceramic bowl, resting on a simple light wooden table. The creamy, off-white coconut milk broth fills the bowl, with tender, irregularly cut 2cm chicken chunks and delicate, wavy oyster mushroom slices visible beneath the surface. Bright green chopped cilantro leaves are generously scattered over the top, providing a fresh contrast. A few thin, bright red slices of bird's eye chili are artfully placed among the cilantro, hinting at a subtle heat. The soup's surface has a subtle sheen from the coconut milk. A traditional ceramic Asian soup spoon rests inside the bowl, invitingly. Beside the bowl, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks lies neatly on a white cotton napkin. A small, matching white ceramic bowl filled with fluffy, white jasmine rice sits nearby, ready to accompany the soup. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, with natural, even lighting casting soft shadows, highlighting the dish as the focal point. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a relaxed dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small dish of fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies on the side for those who prefer more heat.
Enjoy with a traditional ceramic soup spoon and chopsticks.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2cm cubes.
Thinly slice galangal. Bruise lemongrass stalks and cut into 5cm pieces. Tear kaffir lime leaves.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add sliced galangal, bruised lemongrass, and torn kaffir lime leaves. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add chicken cubes. Cook for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Stir in coconut milk. Bring soup to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.
Add oyster mushrooms, torn or sliced. Cook for 2-3 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Remove from heat. Stir in fish sauce and lime juice. Add palm sugar if desired, dissolving completely.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more fish sauce or lime juice if needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and thin slices of red chilies.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Do not vigorously boil coconut milk after adding it, as it can cause it to separate. Maintain a gentle simmer.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage and Broccoli Risotto with Crispy Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of creamy Italian sausage and broccoli risotto is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. The risotto is fluid and glossy, displaying a warm, pale green hue from the integrated broccoli, with visible flecks of golden-brown crumbled sausage and vibrant green broccoli florets. Scattered artfully over the risotto are golden-brown, crispy 1.5 cm potato cubes, some adorned with small flecks of fresh rosemary. A light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese adds a subtle white shimmer. A few small, whole fresh basil leaves are strategically placed on top for a pop of contrasting color. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded dark grey cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Silver cutlery (fork and spoon) lies to the right. The background is a softly blurred, warm restaurant setting, illuminated by natural, even light from the top-right, creating a clean, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with crusty Italian bread to sop up the creamy risotto.
instructions: Prepare ingredients. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Cut broccoli into small florets. Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Remove sausage from casings. Crumble sausage meat.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add crumbled sausage. Cook until browned and cooked through. Break up meat with a spoon. Remove sausage from pan. Set aside.

Add 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add diced potatoes. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and tender, about 10-12 minutes. Add chopped fresh rosemary during the last 2 minutes of cooking. Season with a pinch of salt. Remove potatoes. Set aside.
In a separate saucepan, heat chicken stock until simmering. Keep warm over low heat.

In the large pan (used for sausage and potatoes), add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 20 g butter. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice grains.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.

Add one ladle of warm chicken stock to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly until each addition is absorbed before adding the next.
After about 10 minutes of adding stock, add broccoli florets to the risotto. Continue adding stock and stirring.
Cook risotto until rice is al dente, tender with a slight bite, about 18-20 minutes total. The risotto should be creamy and fluid, not dry.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in cooked sausage, remaining 30 g butter, and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir well to combine.
Let risotto rest for 2 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Pollo en Mole Poblano is presented on a clean, round, white porcelain dinner plate. A large, dark-skinned chicken thigh, deeply caramelized from searing, rests prominently on a pool of rich, glossy mole sauce. The mole, a deep, complex reddish-brown, exhibits a smooth, thick consistency, clinging to the chicken. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh cilantro leaves provides a vibrant color contrast against the dark sauce, along with a sprinkle of pale, toasted sesame seeds for texture. The chicken piece is whole, showcasing its succulent, tender appearance. The plate sits on a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. A small, white ceramic bowl of fluffy white rice and a stack of warm, soft corn tortillas are positioned nearby, along with a traditional Mexican talavera-style water glass. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the sauce's sheen and the chicken's inviting texture, creating an authentic and approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the mole sauce.
Accompany with a side of traditional Mexican rice.
Offer a small bowl of pickled red onions or jalapeños for a tangy counterpoint.
Serve with a refreshing Agua Fresca or Horchata.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt.
Sear chicken skin-side down in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cook until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear other side briefly. Remove chicken, set aside.

Carefully remove stems and seeds from dried chiles. Toast chiles in the dry pot for 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Do not burn. Place chiles in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let rehydrate for 20 minutes.
In the same pot, add a little oil. Sauté chopped tomatoes, onion, and garlic until softened and lightly browned.

Drain rehydrated chiles. Add chiles, sautéed vegetables, almonds, raisins, half of the sesame seeds, tortilla piece, cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, and cumin seeds to a blender. Add 200 ml chicken broth.
Blend until very smooth. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Press solids to extract liquid. Discard solids.

Heat 15 ml lard or oil in the pot over medium heat. Add strained mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 10-15 minutes. The paste will thicken and darken. This step is crucial for flavor development.
Gradually whisk in remaining chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add chopped dark chocolate and sugar. Stir until chocolate is fully melted and incorporated. Season with salt to taste.

Return seared chicken thighs to the mole sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Serve chicken with mole sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro and remaining toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The mole paste requires patient cooking to develop its deep flavor and color.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Italian Sausage and Tomato Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rigatoni with Italian Sausage and Tomato Ragu is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl. Al dente rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rustic, rich red tomato ragu. Irregular chunks of browned Italian sausage are interspersed throughout the sauce, visible alongside diced onion and hints of fresh basil. A generous scattering of freshly grated Parmesan cheese tops the dish, with several vibrant green basil leaves, some torn, placed artfully on top. The colors are warm: deep red, golden-brown, and fresh green. The texture appears hearty and comforting. The bowl is centered on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are neatly arranged beside the bowl. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the inviting warmth of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the ragu.
Offer extra grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano cheese at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Break into irregular chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add sausage chunks. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage and set aside, leaving fat in pan.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
If using wine, add to pan. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Return cooked sausage to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for at least 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 125ml pasta water.
Add cooked rigatoni directly to the sauce. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Toss pasta with sauce until well coated. Stir in half of the fresh basil, torn.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For best flavor, simmer the sauce longer if time allows, up to 1 hour.
Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes to control spice level.
traditional_techniques: Manteca (tossing pasta directly in sauce with cheese to emulsify)

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pineapple & Peach Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is arranged on handcrafted ceramic plates in earth tones. Diced fermented pineapple cubes and thin slices of fermented peaches are artfully scattered over a bed of vibrant mixed seasonal greens. The composition is minimalistic, emphasizing natural forms and colors. A light, glistening drizzle of the honey-ginger dressing coats the ingredients. Toasted pumpkin seeds are sparsely sprinkled, adding a contrasting texture and earthy hue. The natural golden, peachy, and green tones are celebrated. The plate rests on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, highlighting its natural texture. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed beside the plate. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring soft, natural lighting from a window, with a hint of a green plant visible, suggesting an eco-conscious environment. An individual portion is presented, with all diverse ingredients clearly visible and artfully distributed, showing proper knife work on the diced pineapple and sliced peaches. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space.
instructions: Ensure pineapple is diced into 1.5 cm cubes.
Ensure peaches are sliced into 0.5 cm thick crescents.
Toast pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Set aside to cool.
Prepare dressing: Whisk honey, grated ginger, lime juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper in a small bowl until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine fermented pineapple, fermented peaches, and mixed greens.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Divide salad among four plates.
Garnish each plate with toasted pumpkin seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe highlights sustainable practices by utilizing fermented fruits for enhanced flavor and preservation. Embrace seasonal greens for a fresh, local touch. Consider using 'ugly' or imperfect produce to reduce food waste. Compost any remaining fruit scraps.

recipes.recipe_name: Poblanos Rellenos de Papa y Elote Picante
recipes.visual_description: A single, robustly stuffed poblano pepper rests centrally on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The roasted poblano exhibits a deep, slightly charred green skin, revealing a generous, golden-yellow filling of mashed potato and corn, studded with melted, bubbly Oaxaca cheese. Specks of fresh green cilantro are visible within the filling and as a garnish. A small, neat dollop of bright white Crema Mexicana sits beside the pepper, with a contrasting vibrant red salsa roja pooling nearby. The pepper is presented whole, showcasing its natural shape. The background features a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin positioned neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, creating a clean, inviting restaurant-style presentation that honors its Mexican heritage.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Accompany with a side of traditional Mexican red rice.
Offer black beans as an additional side dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with foil.
Place poblano peppers on the baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Turn occasionally. Peppers should be softened and lightly charred.
Transfer roasted peppers to a bowl. Cover tightly with plastic wrap. Let steam for 10 minutes. This loosens the skin.
Peel skin from peppers. Make a lengthwise slit on one side of each pepper. Carefully remove seeds and membranes. Leave stems intact.
While peppers roast, peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well.
Mash potatoes until smooth. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and corn kernels to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes. Corn should be slightly tender.
Stir in mashed potatoes, shredded Oaxaca cheese, cayenne pepper, vegetable broth, chopped cilantro, and juice from half a lime. Mix well. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Carefully fill each poblano pepper with the potato and corn mixture. Do not overstuff.
Place stuffed peppers back on the baking sheet. Bake for 15-20 minutes. Cheese should be melted and bubbly, peppers heated through.
Serve immediately. Garnish each pepper with a dollop of Crema Mexicana and a spoonful of salsa roja.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun Chicken Jambalaya
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of vibrant Cajun Chicken Jambalaya is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish is a mosaic of rich, earthy colors: tender, browned chicken chunks, deep red bell pepper cubes, translucent onion pieces, and golden-brown sausage slices, all intertwined with fluffy, saffron-tinted rice. Rice grains are separate yet moist, flecked with green parsley. Chicken pieces show a slight sear. A sprinkle of fresh chopped green parsley provides a bright counterpoint. The jambalaya is mounded naturally, creating a comforting, inviting appearance. The bowl rests on a rustic wooden table. A simple white cotton napkin is beside it. A small glass ramekin holds red hot sauce. Lighting is natural and even. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cornbread
Offer hot sauce on the side
Enjoy as a communal one-pot meal
instructions: Dice chicken into 2.5cm cubes. Dice bell peppers, onion, and sausage into 1.5cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken. Cook until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add sausage to pot. Cook until browned. Remove sausage from pot.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, Cajun seasoning, smoked paprika, and thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes (undrained), chicken broth, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in rice. Return cooked chicken and sausage to pot.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 20-25 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes, covered.
Fluff with a fork. Remove bay leaf.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Adjust spice level of Cajun seasoning to personal preference.
traditional_techniques: Building the aromatic base (Holy Trinity influence)
Browning meat for depth of flavor

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Pickled Mushrooms and Ancient Grain Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented with a clean, minimalistic aesthetic on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface, emphasizing natural elements. A single portion of ancient grain pilaf, a harmonious blend of brown rice and quinoa, forms a natural, slightly mounded base, showcasing its varied textures and light brown hues. Beside it, a perfectly pan-seared salmon fillet, skin-side up, exhibits a rich golden-brown crispness contrasting with its tender, flaky flesh. Its natural shape is preserved; no slicing or fanning. Around the main components, artfully arranged clusters of sautéed mushrooms, showcasing their earthy tones and varied shapes, intermingle with vibrant, translucent pickled mushroom slices, adding a touch of bright acidity and visual pop. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green dill provides a subtle accent of color and freshness. The composition embraces negative space, allowing each ingredient to stand out. The lighting is soft, natural, and diffused, highlighting the food's inherent textures and colors. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed, along with a minimalist, unadorned fork and knife, reinforcing the eco-conscious, sustainable theme.
instructions: Prepare Pickled Mushrooms: In a small saucepan, combine 125ml water, 125ml apple cider vinegar, 1 tsp sea salt, 1 tsp sugar, optional bay leaf, and optional peppercorns. Bring to a simmer until salt and sugar dissolve. Remove from heat. Place 100g thinly sliced mushrooms in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over mushrooms. Ensure mushrooms are submerged. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving. Drain before plating.

Cook Ancient Grain Pilaf: Rinse brown rice and quinoa separately. In a medium pot, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add brown rice and quinoa, stir to coat. Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-35 minutes, or until grains are tender and liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.

Sauté Mushrooms: While pilaf cooks, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add remaining 200g sliced mushrooms (and any finely chopped mushroom stems). Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 7-10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook Salmon: Pat salmon fillets dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat a separate large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add a splash of olive oil. Place salmon fillets skin-side down. Cook for 5-7 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Flip and cook for another 3-5 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Squeeze fresh lemon juice over salmon.

Assemble and Serve: Divide ancient grain pilaf among four plates. Place a pan-seared salmon fillet next to the pilaf. Arrange sautéed mushrooms and drained pickled mushrooms around the salmon and pilaf. Garnish with chopped fresh dill and a thin lemon slice.
notes: Use mushroom stems and vegetable scraps to make homemade broth for zero-waste cooking.
Adjust cooking time for salmon based on thickness and desired doneness. Ensure internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Ham, Mushroom and Spinach Tart with Cherry-Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: A slice of golden-brown savory tart, approximately 1/4 of a 24cm round tart, showcases a rich, creamy filling of diced smoked ham, sautéed sliced mushrooms, and wilted roughly chopped spinach. The flaky pastry crust is visibly browned. The filling appears set but moist. Beside the tart, a small, vibrant mound of fresh salad featuring thinly sliced cucumber rounds and halved dark cherries, lightly dressed. The dish is presented on a clean white round porcelain dinner plate. A silver fork and knife are placed beside the plate on a simple wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a subtly blurred bistro-style background creating a casual yet refined atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry white wine, such as a Sauvignon Blanc or Chardonnay.
Offer a crusty baguette on the side for a complete French bistro experience.
instructions: Prepare the pastry: Combine flour, cubed cold butter, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Rub butter into flour until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Gradually add cold water, mixing until a dough forms. Do not overwork. Form into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Roll out the chilled pastry on a lightly floured surface. Line a 24cm tart tin with the pastry. Trim edges. Prick the base with a fork. Line with baking paper and fill with baking beans or rice. Blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove paper and beans. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until lightly golden. Remove from oven and reduce temperature to 180°C (350°F).

Prepare the filling: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and moisture has evaporated. Add diced smoked ham and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in roughly chopped spinach until wilted. Remove from heat.
Prepare the custard: In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, double cream, milk, 1 tablespoon of Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper.

Assemble the tart: Spread the remaining 1 tablespoon of Dijon mustard evenly over the base of the blind-baked pastry crust. Spoon the sautéed ham, mushroom, and spinach mixture into the tart shell. Pour the egg custard evenly over the mixture. Sprinkle grated cheese over the top.
Bake the tart for 30-35 minutes, or until the custard is set and golden brown. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean. Let the tart cool slightly before slicing.

Prepare the Cherry-Cucumber Salad: In a medium bowl, combine thinly sliced cucumber and halved cherries. In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, white wine vinegar, 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard, optional honey, salt, and pepper to create the dressing. Pour the dressing over the cucumber and cherries. Toss gently to combine. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives.
Serve individual slices of the warm tart with a side of the fresh Cherry-Cucumber Salad.
notes: Ensure the pastry is well chilled before rolling to prevent shrinking.
Do not overbake the tart; it should be set but still have a slight jiggle in the center.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste in both the tart filling and the salad dressing.

recipes.recipe_name: Gratin de Haricots Blancs et Brocolis
recipes.visual_description: The Gratin de Haricots Blancs et Brocolis is presented in a rustic, oval ceramic gratin dish, showcasing a golden-brown, bubbling crust. The top layer, a mix of melted Gruyère cheese and lightly toasted breadcrumbs, is unevenly textured with darker caramelized spots. Beneath, the vibrant green broccoli florets emerge from a creamy, off-white white bean base. Some broccoli edges are slightly charred from baking, adding depth. The white beans are partially mashed, creating a rustic, comforting texture, with some whole beans visible. The dish is served on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple white ceramic plate. A folded linen napkin and a fork with classic French design are casually placed. Warm, soft light from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, highlighting the gratin's comforting appeal. The portion is modest, filling the plate invitingly.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty baguette slices for dipping.

ingredients.name: Canned white beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Steam or boil broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Drain well. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add drained white beans to the pan. Mash about half of the beans directly in the pan with a fork or potato masher to create a rustic paste. Stir to combine with onion and garlic. Discard thyme sprigs.
For the béchamel sauce: In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add flour. Whisk for 2 minutes to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Add bay leaf and nutmeg. Bring to a simmer, whisking constantly. Cook until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper. Remove bay leaf from sauce.
Pour béchamel sauce over the bean mixture in the pan. Stir well to combine. Gently fold in cooked broccoli florets.
Sprinkle grated Gruyère cheese and breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbling and golden brown. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Korean Tofu and Broccoli Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, common in Korean home kitchens. Golden-brown pan-fried tofu cubes and vibrant green broccoli florets are generously coated in a rich, savory, reddish-brown sauce. The broccoli retains its crisp-tender texture and bright color. The tofu has a slightly crispy exterior and soft interior. The sauce clings to the ingredients, showing a glossy sheen. The dish is casually mounded, creating a comforting, inviting appearance. It is garnished simply with thinly sliced green onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds on top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a separate bowl of fluffy white rice and a small dish of red kimchi, reflecting a typical Korean family meal. Everyday metal chopsticks rest beside the bowl. Warm, cozy light illuminates the scene from above, creating a natural, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Serve with various banchan (side dishes) like kimchi, pickled radishes, or seasoned spinach.
Eat with metal chopsticks and a spoon.
instructions: Press tofu for 20 minutes to remove excess water. Cut into 2-3 cm cubes.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
In a small bowl, combine doenjang, gochujang, soy sauce, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, and brown sugar. Mix well to form a paste.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes. Pan-fry until golden brown and slightly crispy on all sides. Remove tofu from the pan. Set aside.
Add the prepared bean paste mixture to the hot pan. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add water or vegetable broth to the pan. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
Return pan-fried tofu and blanched broccoli to the pan. Toss gently to coat with the sauce.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly and flavors to meld.
Remove from heat. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust gochujang amount for desired spice level.
Pressing tofu is crucial for texture and absorption of flavor.
traditional_techniques: Doenjang (fermented soybean paste) and Gochujang (chili paste) usage
Blanching vegetables for texture and color

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Belly with Pickled Onion and Peanut Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a handcrafted, natural cream ceramic plate. A base of vibrant, deep green blanched seasonal greens, such as bok choy leaves, is artfully arranged with natural flow. Upon this, two to three substantial 4 cm cubes of braised pork belly are placed. The pork belly features a golden-brown, slightly crisped exterior and rich, tender interior. A glossy, amber-toned peanut and fish sauce glaze generously coats the pork and pools gently. Thinly sliced, translucent ruby-red pickled red onions are scattered thoughtfully around the pork, providing a sharp color contrast. The plate maintains ample negative space, highlighting each ingredient's natural beauty. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain steamed rice or other simple grains.
instructions: Prepare Pickled Onions: Thinly slice red onions. Combine apple cider vinegar, sugar, 10g salt, and peppercorns in a small pot. Simmer until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over sliced red onions in a jar. Cool. Refrigerate 2 hours minimum.
Sear Pork Belly: Score pork belly skin. Season pork cubes with salt. Place skin-side down in a cold Dutch oven. Cook over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes. Render fat. Remove rendered fat.
Braise Pork Belly: Add white onion, crushed garlic, bay leaves, and sliced ginger to pot. Add 500ml water. Bring to simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Braise 1.5 hours, or until pork is very tender.
Prepare Peanut Glaze: Combine peanut butter, fish sauce, and minced garlic in a small saucepan. Whisk in 60ml braising liquid from pork. Simmer over low heat until glaze thickens slightly. Keep warm.
Finish Pork: Remove pork from braising liquid. Pat dry. Strain braising liquid for future use.
Blanch Greens: Quickly blanch seasonal greens in boiling water for 1-2 minutes. Drain.
Plate Dish: Place blanched greens on a plate. Arrange 2-3 pork belly cubes on top. Drizzle generously with peanut glaze. Garnish with pickled red onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Ham, Mushroom, and Spinach Tart with Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single generous wedge of a golden-brown smoked ham, mushroom, and spinach tart is neatly centered on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pastry crust is crisp and flaky, with visible layers. The rich, savory filling peeks from the cut edge, revealing diced smoked ham, tender sliced mushrooms, vibrant wilted spinach, and creamy yellow custard. The top crust features melted, lightly browned Gruyere cheese. Beside the tart, a compact mound of thinly sliced cucumber rounds, lightly dressed and sprinkled with fresh green dill, adds a refreshing contrast. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. Standard European flatware (fork and knife) is positioned beside the plate. A folded white cotton napkin rests nearby. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with balanced negative space.
instructions: Prepare the pastry: Combine flour, butter, and salt in a bowl. Rub butter into flour until crumbly. Add cold water gradually. Form dough, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 190°C. Roll out pastry on a floured surface. Line a 24cm tart tin. Trim edges. Prick base with a fork. Blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove baking beans/foil and bake for another 5 minutes until lightly golden. Set aside.
Prepare the filling: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced smoked ham and cook until lightly browned. Remove ham from pan and set aside.

Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until golden and moisture evaporates. Add diced onion and cook until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in fresh spinach. Cook until spinach wilts. Remove from heat.
Combine cooked ham, mushrooms, onion, and spinach. Spread mixture evenly into the pre-baked tart shell.
Prepare the custard: In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, double cream, milk, and Dijon mustard. Season with salt, black pepper, and nutmeg.
Pour custard over the filling in the tart shell. Sprinkle grated Gruyere cheese over the top.
Bake tart for 30-35 minutes, or until custard is set and top is golden brown. Let cool slightly before slicing.
Prepare cucumber salad: Thinly slice cucumber into rounds. In a bowl, whisk white wine vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Add cucumber slices and chopped fresh dill or parsley. Toss to combine.
notes: Allow the tart to cool for at least 15 minutes before slicing; this helps the custard set properly for clean cuts.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef and Vegetable Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of beef stew served in a wide, shallow ceramic bowl with slight glaze imperfections. The bowl sits on a dark, well-worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features four to five large, thick chunks of seared beef, appearing dark and tender. Surrounding the meat are thick rounds of carrots and large, irregular wedges of softened potatoes. A rich, glossy dark brown gravy coats all ingredients without submerging them completely. A light sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley provides the only color contrast. Beside the bowl lies a simple stainless steel spoon and a piece of crusty rustic bread. The lighting is warm and soft, suggesting a cozy kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette or rustic sourdough bread
Pair with a glass of dry red wine
Present in the center of the table in a large cast iron pot
instructions: Pat beef dry with paper towels.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks on all sides.
Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add onion to the same pot.
Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste.
Cook for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot.
Add carrots, potatoes, and thyme.
Pour in beef stock.
Bring liquid to a boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover with a lid.
Simmer for 90 minutes or until beef is tender.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure beef is patted dry to achieve a deep brown sear.
Do not boil the stew rapidly; a gentle simmer keeps the meat tender.
The stew tastes even better the next day after flavors meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Sautéed Mushrooms, Olives, and Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Orecchiette pasta is neatly mounded on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, sautéed mixed mushrooms, primarily sliced cremini and quartered shiitake, are interspersed throughout the pasta. Bright red halved cherry tomatoes and deep purple-black halved Kalamata olives provide vibrant color contrast. The dish has a light, glossy coating from olive oil and pan juices. A generous sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley covers the top, along with a dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese. The composition is natural and inviting, not overly structured. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Pair with a light-bodied Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio

ingredients.name: Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, grated

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook orecchiette pasta according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, prepare vegetables. Thinly slice garlic. Finely dice red onion. Slice mushrooms. Halve cherry tomatoes. Halve pitted Kalamata olives. Roughly chop parsley.
Heat olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add diced red onion and sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Increase heat to medium-high. Sauté mushrooms for 5-7 minutes until they release their liquid and brown. Stir occasionally.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce wine by half, about 2 minutes.
Add vegetable broth, halved cherry tomatoes, and halved olives to the pan. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Drain cooked pasta, reserving 100ml of pasta water. Add pasta directly to the sauté pan with the mushroom mixture.
Toss to combine. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if the sauce is too thick. Stir in half of the chopped parsley and half of the grated cheese.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Toss again.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh parsley and grated cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mushroom-Onion Ragout and Garlic Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, resting on a simple wooden table. A mound of creamy garlic smashed potatoes forms a soft base. A whole, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to perfection, is placed alongside the potatoes. A rich, earthy mushroom-onion ragout is spooned generously over the chicken and around the plate, showcasing tender, golden mushrooms and soft caramelized onions. Vibrant green blanched broccoli florets are neatly arranged, adding a pop of color and fresh texture. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley, enhancing its visual appeal. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and colors. A simple cotton napkin and standard cutlery are placed beside the plate, completing the modern bistro setting. The presentation is balanced, professional, and inviting, with appropriate negative space.
instructions: Prepare potatoes: Place potato chunks in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Return potatoes to the hot pot. Add 15g butter, half of the minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Roughly mash until creamy but still textured. Keep warm.

Prepare broccoli: Bring a medium pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch for 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender and bright green. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 6-8 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Make mushroom-onion ragout: In the same skillet, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and turn golden, about 7-10 minutes. Add remaining minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate the dish: Spoon a generous portion of garlic smashed potatoes onto the center of each white porcelain plate. Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast beside or slightly on top of the potatoes. Spoon a generous amount of mushroom-onion ragout over the chicken and around the plate. Arrange blanched broccoli florets neatly beside the chicken and potatoes. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Hake with Fermented Lotus Seed Puree and Kudzu-Framboise Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single seared hake fillet, skin golden-crisp, rests centered on a creamy off-white ceramic plate. Beneath the hake, a smooth, pale beige fermented lotus seed puree forms an organic mound. Alongside, blanched asparagus spears add a vibrant green contrast. A translucent, glossy kudzu-framboise glaze subtly drizzles over the hake, highlighting its delicate texture. The minimalist plating features ample white space, emphasizing the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. A few fresh dill sprigs provide a final touch of green. The dish sits on a light bamboo table surface, with an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, featuring a clean background with subtle green foliage, creating an eco-conscious ambiance. The hake is presented as a whole piece, unsliced.

ingredients.name: Fish bones/heads
ingredients.quantity: from hake or other white fish

instructions: Soak dried lotus seeds in water overnight. Drain.
Prepare a brine: Dissolve 5g sea salt in 250ml filtered water. Add 30ml apple cider vinegar.
Place soaked lotus seeds in a clean jar. Pour brine over seeds, ensuring full submersion.
Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until tangy. Taste daily.
Once fermented, drain seeds, reserving a small amount of brine.
Combine fish bones/heads and vegetable scraps in a pot. Add 1 litre cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Skim any foam. Simmer for 20-30 minutes. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Blend fermented lotus seeds with a splash of reserved brine and a little fish stock until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
In a small saucepan, combine 100ml fish stock with kudzu root starch. Whisk until dissolved.
Heat gently, whisking constantly, until mixture thickens to a clear, glossy glaze.
Remove from heat. Stir in white chocolate until melted and smooth. Add framboise eau de vie. Stir to combine. Keep warm.
Pat hake fillets dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place hake skin-side down. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip hake. Cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Blanch or quickly sauté seasonal greens until tender-crisp. Season lightly.
Spoon a generous dollop of lotus seed puree onto the center of each plate, creating a natural, organic shape.
Place a seared hake fillet on top of the puree.
Arrange a small portion of blanched greens next to the hake.
Spoon the kudzu-framboise glaze sparingly over the hake and around the plate.
Garnish with a few fresh dill sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Rosemary Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Apple & Rosemary Crumble is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl of a soft cream or beige hue, placed centrally on a light, textured bamboo table surface. The roasted apple wedges, with their naturally softened edges and a hint of caramelized warmth, form the base, their natural yellow-red tones peeking through. Above them, a rustic, golden-brown oat and almond flour crumble is loosely scattered, displaying varied textures from crispy clumps to finer crumbs. A glossy, amber-colored fermented apple-rosemary reduction is artfully drizzled over the crumble, catching the soft natural light. A single, small sprig of fresh green rosemary is delicately placed on top as a natural, understated garnish. The composition emphasizes natural forms and textures, with ample negative space around the bowl. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly placed to the side. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery, enhancing the eco-conscious and pure aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Maple Syrup
ingredients.quantity: 30 ml (for crumble) + 50 ml (for reduction) + 15 ml (for apples)

instructions: Prepare Apple Reduction Base: Peel and core apples. Reserve all peels and cores. Place peels, cores, and 1 sprig of rosemary in a small saucepan. Add 200 ml water. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Strain liquid, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Let liquid cool to room temperature.

Ferment Reduction: Stir 15 ml apple cider vinegar and 50 ml maple syrup into the cooled apple liquid. Pour into a clean glass jar. Cover with a breathable cloth and secure with a rubber band. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 2-3 days, or until slightly tangy and complex in flavor. Taste daily.
Prepare Apples for Roasting: Cut peeled and cored apples into thick wedges. Toss lightly with 15 ml maple syrup and a few rosemary leaves from the second sprig.
Prepare Crumble Topping: In a bowl, combine rolled oats, almond flour, and a pinch of sea salt. Pour in melted coconut oil and 30 ml maple syrup. Mix until a crumbly texture forms.
Roast Apples: Preheat oven to 180°C. Spread apple wedges in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until tender-crisp.
Bake Crumble: While apples roast, spread crumble topping on a separate small baking tray. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.

Assemble: Divide roasted apples among 4 individual serving bowls. Top with baked crumble. Drizzle generously with the fermented apple-rosemary reduction. Garnish each with a small fresh rosemary sprig. Serve warm.
notes: Adjust fermentation time for the apple reduction based on desired tanginess.
Use local, seasonal apples for best flavor and sustainability.
Apple peels and cores are typically food waste; using them for the reduction exemplifies zero-waste cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Red Wine Braised Lamb Stew
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Rustic Red Wine Braised Lamb Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a subtly uneven glaze. The stew features large, tender chunks of braised lamb, rich with a dark, glossy red-brown sauce. Visible pieces of soft, earthy brown cubed potatoes, bright orange diced carrots, and light green diced celery are nestled amongst the lamb. A few fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley leaves are scattered over the top, adding a fresh pop of color. The bowl rests on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table, showing subtle grain and imperfections. A simple, silver-colored fork with a classic design is placed casually beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy family kitchen, casting soft shadows. The overall presentation is homely and comforting, highlighting the hearty nature of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Enjoy with a glass of the same red wine used in the stew.
instructions: Trim excess fat from lamb. Cut lamb into 4-5 cm chunks.
Season lamb chunks generously with salt and black pepper. Toss with flour to coat evenly.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared lamb and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Return seared lamb to the pot. Add beef or lamb broth, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs. Ensure lamb is mostly submerged. If not, add more broth or water.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Peel and cut potatoes into 3-4 cm cubes.
Add cubed potatoes to the pot. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 30-45 minutes, or until lamb is very tender and potatoes are cooked through.
Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir into the stew just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Tomato Rice is presented in a shallow, wide ceramic bowl. A golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is nestled prominently on top of a vibrant orange-red bed of short-grain rice. The rice is tender, studded with soft, diced tomato pieces and flecks of minced garlic and onion. The grains are separate yet moist. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is generously scattered over the chicken and rice, providing a contrasting color and fresh aroma. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the rim of the bowl, ready to be squeezed. The overall composition is rustic yet refined, showcasing the rich colors and textures of the dish. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan if serving family style, or in individual wide, shallow bowls.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the flavorful juices.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
