Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and vibrant colors of the dish. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, creating a professional and inviting presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Often enjoyed as a hearty brunch or light dinner.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or pot over medium heat.
Add diced onions. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Stir well. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Season sauce with salt and black pepper to taste.
Create 8 small wells in the simmering tomato sauce. Carefully crack one egg into each well.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until egg whites are set and yolks are still runny.
While eggs bake, prepare crostini. Brush remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil on both sides of bread slices.
Toast bread in a separate pan or under a broiler until golden brown. Rub lightly with a raw garlic clove if desired.
Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese generously over toasted bread. Return to oven or broiler briefly until cheese melts and is bubbly.
Remove skillet from oven. Garnish baked eggs with torn fresh basil leaves.
Serve immediately with Parmesan crostini on the side. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Vegetable Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A refined, individual portion of Sustainable Chicken & Fermented Vegetable Bowl in a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. Fluffy brown rice forms the base. A beautifully seared chicken thigh, with crispy golden skin, is placed prominently. Roasted broccoli florets, caramelized onion wedges, and halved cremini mushrooms are artfully arranged around the chicken, showcasing natural colors and textures. A vibrant, quick-lacto-fermented carrot pickle, cut into thin rounds, adds a bright pop of orange and a distinct preserved element. The composition is minimalistic, with ample white space, emphasizing purity and natural beauty. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill. The bowl sits on a light, natural wood surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting organic textures. The background is clean and unobtrusive, with a hint of natural greenery, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a complete meal, highlighting the balance of protein, grains, and fermented elements.
Encourage mindful eating, appreciating each ingredient's contribution to a sustainable diet.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Carrot Pickle: Wash and thinly slice carrots into rounds or batons. Dissolve 10g non-chlorinated salt in 500ml water to make brine. Pack carrots tightly into a clean jar. Pour brine over carrots, ensuring they are fully submerged. Cover loosely or use an airlock. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove skillet from heat. Transfer chicken to a plate. Drain excess fat, reserving about 15ml in the pan.

Cook Rice: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine rice with 500ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Roast Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roughly chop broccoli into florets. Halve cremini mushrooms. Peel and cut onion into wedges. Peel and smash garlic cloves. Toss all vegetables with remaining olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.

Finish Chicken: Place chicken thighs skin-side up back into the skillet (or a new baking dish). Bake in the preheated oven with the vegetables for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.

Assemble Bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among 4 bowls. Place one chicken thigh on top of or next to the rice in each bowl. Arrange roasted vegetables around the chicken and rice. Add a generous portion of fermented carrot pickle to each bowl. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill.
notes: For zero-waste, chicken bones and vegetable scraps can be simmered with water to create a light broth for future use.
The fermented carrot pickle can be prepared days in advance, enhancing its probiotic benefits and flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken, Tomato & Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Rustic Chicken, Tomato & Rice Soup is presented in a sturdy, natural-colored ceramic bowl. The generous portion fills the bowl, showcasing tender, rustic 2-3 cm chicken chunks, soft, plump rice grains, and bright red diced tomatoes suspended in a rich, amber-hued broth. A scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley rests on the surface, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table, suggesting a homely family setting. A simple, folded off-white linen napkin is casually placed to the side, and a basic, sturdy metal spoon rests near the bowl. Warm, diffused light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere. The background is slightly blurred, showing subtle hints of a lived-in kitchen, maintaining focus on the comforting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Dice chicken into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chicken. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and chopped chili. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped tomatoes, chicken broth, and fresh thyme. Bring to a boil.
Add rinsed rice. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Return chicken to the pot. Continue to simmer for 10-15 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Rice should be tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This hearty soup is perfect for a comforting meal on a chilly evening.

recipes.recipe_name: Gâteau Renversé Poire-Figue au Miel et Thé Earl Grey
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of the Gâteau Renversé Poire-Figue is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, positioned slightly off-center to allow for negative space. The cake slice reveals a beautiful cross-section of moist, golden cake and a generous layer of glistening, deeply caramelized pears and figs. The pear slices are thinly cut, showcasing their natural curves, while the fig halves are rich and dark, their seeds slightly visible. The fruit layer possesses a deep amber hue from the honey and caramel, contrasting with the light, tender crumb of the Earl Grey-infused cake. A whole, inverted cake, still on its cake stand, sits slightly blurred in the background, hinting at its full glory. The setting is a modern bistro, with a light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the cake's textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of crème fraîche
Serve with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Grease a 20 cm round cake pan. Line bottom with parchment paper.
Melt 50 g butter and 100 g sugar in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until sugar dissolves and caramelizes to a golden amber.
Pour hot caramel into the prepared cake pan. Spread evenly.
Peel, core, quarter, and thinly slice pears. Halve figs lengthwise. Arrange sliced pears and halved figs decoratively over the caramel. Ensure fruit covers the base.
Brew strong Earl Grey tea. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream 100 g softened butter and 120 g sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Stir in vanilla extract.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with milk. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold the cooled Earl Grey tea into the batter.
Carefully spoon the cake batter over the fruit layer in the pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in pan for 10 minutes.
Invert cake onto a serving plate. Carefully remove pan and parchment paper.
While warm, gently brush the apricot liqueur over the fruit topping.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Pineapple Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A small pile of golden-brown pineapple fritters rests on a simple, everyday ceramic plate, showcasing their homemade nature. The fritters are irregularly shaped, some revealing glimpses of the pale yellow pineapple chunks or rings within their crispy, golden-brown whole wheat batter. They are generously dusted with fine white powdered sugar, creating a soft, inviting contrast. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture. A plain cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The background hints at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere, maintaining focus on the comforting, individual portion of 3-4 naturally stacked fritters.
instructions: If using canned pineapple, drain thoroughly. Pat pineapple pieces very dry with paper towels.
In a medium bowl, whisk whole wheat flour, baking powder, granulated sugar, and salt.
Gradually add milk to the dry ingredients. Whisk until a smooth, thick batter forms.
Heat vegetable oil in a small, deep pan to 175°C.
Dip each pineapple piece into the batter. Ensure it is fully coated.
Carefully place battered pineapple into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, turning once, until golden brown and cooked through.
Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Arrange fritters on a serving plate. Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.
notes: Ensure pineapple is very dry before coating in batter to prevent oil splattering and ensure crispy fritters.
Maintain oil temperature to ensure even cooking and browning without burning.

recipes.recipe_name: Earl Grey Poached Pear & Fig Honey Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of Earl Grey Poached Pear & Fig Honey Cake is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The cake slice, with its light golden crumb, stands upright, revealing its moist texture. The top of the slice is adorned with delicately fanned, pale yellow poached pear slices and vibrant deep purple fresh fig wedges, glistening under a thin, translucent amber glaze. The glaze gently drips down the sides of the cake slice, adding a refined sheen. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. In the soft-focused background, the remaining whole cake, lightly glazed and topped with more artfully arranged pear and fig, sits on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Earl Grey Tea (strong brew, cooled, for cake)
Earl Grey Tea (strong brew, cooled, for glaze)

instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
Peel, halve, and core pears. Set aside.
In a saucepan, combine 500 ml water, 100 g granulated sugar, and 2 Earl Grey tea bags. Bring to a simmer.
Add pear halves to simmering liquid. Poach gently for 15-20 minutes, until tender. Remove pears. Cool tea liquid. Reserve 30 ml for cake, 15 ml for glaze.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and 100 g granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in honey. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with milk and 30 ml Earl Grey tea. Mix until just combined.
Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Bake for 30-35 minutes, until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze: Whisk powdered sugar, apricot liqueur, and 15 ml Earl Grey tea until smooth.
Slice poached pear halves into thin slices. Cut fresh figs into wedges.
Pour glaze over cooled cake. Arrange poached pear slices and fresh fig wedges decoratively on top of the cake before the glaze sets.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tofu Soba Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Tofu Soba Bowl is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a warm cream tone. Buckwheat soba noodles form a neat, natural base. Firm, pan-seared or baked fermented tofu cubes, approximately 2 cm, are artfully placed on the noodles. A perfectly halved jammy egg, revealing its golden-orange yolk, rests beside the tofu. Thinly sliced, quick-pickled green onions are scattered across the dish, adding vibrant green color and a slight textural contrast. A light, savory dressing glistens over the components. The overall composition is clean and minimalistic, emphasizing the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a pair of simple wooden chopsticks and an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's fresh, wholesome appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in individual ceramic bowls.
Eat with chopsticks.
Offer a small side of chili oil for extra heat.
instructions: Press tofu: Wrap tofu block in a clean cloth. Place a heavy object on top. Press for 30 minutes to remove excess water.

Prepare fermented tofu: Cut pressed tofu into 2 cm cubes. Place cubes in a clean, airtight container. Cover with a brine made from 250 ml water and 10 g salt. Add 1 thinly sliced ginger piece and 1 crushed garlic clove. Seal container. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days. Refrigerate after 2-3 days. (See notes for quick marinade alternative).
Cook eggs: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for 6.5 minutes for jammy yolks. Immediately transfer eggs to an ice bath. Peel when cool.

Prepare quick-pickled green onions: Thinly slice white and light green parts of green onions into 2 cm pieces. Combine in a small bowl with 15 ml rice vinegar, 5 ml maple syrup, and a pinch of salt. Let sit for 15 minutes.

Cook soba noodles: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add soba noodles. Cook according to package directions, typically 4-5 minutes, until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 30 ml soy sauce, 15 ml rice vinegar, 10 ml toasted sesame oil, and chili flakes (if using).

Assemble bowls: Divide cooked soba noodles among 4 individual serving bowls. Arrange fermented tofu cubes on top of noodles. Halve peeled eggs lengthwise and place one half in each bowl. Scatter quick-pickled green onions over. Drizzle generously with prepared dressing. Serve immediately.
notes: For zero-waste, save any dark green parts of the green onions for making a flavorful green onion oil or broth base.

Quick marinade alternative: If not fermenting tofu, marinate pressed tofu cubes in 30 ml soy sauce, 15 ml rice vinegar, 5 ml sesame oil, grated ginger, and minced garlic for at least 30 minutes before pan-searing or baking.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pineapple & Black Bean Stew with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of dark, rich black bean stew is served in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a natural, earthy finish. Bright yellow, lacto-fermented pineapple chunks are visible within the stew, offering a vibrant contrast. Scattered artfully on top are substantial, caramelized chunks of roasted root vegetables—carrots, parsnips, and potatoes—displaying their natural, varied colors and slightly browned edges. A few fresh cilantro sprigs provide a minimalist, green accent. The overall composition is clean and ingredient-focused, emphasizing natural textures and colors. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the pure beauty of the sustainable ingredients in a clean, uncluttered setting.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium (peeled, cored, cut into 2 cm chunks)

ingredients.name: Carrots, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm chunks
Parsnips, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm chunks
Potatoes, scrubbed, cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Prepare Fermented Pineapple: Combine water and salt to create a brine. Dissolve salt completely. Place pineapple chunks (and optional chili/ginger) into a clean jar. Pour brine over pineapple, ensuring it is fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight to keep pineapple below the brine. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Store fermented pineapple in the refrigerator.

Prepare Black Beans: Soak dried black beans overnight. Drain and rinse. Place soaked beans in a large pot with 1.5 litres of vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until beans are tender. Drain beans, reserving cooking liquid.

Roast Root Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. In a large bowl, toss carrot, parsnip, and potato chunks with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread vegetables in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-35 minutes, stirring once, until tender and caramelized.

Prepare Stew Base: Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced red bell pepper; cook for another 5 minutes.

Build the Stew: Stir in tomato paste, smoked paprika, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Add cooked black beans and 500 ml of the reserved bean cooking liquid or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add Fermented Pineapple: Stir in the fermented pineapple chunks and 60 ml of its brine. Simmer the stew for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve: Ladle generous portions of the black bean and pineapple stew into individual bowls. Top each serving with a few roasted root vegetable chunks. Garnish with fresh cilantro or parsley.
notes: Zero-Waste Tip: Use pineapple peel and core to make homemade tepache or a fruit-infused broth base.
Zero-Waste Tip: Collect vegetable scraps (onion skins, carrot tops, bell pepper cores) to make a flavorful homemade vegetable broth.
Zero-Waste Tip: The aquafaba (cooking liquid from black beans) can be used in other recipes as an egg substitute or thickener.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Milanese with Saffron Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, classic round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous, fluid mound of golden-yellow saffron risotto occupies one side, its creamy texture visible, with finely diced onion. Beside it, a thick, golden-brown Chicken Milanese rests, its crispy, textured breading invitingly displayed. The chicken is a whole piece. A vibrant green sprinkle of fresh chopped Italian parsley garnishes both the risotto and the chicken. A bright yellow lemon wedge is placed alongside. The presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. Colors are natural: rich saffron yellow, golden chicken, fresh green parsley. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with standard silver flatware and a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors, with a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Offer freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table for additional seasoning.
instructions: Pound chicken breasts to 1.5 cm uniform thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow dishes. First with flour. Second with beaten eggs. Third with breadcrumbs mixed with 20g grated Parmesan.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shake off excess. Dip in egg, coating completely. Coat in breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, melt 30g butter and 30ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add a ladle of hot chicken broth. Stir until absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring frequently. Add saffron liquid with the second or third ladle of broth.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is al dente and creamy. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter and 60g grated Parmesan. Cover and let rest 2 minutes. This is 'mantecatura'.

While risotto rests, heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Cook 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Spoon saffron risotto onto plates. Place a cooked Chicken Milanese beside it. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.
notes: For best results, use high-quality Arborio rice and fresh saffron threads.
Ensure broth is hot when adding to risotto to maintain cooking temperature.
Do not overcook the risotto; it should be creamy with a slight bite.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Brioche & Pear Bread Pudding
recipes.visual_description: An elegant single slice of spiced brioche and pear bread pudding is centrally plated on a clean, round white porcelain dish. The pudding showcases a golden-brown, slightly crisp top crust, revealing a soft, custardy interior with distinct, tender brioche cubes and caramelized pear wedges. A vibrant green basil crème anglaise pools gracefully at the base of the slice, while a delicate, amber-hued honey-mustard drizzle artfully zigzags across the pudding's surface. A small, fresh basil sprig garnishes the plate, adding a pop of natural green. The setting is a modern bistro, with the dish resting on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a polished silver fork are placed neatly beside the plate. In the softly blurred background, a larger, whole bread pudding on a simple cake stand hints at more indulgence, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Cut brioche into 2.5 cm cubes. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake 10 minutes to lightly dry. Set aside.
Whisk eggs, milk, heavy cream, 100g granulated sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, and dry mustard powder in a large bowl until combined.
Add brioche cubes to custard mixture. Press gently to submerge. Let soak 20 minutes, turning once.
Peel and core pears. Cut into 1 cm thick wedges.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add brown sugar. Cook 1 minute until dissolved.
Add pear wedges. Cook 3-4 minutes per side until caramelized and tender-crisp. Remove from heat.
Layer half the soaked brioche in the prepared baking dish. Arrange caramelized pear wedges over brioche.
Top with remaining brioche. Pour any remaining custard over the top.
Bake 40-45 minutes, or until golden brown and set. A knife inserted near the center should come out clean.

While pudding bakes, prepare basil crème anglaise. Heat 100ml heavy cream in a saucepan until simmering. Remove from heat. Add 20g fresh basil leaves. Steep 15 minutes. Strain out basil leaves. Reheat infused cream.
Whisk 3 egg yolks with 50g granulated sugar until pale. Slowly temper hot cream into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon (80-85°C). Do not boil. Strain and chill.
Prepare honey-mustard drizzle. Whisk honey, Dijon mustard, and water in a small bowl until smooth.
Let bread pudding cool slightly before serving. Serve warm slices with basil crème anglaise and a drizzle of honey-mustard sauce. Garnish with a fresh basil sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Baked Buffalo Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Baked Buffalo Chicken Thighs is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic dinner plate, placed on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. Two substantial, golden-brown baked chicken thighs are nestled closely together, generously coated in a rich, creamy, reddish-orange sauce. Small specks of finely diced onion and dried oregano are visible within the sauce, which pools slightly around the chicken. The chicken exhibits a tender, moist texture with a slight crispness from baking. The plating is casual and natural, with components touching. A simple metal fork and knife rest beside the plate. A loosely folded, plain cloth napkin sits nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere with subtle background clutter that enhances the homely feel.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to skillet. Cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in hot sauce, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, dried oregano, and cayenne pepper. Mix well.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low.
Return chicken thighs to skillet, nestling them into the sauce.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast Stuffed with Bacon and Cheddar, with Creamy Potato Hash
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and plump, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is served whole, showcasing its inviting crust. Beside it, a generous portion of creamy potato hash with visible caramelized onion pieces and flecks of crispy bacon is artfully spooned. The hash has a soft, inviting texture with some slightly mashed potato chunks. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped chives garnishes both the chicken and the hash, adding a pop of color. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard polished flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich, warm colors.
instructions: Dice bacon into 1cm pieces. Cook in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 15ml bacon fat in skillet.
Dice one onion into small cubes. Mince garlic. Add diced onion to skillet with bacon fat. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Grate cheddar cheese. In a bowl, combine crispy bacon, sautéed onion, garlic, and grated cheddar. Mix well.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Using a sharp knife, cut a deep pocket into the thickest side of each chicken breast. Do not cut all the way through.
Spoon bacon-cheddar mixture into each chicken pocket. Close opening as much as possible.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Bake 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
While chicken bakes, prepare potato hash. Peel potatoes. Cut into 1.5cm cubes. Dice remaining onion into 1cm cubes.
Boil cubed potatoes in salted water until tender, about 10-12 minutes. Drain well.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a separate large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until caramelized and tender, about 8-10 minutes.

Add drained potatoes to skillet with caramelized onions. Gently mash some potatoes with a fork, leaving some chunks. Stir in heavy cream. Cook 2-3 minutes until heated through and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Finely chop fresh chives. Stir half into potato hash. Garnish finished dish with remaining chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Wok-Kissed Lentils with Fermented Black Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Wok-Kissed Lentils with Fermented Black Beans is presented in a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl, allowing ample negative space. The dish features dark, glistening green lentils combined with golden-brown, crispy tofu cubes and vibrant, tender-crisp green vegetable pieces, such as bok choy florets and gai lan stems, all coated in a rich, dark sauce infused with fermented black beans. Thin slices of bright green scallion tops are scattered over the top. The textures are varied: firm lentils, chewy tofu, and crisp-tender vegetables. The colors are earthy greens, browns, and dark umber from the sauce. The bowl is placed on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, alongside a small, plain white rice bowl filled with steamed brown rice and a pair of simple wooden chopsticks. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the ingredients' natural beauty. The background is clean and minimalist, with a subtle hint of green from a potted plant.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed brown rice as a staple.
Offer small bowls of pickled radish or cucumber on the side for freshness.
Accompany with hot Chinese tea, such as Pu-erh or Oolong.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.quantity: 4, white and green parts separated, sliced

ingredients.name: Seasonal green vegetables (e.g., bok choy, gai lan)
Vegetable stock (preferably homemade from vegetable scraps)

instructions: Rinse green lentils. Cook lentils in 750 ml water until tender but not mushy, about 20-25 minutes. Drain any excess liquid. Set aside.
Press firm tofu to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 2 cm cubes. Pan-fry tofu cubes in 1 tablespoon vegetable oil until golden brown and slightly crispy on all sides. Set aside.
Rinse fermented black beans. Roughly chop. In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and chopped fermented black beans. Set aside.
In another small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water to create a slurry. Set aside.
Heat a large wok or deep pan over high heat. Add 2 tablespoons vegetable oil. Add white parts of scallions, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced shiitake mushrooms to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add green vegetables to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until vibrant and slightly tender-crisp.
Add cooked lentils and pan-fried tofu to the wok. Pour in the vegetable stock and the soy sauce-black bean mixture. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry. Cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the ingredients, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in sesame oil and green parts of scallions. Serve immediately.
notes: To create a zero-waste vegetable stock, collect trimmings from carrots, celery, onions, mushroom stems, and other vegetable scraps. Simmer them in water for at least 30 minutes, then strain.
Fermented black beans (douchi) are a key ingredient for authentic flavor; they add a savory, umami depth.
Seasonal green vegetables can be swapped based on availability and local sourcing.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Garlic Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Garlic Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, pan-seared bone-in chicken thighs are arranged centrally, their skin crisp and glistening. A rich, glossy, light amber garlic sauce pools around the chicken, studded with tender, slightly translucent slices of garlic. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is generously scattered over the chicken and sauce, adding a burst of color. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the chicken, ready to be squeezed. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a small side of crusty artisan bread for dipping. Lighting is natural and even, creating a warm, inviting casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the garlic sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden and crisp, about 8-10 minutes.
Flip chicken. Cook for 5 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced garlic to skillet. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Do not brown.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of skillet. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock, bay leaf, and red pepper flakes. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to skillet. Cover. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in lemon juice and most of the fresh parsley.
Serve hot. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Chicken & Broccoli Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Garlic Chicken & Broccoli Bake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features tender, seared chicken cubes (2-3 cm) and vibrant green broccoli florets, generously coated in a rich, golden-baked American cheese sauce. The sauce appears bubbly and slightly caramelized on top, with visible hints of garlic and oregano. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s creamy texture and comforting appeal, with a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a simple green salad.
Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Cut broccoli into small florets. Blanch broccoli in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain well.
Melt butter in the same pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Whisk in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk. Bring to a simmer, stirring until thickened.
Reduce heat to low. Add American cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce is smooth.
Stir in dried oregano, salt, and pepper to taste.
Combine seared chicken and blanched broccoli in a 20x30 cm baking dish. Pour cheese sauce over chicken and broccoli.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and lightly golden.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: This dish is a comforting classic, perfect for a family meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Garlic Pasta with Seared Halloumi and Cucumber
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Garlic Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The linguine is lightly coated in a glossy, pale yellow lemon-garlic sauce. Golden-brown seared halloumi chunks are artfully placed atop the pasta. Vibrant green, thin cucumber ribbons are delicately draped over the dish, adding a fresh, crisp contrast. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes and thinly sliced purple red onion are interspersed throughout, providing pops of color and texture. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of finely chopped fresh dill and mint. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh ingredients and refined plating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
instructions: Cook pasta. Follow package directions. Cook until al dente. Drain. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Prepare cucumber. Use a vegetable peeler. Create long, thin ribbons. Set aside.
Cut halloumi. Slice into 1 cm thick pieces. Pat dry.
Sear halloumi. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add halloumi slices. Sear 2-3 minutes per side. Cook until golden brown. Remove from skillet.
Make sauce. Add remaining 45ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add lemon zest. Add lemon juice. Add red pepper flakes if using. Stir well.
Combine pasta. Add cooked pasta to the skillet. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water gradually. Stir until a light sauce forms.
Add vegetables. Add halved cherry tomatoes. Add thinly sliced red onion. Add pitted olives if using. Toss gently.
Finish dish. Fold in fresh dill. Fold in fresh mint. Season with salt and black pepper.
Plate and serve. Arrange pasta on plates. Top with seared halloumi. Drape cucumber ribbons over the dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Onion & Chard Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, its skin crisped to a deep golden-brown, rests on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. Beside it, a precisely cut rectangular portion of the gratin showcases layers of tender, thinly sliced potatoes, soft green chard, and melted, golden-brown cheese crust. A small, elegant smear of pale beige onion-herb mayonnaise is placed to the side, dotted with tiny green thyme flecks. A few translucent, thinly sliced quickly fermented onion rings are delicately placed on the gratin for subtle color contrast. The plate features ample negative space, highlighting natural textures and colors. The setting is minimalist: a light, natural wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in soft beige, and a simple background with soft, natural light. No ornate garnishes. The chicken is presented whole.
instructions: Thinly slice half the onion. Place in a small jar. Dissolve 5g salt and sugar in 100ml warm water, then add white wine vinegar. Pour over onions. Seal jar and let sit at room temperature for at least 4 hours.

Separate chard leaves from stems. Finely dice chard stems. Roughly chop chard leaves. Blanch chard leaves in boiling salted water for 1 minute. Immediately transfer to ice water. Drain well and squeeze out excess water.
Peel potatoes. Slice thinly, about 2-3mm thick.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a baking dish. Layer half the sliced potatoes, then half the blanched chard leaves, half the diced chard stems, and half the grated cheese. Repeat layers.
Mince remaining half onion and garlic. Sauté in a small pan with 15ml olive oil until softened. Add 200ml water and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer. Pour this liquid over the gratin layers.
Cover baking dish with foil. Bake for 40 minutes. Remove foil and bake for another 20-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to oven with the gratin. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Drain the quickly fermented onions (reserve a few slices for garnish). Finely mince the drained fermented onions. Mix with mayonnaise and picked thyme leaves. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.

Cut gratin into 4 portions. Plate one chicken thigh and one gratin portion. Add a dollop or smear of onion-herb mayo beside it. Garnish with reserved fermented onion slices or a tiny sprig of fresh thyme.
notes: Compost potato peelings and any unused chard trimmings.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Mustard Cream
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two pan-seared chicken breasts, each a golden-brown hue, resting slightly overlapping on a pristine white round plate. The chicken is whole, not sliced, showcasing its succulent texture. A rich, creamy, light orange-hued sauce, infused with mustard and a hint of red from the hot sauce, generously coats and pools around the chicken. The sauce has a smooth, glossy texture. A sprinkling of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley contrasts beautifully against the sauce and chicken. The plate is positioned on a rustic wooden table surface. A simple cotton napkin, folded neatly, lies beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting with subtle, warm tones.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits.
Reduce heat to low. Whisk in mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, hot sauce, cayenne pepper, and dried oregano.
Simmer sauce 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened. Do not boil.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F).
Adjust hot sauce to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Stone Fruit & Sourdough Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant portion centers on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate. A smooth, pale cashew cream forms the base, topped with a vibrant mound of deeply colored, glistening fermented stone fruit compote. The fruit chunks, approximately 2 cm, are soft and plump. A crisp, curved golden-brown sourdough discard tuile stands gracefully beside the fruit, offering textural contrast. Fine strands of bright yellow lemon zest are delicately scattered over the compote, adding a fresh visual accent. The scene is minimalist, set on a light reclaimed wood surface with an undyed linen napkin, bathed in soft, natural light from above, emphasizing the dish's organic beauty and natural colors.

ingredients.name: Ripe stone fruit (peaches, plums, or apricots)
Melted coconut oil or unsalted butter

instructions: Wash and pit stone fruit. Cut fruit into 2 cm chunks. Do not peel.
Combine fruit chunks with 50g raw sugar and 200ml filtered water in a clean glass jar.
Cover the jar loosely with a breathable cloth or coffee filter. Secure with a rubber band.
Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Taste daily for desired tanginess. Small bubbles indicate active fermentation.
Once desired tanginess is achieved, transfer fermented fruit and its liquid to a small saucepan.
Simmer gently over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit softens and liquid slightly thickens into a compote. Adjust sweetness with more sugar if desired.
Remove from heat. Cool completely. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
For the cashew cream, soak cashews in hot water for 30 minutes, or cold water for at least 4 hours. Drain thoroughly.
Blend soaked cashews with 120ml fresh water, maple syrup, vanilla extract, and a pinch of salt until completely smooth and creamy. Add more water, 15ml at a time, if needed for desired consistency.
Transfer cashew cream to a bowl. Chill for at least 1 hour.
For the sourdough discard tuiles, preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, combine sourdough discard, all-purpose flour, remaining 30g raw sugar, and melted coconut oil or butter. Mix until a smooth, thin batter forms.
Spoon small amounts of batter onto the prepared baking sheet. Use an offset spatula to spread into thin, even circles approximately 8 cm in diameter. Leave space between each.
Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the tuiles are crisp.
Immediately remove tuiles from the oven. Carefully drape each hot tuile over a rolling pin, bottle, or thin dowel to create a curved shape. Let cool completely to harden.
To assemble, spoon a generous dollop of chilled cashew cream onto the center of each plate.
Top the cashew cream with a portion of the fermented stone fruit compote.
Garnish each dessert with one curved sourdough discard tuile and a sprinkle of fresh lemon zest.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust fermentation time based on desired tanginess. Warmer temperatures will accelerate fermentation.
Leaving fruit peels on contributes to color, nutrients, and a rustic texture in the compote.
Cashew cream can be prepared up to 2 days in advance and stored in the refrigerator.
Sourdough discard tuiles can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Italian Sausage & Polenta Soup
recipes.visual_description: The soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its hearty, rich appearance. Large, irregularly shaped chunks of browned Italian sausage are prominent, interspersed with vibrant, wilted dark green spinach leaves and pale, quartered artichoke hearts. The creamy, golden polenta base is fluid, not stiff, with visible melted strands of smoked provolone cheese creating a comforting texture. A slight sheen of olive oil may be visible on the surface. The soup is garnished with a scattering of freshly torn green basil leaves, adding a pop of fresh color and aromatic contrast. The overall composition is inviting and robust, with a balanced distribution of ingredients. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard European flatware, under even natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thick slices of crusty Italian bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Canned artichoke hearts, drained and quartered
Fresh basil or parsley, for garnish

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add Italian sausage. Break it apart into large chunks. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Gradually whisk in the quick-cooking polenta. Stir continuously to prevent lumps. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until polenta thickens to a creamy consistency.
Stir in fresh spinach until it wilts, about 2-3 minutes.
Add quartered artichoke hearts and cubed smoked provolone cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and well combined.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh basil or parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure sausage is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beer & Beef Chili
recipes.visual_description: A hearty bowl of rich, dark red-brown chili fills a simple, deep ceramic bowl, showcasing a generous single portion. Crumbled ground beef, visible kidney beans, and diced tomatoes are simmered together, creating a thick, comforting texture. Bright green peas are scattered throughout, adding pops of vibrant color against the deep chili base. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green cilantro and a melting layer of shredded cheddar cheese sit atop the chili. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a robust metal spoon and a casually draped cloth napkin. Warm, inviting kitchen light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the homely, satisfying nature of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with cornbread or tortilla chips
Offer additional toppings like sour cream or extra hot sauce

ingredients.name: Canned kidney beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, chili powder, ground cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer. Scrape bottom of pot to loosen any browned bits.
Add diced tomatoes, kidney beans, beef broth, and hot sauce. Stir well.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in frozen green peas. Cook for an additional 5 minutes, or until peas are heated through and chili has thickened.
Season chili with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish with chopped cilantro and shredded cheddar cheese if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pineapple Oat Crumble with Rum-Lemon Foam
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of this sustainable dessert is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a natural, earthy tone (light beige or off-white). At the base, perfectly cubed, pale yellow fermented pineapple pieces are arranged organically, allowing for natural negative space. A light scattering of golden-brown oat crumble rests atop the pineapple, providing textural contrast. A delicate, cloud-like dollop of bright white rum-lemon foam is gently placed off-center, showcasing its airy texture. A few small, deep crimson streaks of cherry reduction are artfully drizzled over the foam and around the pineapple, adding a touch of vibrant color. Garnish is minimal: a single, small, vibrant green mint leaf or a delicate edible flower petal is placed beside the foam, offering a fresh accent. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful composition and ample negative space. The bowl is set on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood or bamboo surface. An undyed, loosely folded linen napkin in a natural beige tone is placed casually beside the bowl. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the textures of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, with a subtle hint of green foliage from a houseplant, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Peel pineapple. Reserve peel and core for other zero-waste uses.
Cut pineapple flesh into 2 cm cubes.
Combine 500 ml water, 30 ml maple syrup, and salt in a clean jar. Stir to dissolve.
Add pineapple cubes to the jar. Ensure pineapple is submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Cover with an airlock lid or cloth. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Taste daily for desired tanginess. Refrigerate when ready.
Preheat oven to 170°C.
Combine rolled oats, flour, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in 30 ml maple syrup.
Spread oat mixture on a baking sheet. Bake 15-20 minutes, until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
Pit cherries. Combine pitted cherries, 30 ml water, and optional 10 ml maple syrup in a small saucepan.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes. Mash cherries slightly. Reduce until slightly thickened. Set aside.
In a clean bowl, whisk egg whites to soft peaks.
Gradually add 15 ml maple syrup, whisking until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Gently fold in lemon juice and rum.
To assemble, place fermented pineapple cubes in each serving bowl.
Spoon oat crumble over pineapple. Dollop rum-lemon foam on top.
Drizzle with cherry reduction. Serve immediately.
notes: The pineapple peel and core can be used to make a fermented pineapple vinegar or infused water, contributing to a zero-waste kitchen.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Polenta with Italian Sausage, Spinach, and Smoked Provolone
recipes.visual_description: Creamy, golden polenta forms a soft bed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rustic ragù of browned Italian sausage chunks, wilted dark green spinach, and small diced crimson soppressata is spooned generously over the polenta. The sauce is glossy from crushed tomatoes. Melted, slightly stretched smoked provolone cheese strands are visible throughout and on top. A sprinkle of fresh green basil leaves adds vibrant garnish. The dish showcases warm golden yellow, deep reds, and dark greens. It is set on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and traditional flatware, under natural, even lighting, depicting a single, refined casual dining portion. The background is minimal, highlighting the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table
instructions: Prepare polenta: Bring stock to a simmer in a large pot. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes until creamy and thick. Stir in butter, Parmesan, salt, and pepper. Cover and keep warm.
Prepare ragù: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add crumbled Italian sausage. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon; set aside.
Add diced soppressata to the same skillet. Cook until crispy. Remove soppressata; set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Return cooked sausage to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Stir in fresh spinach until wilted. Remove from heat. Gently fold in shredded smoked provolone until melted and combined.
To serve, spoon creamy polenta onto individual plates. Top generously with the Italian sausage and spinach ragù. Garnish with torn fresh basil leaves and the crispy soppressata.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Oat Panna Cotta with Spiced Pineapple and Cherry Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Oat Panna Cotta is elegantly presented on a natural, unglazed cream-colored ceramic plate. The panna cotta, a soft off-white hue, is unmolded into a smooth, slightly wobbly dome, showcasing its delicate texture. Beside it, a small cluster of golden-brown, caramelized pineapple cubes, approximately 1.5 cm diced, are arranged naturally, their edges glistening from the rum and butter. A vibrant, deep ruby-red cherry compote, with visible pieces of pitted cherries, is artfully spooned alongside the panna cotta, creating a striking color contrast. A small, delicate curl of fresh lemon zest or a tiny sprig of edible herb (like lemon balm) rests gently on the panna cotta, adding a touch of fresh green. The plate is clean and uncluttered, with ample negative space. The overall composition is minimalistic and organic, highlighting the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. The lighting is soft, natural, and diffused, creating subtle shadows and enhancing the earthy tones of the ceramic. The background is simple and unobtrusive, perhaps a light wooden or stone surface with a hint of natural light.
instructions: Prepare oat milk: Combine oats and water. Blend until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or nut milk bag. Discard pulp or reserve for other use.
Ferment oat milk: Transfer strained oat milk to a clean jar. Cover with a breathable cloth. Let sit at room temperature (20-25°C) for 12-24 hours. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate.

Make panna cotta: In a saucepan, whisk fermented oat milk, agar-agar, maple syrup, and lemon zest. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, whisking constantly for 2 minutes. Dissolve agar-agar completely.
Pour panna cotta mixture into four 150 ml molds. Chill in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until set.
Prepare spiced pineapple: Dice pineapple into 1.5 cm cubes. Melt butter in a pan over medium heat. Add pineapple and cinnamon. Sauté for 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Add rum to pineapple. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing alcohol to evaporate and pineapple to caramelize lightly.

Prepare cherry compote: Combine pitted cherries, 15 ml lemon juice, and 15 ml maple syrup in a small saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat for 10-12 minutes, mashing some cherries, until sauce thickens. Cool completely.

To serve: Gently unmold panna cotta onto individual plates. Arrange spiced pineapple cubes beside panna cotta. Spoon cherry compote over or beside. Garnish with a small curl of fresh lemon zest or a tiny sprig of edible herb.
notes: For zero-waste, pineapple skin and core can be used to make fermented pineapple vinegar or tepache.
Oat pulp from making oat milk can be incorporated into baked goods like muffins or bread.
Adjust sweetness of panna cotta and compote to taste, depending on fruit ripeness.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Risotto with Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, free-flowing Chicken and Tomato Risotto is presented centrally on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto has a rich orange-red hue from the tomatoes, with visible golden-brown roasted chicken breast cut into 2cm chunks nestled throughout. Flecks of bright green chopped fresh basil are scattered over the top, along with a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese. The texture is moist and fluid, characteristic of a well-made risotto, not dry or stiff. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A silver fork and knife are placed to the right of the plate, and a folded white cotton napkin is positioned to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and fresh ingredients. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the creamy sauce
Pair with a light Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference
instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Let rest, then cut into 2cm chunks. Set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter over medium heat. Add finely diced onion and minced garlic. Cook 5 minutes until softened, without browning. This is the soffritto.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice grains. They should become slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add chopped tomatoes to the rice. Stir to combine.
Heat chicken broth in a separate saucepan. Keep it hot. Add one ladle of hot broth to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is almost fully absorbed.
Continue adding hot broth one ladle at a time. Stir constantly after each addition until absorbed. This process takes about 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Stir in cooked chicken chunks during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Ensure chicken is heated through.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and half of the chopped basil. Season with salt and pepper to taste. This step is called manteca.
Let risotto rest for 2 minutes, covered.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Cod with Mediterranean Roasted Vegetables and Couscous
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of baked cod is centrally placed on a bed of fluffy, golden whole wheat couscous on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The cod fillet, approximately 150g, is thick, opaque white, and gently flaky, showing a light golden crust from baking. Surrounding the fish and scattered artfully around the couscous are vibrant roasted Mediterranean vegetables. These include halved bright red cherry tomatoes, tender green zucchini cut into 1 cm thick half-moons, yellow bell pepper diced into 2 cm squares, and thinly sliced red onion. Dark, briny Kalamata olives, halved, are interspersed. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a verdant pop of color and freshness. A small lemon wedge rests beside the fish. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware beside it, under natural, even lighting, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the flavorful pan juices.
Pair with a simple, crisp green salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Cut zucchini into 1 cm thick half-moons. Dice bell pepper into 2 cm squares. Thinly slice red onion. Halve Kalamata olives.

In a large bowl, toss cherry tomatoes, zucchini, bell pepper, red onion, and olives with 30 ml olive oil, 5 ml dried oregano, 2.5 ml salt, and 1 ml black pepper. Spread vegetables evenly on a large baking tray.
Bake vegetables for 15 minutes.
While vegetables bake, pat cod fillets dry. Season each fillet generously with salt and black pepper.
Remove baking tray from oven. Nestle cod fillets among the roasted vegetables. Return to oven.
Bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until cod is opaque and flakes easily. Internal temperature should reach 63°C.

While fish bakes, prepare couscous. Bring 500 ml vegetable broth to a boil in a medium saucepan. Stir in 250 g whole wheat couscous. Cover the saucepan, remove from heat, and let stand for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Finely chop fresh parsley.
To serve, spoon a portion of couscous onto each plate. Top with a baked cod fillet and a generous portion of roasted Mediterranean vegetables. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge.
notes: For best results, use fresh, high-quality cod fillets.
This dish is versatile; other white fish like halibut or snapper can be substituted for cod.
Adjust roasting time for vegetables based on desired tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage, Spinach, and Smoked Provolone Soup
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Italian Sausage, Spinach, and Smoked Provolone Soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The soup features browned Italian sausage chunks, small diced soppressata, and thin diced salami pieces, all dispersed throughout a rich, savory tomato-based broth. Vibrant green wilted spinach leaves are interspersed, adding a fresh contrast. Melted smoked provolone cheese creates delightful, gooey pockets and swirls, lending a creamy texture. Colors are warm: deep reds from tomatoes, earthy browns from meats, bright green from spinach. The texture is comforting and robust. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed, simple cloth napkin. Warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, enhancing the homely, comforting atmosphere. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top. The entire bowl is visible, showcasing the ample portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add Italian sausage. Brown thoroughly, breaking into chunks. Cook to 75°C (167°F). Drain excess fat.
Add diced soppressata and salami to the pot. Sauté until slightly crispy.
Add diced onion and minced garlic. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add fresh spinach. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in smoked provolone cheese until melted and gooey.
Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes if desired.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: This soup is perfect for a comforting meal on a cold evening.
Adjust red pepper flakes to your preferred level of spice.

recipes.recipe_name: French Onion Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single whole bone-in chicken thigh sits centered in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl. The chicken is partially submerged in a rich, dark mahogany onion gravy filled with soft, caramelized thin half-moon onion slices. A thick layer of melted, slightly browned Gruyere cheese blankets the top of the chicken piece. Small specks of dried thyme are visible throughout the glossy sauce. The chicken skin at the edges shows a deep golden-brown sear. The bowl rests on a rustic, dark oak table next to a linen napkin and a small wooden board holding thick wedges of crusty baguette. Warm, soft kitchen lighting creates gentle highlights on the melted cheese and the viscous sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the onion gravy.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed in a sharp vinaigrette.
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine like Pinot Noir.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes.
Flip and sear for 4 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add butter and sliced onions to the same skillet.
Cook onions on medium heat for 20 minutes until dark brown.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in beef stock while stirring.
Add dried thyme to the sauce.
Place chicken back into the skillet.
Simmer for 15 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Sprinkle shredded cheese over the chicken pieces.
Cover the skillet for 2 minutes to melt the cheese.
notes: Do not rush the onions; deep caramelization is essential for flavor.
Use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches exactly 75°C.
If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of water or extra stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chili-Mustard Chicken with Root Vegetable Roast
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Chili-Mustard Chicken with Root Vegetable Roast is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, resting on a light bamboo table surface. The central element is a golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, its surface showing a subtle char and the texture of the chili-mustard marinade. Beside it, a rustic mound of creamy off-white cannellini bean puree provides a soft contrast. Around these, roasted potato halves, their skins lightly crisped, and caramelized yellow onion wedges with softened edges are artfully scattered. Vibrant halved cherry tomatoes add pops of rich red. The arrangement is natural and unforced, with ample white space on the plate, emphasizing the pure beauty of each ingredient. A few translucent, thinly sliced quick-pickled red onion rings are placed delicately on top of the chicken, adding a bright pink accent and a hint of tang. Fresh green parsley leaves are sparingly scattered for a final touch of color and freshness. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring soft natural lighting, with a hint of natural plant elements creating an eco-conscious, serene dining ambiance. The overall presentation is simple, clean, and highlights the inherent textures and colors of the sustainable ingredients.

ingredients.name: Small new potatoes or fingerling potatoes
Yellow onion, cut into thick wedges
Cannellini beans, canned, drained and rinsed
Fresh parsley or cilantro, for garnish

instructions: Trim chicken thighs. Pat dry.
In a bowl, combine Dijon mustard, cayenne pepper, minced garlic, chopped red chili, 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Coat chicken thighs thoroughly with marinade. Marinate at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours refrigerated.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut small potatoes into halves or quarters. Peel yellow onion. Cut into thick wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes.
On a baking tray, toss potatoes, onion wedges, and cherry tomatoes with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized.
Drain and rinse cannellini beans.
In a saucepan, combine beans, 2 minced garlic cloves, tomato paste, and vegetable stock. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Mash beans with a fork or potato masher for a rustic texture. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of olive oil.
Sear marinated chicken thighs presentation-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
For quick-pickled red onions: Thinly slice red onion into rings.
Combine equal parts hot water and apple cider vinegar in a small bowl. Add salt and sugar.
Submerge onion slices. Let sit for at least 15 minutes.
Spoon a generous dollop of bean puree onto the center of each plate.
Arrange roasted vegetables around the puree.
Place a cooked chicken thigh next to the vegetables.
Garnish with a few quick-pickled red onion rings and fresh parsley or cilantro leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.
Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until browned.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs.
Place chicken back into the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Whisk heavy cream and butter into the pan juices.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the sauce. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding cream to avoid curdling
Keep the skin above the liquid level during braising to maintain crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, hearty Spanish-Style Chicken Rice dish is presented centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features succulent, seared chicken thigh pieces, rich golden-yellow rice, and colorful diced red and green bell peppers. The rice, cooked to a tender, slightly moist consistency, is infused with smoked paprika and turmeric, creating an inviting hue. Scattered throughout the rice are small, tender cubes of roasted red and green bell peppers, alongside finely diced onions, adding pops of color and texture. The chicken pieces, each a whole, generously sized thigh, are deeply golden-brown from searing and nestled among the rice, showcasing their crisp skin and juicy interior. A sprinkle of vibrant fresh chopped parsley provides a final touch of green contrast. The plate is moderately filled, allowing for some negative space. A simple wooden table surface, a cotton napkin, and traditional flatware complete the clean, inviting bistro setting, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up juices.
Offer a side of simple green salad.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides. Remove chicken.
Dice onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper into 1 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Add onion and bell peppers to the skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and turmeric. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Add rice to the skillet. Stir to coat rice grains with vegetables and spices.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Check chicken internal temperature. It must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand covered 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust liquid if rice absorbs more slowly.
Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs can be used for richer flavor; increase cooking time slightly.
traditional_techniques: Simmering rice and meat together in one pot

recipes.recipe_name: Turkish Baked Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Turkish Baked Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Golden-brown roasted chicken thigh pieces, with their skin crisped, are arranged alongside tender, slightly caramelized potato wedges. Vibrant red diced tomatoes and softened green bell pepper chunks are interspersed, coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato-garlic sauce. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a fresh contrast. The composition is balanced, leaving moderate negative space around the edges of the plate. A piece of warm, fluffy Turkish pide bread rests beside the plate, and a small, white bowl of plain yogurt is nearby, completing the authentic Turkish casual dining experience. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm Turkish flatbread (pide or lavash).
Offer a side of plain strained yogurt (süzme yoğurt) for cooling contrast.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash chicken thighs. Pat dry.
Peel potatoes. Cut into thick wedges.
Peel onion. Slice into thick rings.
Wash bell pepper. Remove seeds. Cut into large chunks.
Wash tomatoes. Dice roughly. Mince garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, potato wedges, onion slices, bell pepper chunks, diced tomatoes, and minced garlic.
In a small bowl, whisk together tomato paste, olive oil, salt, black pepper, red pepper flakes, dried mint, and water or chicken broth.
Pour the sauce mixture over the chicken and vegetables. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly.
Transfer the mixture to a large baking dish or tray. Arrange ingredients in a single layer for even cooking.
Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden-brown. Turn chicken and potatoes halfway through baking for even browning.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
traditional_techniques: Use of Salça (Tomato Paste) as a flavor base

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Sausage, Crushed Potatoes & Broccoli with Fermented Stem Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of seared sausage, crushed potatoes, and vibrant green broccoli florets is artfully arranged on a round, matte cream-colored ceramic plate.
