traditional_techniques: Manual shaping and rolling of sweet confections (similar to Beijinho/Brigadeiro preparation)

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Spicy Beef with Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Sichuan Spicy Beef with Asparagus is meticulously arranged on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thinly sliced, seared beef pieces, boasting a rich dark brown hue, are intermingled with vibrant green, crisp-tender asparagus pieces, cut into 5cm lengths. A glossy, reddish-brown spicy garlic sauce lightly coats the ingredients, reflecting the natural light. Minced garlic and julienned ginger are visible within the sauce, alongside scattered red chili flakes and dark Sichuan peppercorns, providing pops of color and texture. The dish is garnished with bright green sliced spring onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds for visual contrast. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. Beside the plate, a small, separate white rice bowl and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are neatly placed on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's freshness and vibrant colors. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed white rice.
Offer a side of chili oil for those desiring extra heat.
instructions: Slice beef thinly against the grain. Combine beef with marinade ingredients: 15ml soy sauce, 15ml Shaoxing wine, 15g cornstarch, 5ml sesame oil, and a pinch of white pepper. Mix well. Let stand 15 minutes.
Prepare sauce: Whisk together 30ml soy sauce, 15ml rice vinegar, 15ml Shaoxing wine, 5g sugar, 5ml chili oil (if using), 5g cornstarch, and 60ml water or beef broth. Set aside.

Blanch asparagus: Bring a pot of salted water to boil. Trim tough ends of asparagus. Cut into 5cm pieces. Add asparagus to boiling water. Cook 1-2 minutes until crisp-tender. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain again.

Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over high heat until smoking. Add beef in a single layer. Sear 1-2 minutes per side until browned. Cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Remove beef from wok.

Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the wok. Reduce heat to medium-high. Add minced garlic, finely julienned ginger, dried red chilies cut into 1cm pieces, and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beef to the wok. Add blanched asparagus.
Stir sauce mixture well. Pour into the wok. Stir quickly until sauce thickens and coats ingredients, about 1 minute.
Transfer to serving plates. Garnish with sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust the amount of dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns to control spice level.
Velveting the beef with cornstarch and Shaoxing wine ensures tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Pickled Bell Pepper Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, allowing the natural colors of the ingredients to stand out. Small, vibrant green broccoli florets and thinly sliced stems are interspersed with bright red diced bell pepper, all lightly coated in a clear, golden vinaigrette. Small, irregular chunks of perfectly seared, pale chicken breast are nestled amongst the vegetables and fluffy, off-white brown rice. The composition is organic and flowing, with each component clearly visible, avoiding overcrowding. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley and a scattering of toasted pumpkin seeds provide natural garnish and textural contrast. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the ingredients' textures. The background is clean and minimalist, with a subtle hint of green from a potted plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Cut broccoli florets into small pieces. Thinly slice broccoli stems. Dice red bell pepper into small cubes.
In a saucepan, combine 250 ml water, 125 ml apple cider vinegar, 10 grams sea salt, and 5 ml maple syrup for the pickling brine. Bring to a simmer.
Pour hot brine over prepared broccoli and bell pepper in a heatproof jar. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Pat chicken breast dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through to 75°C internal temperature. Remove from heat. Let rest 5 minutes. Dice into small chunks.
If using day-old rice, gently fluff. If using fresh rice, cook according to package directions and cool completely.
In a small bowl, whisk together 60 ml olive oil, 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 10 grams Dijon mustard, 5 ml maple syrup, minced garlic, 2 grams sea salt, and 1 gram black pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine cooked rice, diced chicken, and the pickled broccoli and bell pepper (drain excess brine).
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Divide salad among four plates. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and toasted pumpkin seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Chicken Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Tomato & Chicken Rice is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. A whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh rests centrally on a bed of vibrant reddish-orange short-grain rice. The rice is loosely arranged, showcasing individual grains infused with the rich, deep color of fermented tomatoes. The chicken skin exhibits a subtle crisp texture, contrasting with the tender meat beneath. A few fresh green parsley leaves are scattered minimally for a hint of natural color. The plate is set on a light reclaimed wood table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring a subtle, out-of-focus plant element, emphasizing an eco-conscious and ingredient-focused aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Chicken stock (made from bones and vegetable scraps)

instructions: Prepare chicken stock: Simmer chicken bones (from thighs or extra) with onion peels, garlic skins, and 1 litre water for 30 minutes. Strain. Set aside 800ml hot stock.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear briefly for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Use a roughly chopped cut for the onion.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the rice. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the fermented tomato sauce and hot chicken stock. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Return the seared chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot tightly. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove pot from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Serve individual chicken thighs on a bed of rice. Garnish with a few fresh parsley or basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Picante con Berenjena y Tomate
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo Picante con Berenjena y Tomate is presented on a clean, round white ceramic dinner plate. Diced chicken pieces (3-4 cm cubes) are nestled among soft, cubed eggplant (2-3 cm) and chunky wedges of fresh Roma tomatoes. All ingredients are coated in a rich, reddish-orange, robust sauce, with visible sautéed red onion and red bell pepper. A generous scattering of vibrant green fresh cilantro leaves garnishes the top. The dish appears comforting and slightly rustic, with tender textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table. A small side bowl of fluffy white rice and warm corn tortillas are beside the main dish. A folded cotton napkin rests to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a subtly blurred casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of white rice.
Offer warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Garnish with extra fresh cilantro.
instructions: Dice chicken into 3-4 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Chop onion and bell pepper. Mince garlic. Add onion and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Cut eggplant into 2-3 cm cubes. Cut fresh Roma tomatoes into wedges. Add eggplant, fresh tomatoes, and canned diced tomatoes to the pot. Stir well.
Pour in chicken broth and hot sauce. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Stir to combine. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Uncover and cook for an additional 5-10 minutes if sauce needs to thicken slightly.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Stir in fresh chopped cilantro just before serving.
notes: Always ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Bell Pepper Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of hearty chicken and bell pepper soup is presented in a rustic, imperfect ceramic bowl with a subtly chipped rim, set on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-amber broth holds tender chunks of chicken and vibrantly colored diced bell peppers, carrots, and celery. The chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing their natural texture. Vegetables are clearly visible, with their natural colors. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center, allowing for natural negative space. A simple, comfortable spoon rests beside the bowl. Warm, soft light from a nearby kitchen window illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows. A casually folded plain cloth napkin sits nearby, contributing to a lived-in, homely atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a cozy family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread for dipping
Pair with a simple green salad
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Set aside.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery into 1 cm cubes. Mince garlic. Dice bell peppers into 1 cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and diced bell peppers. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Add dried thyme and bay leaf. Bring soup to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove bay leaf. Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For richer flavour, use homemade chicken broth.
Adjust vegetable quantities based on preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Wood Ear Mushroom & Edamame Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The 'Wood Ear Mushroom & Edamame Rice Salad' is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, mounded appealingly in the center. It showcases a vibrant medley of colors and textures: fluffy white long-grain rice, dark, wavy, thinly sliced wood ear mushrooms, and bright green shelled edamame. Crisp, pale green shredded cabbage and bright orange shredded carrots are interspersed throughout. Thinly sliced spring onions and fresh green coriander leaves add aromatic highlights. The salad is lightly coated in a glossy, chili-sesame vinaigrette, with a few visible chili flakes. The arrangement is organic and inviting, allowing each component to be seen without overcrowding. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by dark chopsticks and a folded cotton napkin, creating a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing main course or a substantial side dish.
Enjoy with chopsticks.
instructions: Cook rice according to package instructions. Fluff with a fork. Spread on a tray to cool completely.
Place dried wood ear mushrooms in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Let rehydrate for 20 minutes until tender. Drain well. Slice into thin strips.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add edamame. Cook for 2-3 minutes. Drain. Rinse with cold water to stop cooking. Drain again.
Shred cabbage thinly. Peel and shred carrots thinly.
Slice spring onions thinly on the diagonal. Roughly chop fresh coriander.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, grated ginger, minced garlic, and chili flakes. Mix until sugar dissolves.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled rice, sliced wood ear mushrooms, edamame, shredded cabbage, shredded carrots, sliced spring onions, and chopped coriander.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently until all components are evenly coated.
Serve immediately or chill for 30 minutes for flavors to meld. Garnish with extra coriander or chili flakes if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Gai Pad Med Mamuang (Chicken with Cashew Nuts)
recipes.visual_description: A single modest portion of Gai Pad Med Mamuang rests on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight rim. The stir-fried chicken chunks, approximately 2 cm cubes, are coated in a glossy, savory-sweet sauce, exhibiting a light golden-brown hue. Vibrant red and green bell pepper wedges, along with translucent onion wedges, are scattered among the chicken. Whole, toasted cashew nuts and a few rehydrated dried red chilies are visible throughout the dish, adding textural contrast. Spring onion batons provide a fresh green garnish. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, inviting look. Beside the main dish, a small, round bowl holds a serving of fluffy white jasmine rice. The setting is a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light. A plain cloth napkin is casually placed nearby.
instructions: Cut chicken into 2 cm cubes. Set aside.
Slice onion into 2 cm wedges. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm wedges. Slice spring onions into 3 cm batons. Mince garlic.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat.
Add cashew nuts and dried red chilies. Fry until cashews are golden and chilies are fragrant. Remove from pan. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic. Stir-fry for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken cubes to the wok. Stir-fry until chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). This takes about 5-7 minutes.
Add onion and bell peppers to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
In a small bowl, whisk together fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, palm sugar, and chicken broth.
Pour sauce mixture into the wok. Stir to coat all ingredients. Cook for 1 minute until sauce thickens slightly.
Return fried cashew nuts and dried chilies to the wok. Add spring onion batons. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Chicken Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Garlic Chicken Bake is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate with a slight rim, resting on a well-worn, light-stained wooden dining table. The golden-brown seared chicken thigh, a whole piece, is positioned slightly off-center. A rich, creamy garlic sauce, speckled with finely diced onion, pools generously around the chicken and lightly coats its top. Melted, bubbly shredded mozzarella cheese forms a golden-brown crust over the chicken, with some cheese visibly stretching. A sprinkling of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley adds a fresh contrast. The chicken shows its seared exterior and moist interior peeking from under the cheese. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light, casting soft shadows. A simple, folded beige linen napkin and a standard silver fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The background suggests a relaxed, lived-in family kitchen, with subtle hints of everyday kitchen items, maintaining focus on the comforting dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat dry chicken thighs. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in heavy cream and chicken broth. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and dried Italian herbs. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly. Cook for 2 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Top chicken with shredded mozzarella cheese.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and cheese is golden and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: This recipe is naturally low-carb and keto-friendly.
Serve with a simple green salad or steamed low-carb vegetables like broccoli or asparagus.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken Curry with Fresh Coriander
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Chicken Curry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is cut into tender, irregular chunks, submerged in a rich, reddish-brown, moderately thick curry sauce. The sauce shows flecks of green chili and a subtle sheen from the oil. A generous sprinkling of roughly chopped fresh green coriander leaves garnishes the center, adding a pop of vibrant color. The plate is positioned slightly off-center on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. Beside the plate, a small, white, round bowl holds a serving of fluffy white basmati rice. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests near the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating soft shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere. Traditional metal flatware is placed beside the plate. The composition is clean, professional, and balanced, showcasing the dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fluffy basmati rice.
Accompany with warm naan bread for dipping.
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip) or sliced red onion salad.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Slice green chilies thinly.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until soft and golden brown.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and sliced green chilies. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground coriander, ground cumin, turmeric powder, and red chili powder. Cook 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear chicken 3-4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, hot sauce, salt, and water or chicken broth. Stir well.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook 20-25 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove lid. Stir in garam masala. Cook uncovered 5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves before serving.
notes: Adjust green chilies and red chili powder to control spice level.
For richer flavor, use ghee instead of vegetable oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Penne al Pomodoro e Asparagi con Basilico Fresco
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Penne al Pomodoro e Asparagi con Basilico Fresco is presented in a wide, clean white porcelain bowl. Al dente penne pasta, coated in a rich, vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce, forms a slightly spiraled mound in the center. The sauce exhibits a smooth texture with hints of crushed tomato. Roasted asparagus spears, trimmed and tender-crisp with a slight char, are elegantly arranged on top of the pasta, some leaning against the mound, others peeking out. A generous scattering of fresh, bright green basil leaves provides a stark color contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese adds a subtle white accent. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple, warm-toned wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and a polished fork and spoon are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual, contemporary bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for 'fare la scarpetta' (sopping up the sauce).
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of light-bodied red wine, such as a Chianti or Barbera.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Toss asparagus with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp.
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic cloves.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large saucepan or deep skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in canned San Marzano tomatoes. Crush tomatoes with a spoon or your hands. Add a pinch of salt and pepper.
Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add penne pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add drained pasta directly to the tomato sauce.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and half of the fresh basil leaves (torn or roughly chopped) to the sauce and pasta. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Toss pasta vigorously to coat completely, allowing sauce to emulsify with pasta starch. This is 'mantecare'.
Plate individual portions of pasta into wide, shallow bowls. Arrange roasted asparagus spears artfully over the pasta.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves. Grate Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano-Reggiano over the top, if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: Using high-quality San Marzano tomatoes is crucial for the best sauce flavor.
Ensure pasta is cooked truly al dente for optimal texture and to absorb the sauce better.
The 'mantecare' step is essential for creating a cohesive and emulsified sauce that clings to the pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Tofu and Asparagus Crostini with White Truffle Sherry Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: The Smoked Tofu and Asparagus Crostini are arranged casually on a rustic wooden board, approximately 8-10 pieces. Each crostini starts with a golden-brown, toasted baguette slice, approximately 1.5 cm thick, providing a crisp base. A generous, creamy layer of mashed smoked tofu, off-white in color with visible small chunks, is spread across the bread. On top, tender-crisp asparagus pieces, cut into vibrant green 2-3 cm segments, are placed artfully. A delicate sheen of white truffle sherry drizzle coats the asparagus and tofu. Finely chopped fresh parsley, a vibrant green, is sprinkled over each canapé, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, showcasing natural textures and colors. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, with a simple, light-colored ceramic platter holding the crostini. Warm, soft lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its comfort food appeal. A casually folded cloth napkin sits nearby, completing the relaxed family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds or diagonals.
Brush both sides of baguette slices with 30 ml olive oil.
Place slices on a baking sheet. Bake 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Remove from oven.
Rub one side of each warm crostini with the peeled garlic clove.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add asparagus spears.
Blanch asparagus for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Cut blanched asparagus into 2-3 cm pieces.
In a bowl, mash the smoked tofu with a fork until mostly smooth. Leave some small chunks for texture.
Add 30 ml dry sherry, 15 ml olive oil, salt, and black pepper to the mashed tofu. Mix well to combine.
Spread a generous layer of the smoked tofu mixture onto each garlic-rubbed crostini.
Arrange 2-3 pieces of blanched asparagus on top of the tofu spread on each crostini.
In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 15 ml olive oil, 15 ml dry sherry, and 10 ml white truffle oil.
Drizzle the sherry-truffle mixture evenly over each assembled crostini.
Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pad Krapow Gai (Thai Basil Chicken) with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, professional restaurant-style portion of Pad Krapow Gai (Thai Basil Chicken) with Jasmine Rice. The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of fluffy white jasmine rice sits neatly on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the rice, the vibrant stir-fried chicken mixture is arranged. The chicken mince is cooked to a golden-brown, interspersed with thinly sliced brown onion, bright red chili slices, and wilted, dark green holy basil leaves. The sauce gives the chicken a glossy, rich brown coating. The textures are varied: tender chicken, slightly crisp onion, and soft rice. The overall color palette is warm and inviting, with contrasting greens, reds, and browns against the white rice. A perfectly fried egg with a crispy edge and a runny yolk is placed on top of the chicken. The plate is well-proportioned with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro. The dish rests on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, highlighting its fresh appearance and textures. Traditional chopsticks are placed beside the plate, and a small, traditional ceramic bowl, possibly containing prik nam pla (fish sauce with chilies), sits subtly in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a fried egg (Kai Dao) on top.
Accompanied by a small bowl of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies).
Typically eaten with a fork and spoon, or chopsticks.
instructions: Cook jasmine rice. Rinse rice until water runs clear. Combine rice with 450ml water in a saucepan. Bring to boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand 10 minutes. Fluff with fork.
Prepare sauce. Combine fish sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, palm sugar, and 60ml water in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat. Add minced garlic and sliced chilies. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chicken mince. Break up chicken with a spoon. Stir-fry until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add thinly sliced brown onion. Stir-fry 2 minutes until softened.
Pour in prepared sauce. Stir well to coat chicken. Cook 1-2 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in holy basil leaves until just wilted.
Optional: Fry eggs. Heat 15ml oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Fry eggs one at a time until whites are crispy and yolks are runny.
Serve immediately. Plate a portion of jasmine rice. Spoon Pad Krapow Gai next to it. Top with a fried egg if desired.
notes: For authentic flavor, use holy basil (krapow). If unavailable, Thai basil is a suitable substitute.
Adjust chili quantity for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato Consommé with Herb Stem Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of this minimalist soup is presented in a handcrafted, round ceramic bowl of natural cream or beige tone. The consommé, a translucent, delicate amber hue, fills the bowl, offering clean depth. Vibrant green herb stem oil is artfully drizzled on the consommé's surface, creating an organic pattern. A few irregularly shaped, reddish-brown dehydrated tomato skin crisps are delicately placed on the liquid or leaning against the bowl's rim, providing textural contrast. The plating emphasizes negative space, allowing the pure beauty of the liquid and its subtle garnishes to stand out. The bowl rests on a light-toned, naturally textured surface, such as reclaimed wood. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the liquid's clarity and garnish crispness. The background is clean, with a hint of blurred green foliage, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Assorted vegetable scraps (carrot peels, onion ends, celery trimmings, mushroom stems, parsley stems)

instructions: Wash and halve or quarter tomatoes. Place in a clean 1-litre jar. Sprinkle with sea salt. Gently press tomatoes to release some juice. Ensure tomatoes are submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed. Seal with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 7-14 days. Taste for desired tanginess.
Strain fermented tomatoes through a fine-mesh sieve. Reserve skins and tomato solids separately. Gently press solids to extract all juice. Do not press too hard if you want a clearer consommé later.
Combine vegetable scraps and water in a large pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 45 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.

Combine strained tomato juice and vegetable scrap broth. Chill well. Whisk egg whites until frothy. Gently fold egg whites into cold broth. Heat slowly over medium-low heat. Do not stir once it starts to heat. A "raft" will form on top. Simmer gently for 20 minutes. Carefully ladle clear consommé from the side or strain through a cheesecloth-lined sieve without disturbing the raft. Discard raft.
Wash herb stems. Roughly chop. Blend stems with neutral oil until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth to extract vibrant green oil. Discard solids.

Preheat oven to 100°C. Spread reserved tomato skins in a single layer on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Dehydrate in oven for 1-2 hours, or until completely crisp. Monitor closely to prevent burning. Skins should be brittle. Store in an airtight container.

Gently warm clarified consommé. Do not boil. Pour 200 ml of warm consommé into each serving bowl. Drizzle a small amount of herb stem oil on the surface. Garnish with a few dehydrated tomato skin crisps. Serve immediately.
notes: The fermentation time for tomatoes can be adjusted based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.
For maximum clarity, the consommé can be passed through a coffee filter after the egg white clarification step.
Ensure all components are prepared and ready before assembling for best presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Sausage and Corn Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: Two vibrantly colored bell pepper halves, one red and one yellow, are generously stuffed with a savory, browned sausage and corn filling. The roasted peppers show slight charring on their edges, their tender skins contrasting with the hearty, crumbly texture of the sausage, diced onion, and golden corn kernels inside. A simple, slightly glistening strawberry-oregano sauce is drizzled over one pepper half and a small pool rests beside the other. The dish is presented on an off-white, rustic ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-worn wooden dining table. A simple fork and knife are set beside the plate, and a casually folded linen napkin completes the homely, inviting scene under warm, natural kitchen light.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Halve bell peppers lengthwise. Remove seeds and membranes. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Tear bread slices into small pieces. Process into coarse bread crumbs using a food processor or by hand.
Remove sausage casings. Crumble sausage meat into a large skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until browned and cooked through, breaking up lumps. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from skillet.
Add olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion and any trimmed bell pepper pieces. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in cooked sausage, corn kernels, bread crumbs, and dried oregano. Pour in chicken broth. Mix well. Season with salt and black pepper.
Spoon sausage mixture evenly into bell pepper halves. Pour 50ml water into the bottom of the baking dish. Cover dish tightly with foil.
Bake 30 minutes. Remove foil. Bake an additional 15-20 minutes, or until peppers are tender and filling is heated through.

While peppers bake, prepare strawberry sauce: Combine strawberries, sugar (if using), and red wine vinegar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook 5-7 minutes, mashing strawberries with a spoon, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Serve stuffed bell peppers hot with a drizzle of the strawberry-oregano sauce.
notes: Ensure sausage is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken and Asparagus Rigatoni with Burst Cherry Tomatoes and Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared Chicken and Asparagus Rigatoni is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Al dente rigatoni pasta is loosely arranged in the center, coated in a light, vibrant tomato-based sauce. Irregularly cut, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among the pasta. Bright green, crisp-tender asparagus batons and burst cherry tomatoes, some still whole, are distributed throughout, adding pops of color. Fresh, large basil leaves are generously scattered over the top. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and a delicate swirl of extra virgin olive oil finish the dish. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, with a subtle, blurred modern bistro background featuring neutral tones and a hint of wall texture, ensuring the dish remains the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Cut into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to skillet. Add finely diced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and optional red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cherry tomatoes to skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most tomatoes burst and release their juices.
Deglaze skillet with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Add asparagus cut into 4 cm batons. Cook 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return seared chicken to skillet with sauce. Add cooked rigatoni and reserved pasta water. Toss to coat.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the fresh basil leaves, roughly torn. Grate in half of the Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.
Ensure pasta is cooked al dente for best texture.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (implied with shallot and garlic base)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Garlic Herb Butter, Creamy Mashed Potatoes, and Roasted Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Pan-Seared Beef Medallions is centrally plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two thick, seared beef medallions, cooked to a perfect medium-rare, are positioned side-by-side, showcasing their rich, golden-brown crust. A dollop of melting garlic herb butter rests atop one medallion. Adjacent to the beef is a generous, smooth scoop of creamy mashed potatoes. Around the plate, vibrant red roasted cherry tomatoes, some slightly burst, are artfully scattered. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley over the beef and potatoes, adding a pop of green. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple, light wooden table surface, a folded cotton napkin, and polished silver flatware, all under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro ambiance.

ingredients.name: Red chili flakes
ingredients.quantity: 1/2 teaspoon (or 1 small fresh red chili, minced)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and cut potatoes into large chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.

While potatoes cook, prepare garlic herb butter. Melt 50g butter in a small pan. Add minced garlic and chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in 2 tablespoons chopped parsley. Set aside.
Toss cherry tomatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast in preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, until tender and slightly burst. Set aside.
Return drained potatoes to the pot. Add remaining 50g butter and milk/cream. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large cast-iron or heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place beef medallions in the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or longer for desired doneness. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Remove beef from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

To plate, place a scoop of creamy mashed potatoes on each white porcelain plate. Arrange two beef medallions beside the potatoes. Spoon some garlic herb butter over the beef. Scatter roasted cherry tomatoes around the plate. Garnish with remaining fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Macaroni with Bolognese and Mozzarella Crust
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of baked macaroni is served in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl, showcasing its comforting, hearty appeal. The top layer features a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted mozzarella and crispy, toasted breadcrumbs. Beneath the crust, rich, deep red Bolognese sauce is visible, interspersed with tender, plump macaroni pasta. The pasta is coated in the savory sauce, with hints of creamy béchamel adding a subtle lightness. A few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are artfully torn and scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, evoking a cozy yet refined bistro ambiance. The composition is clean and professional, focusing on the dish's inviting textures and warm colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add ground beef and pork to the pot. Break up meat with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine is mostly evaporated.
Add crushed tomatoes and 100 ml whole milk. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for at least 1 hour, or up to 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
While Bolognese simmers, prepare breadcrumbs. Pulse stale bread in a food processor until fine crumbs form. Toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Set aside.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Prepare béchamel sauce: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in 500 ml whole milk until smooth. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine cooked macaroni with Bolognese sauce and béchamel sauce in a large bowl. Stir until well coated.
Transfer half of the macaroni mixture to a 2.5-liter baking dish. Layer with half of the shredded mozzarella.
Add remaining macaroni mixture. Top with remaining mozzarella and grated Parmesan cheese. Sprinkle breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbling and the cheese and breadcrumbs are golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Sun-Dried Tomato Puree
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, minimalist plate of Orecchiette pasta sits centrally on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The pasta, perfectly al dente, is tossed in a rich, reddish-orange sun-dried tomato puree, coating each ear-shaped piece. Interspersed throughout are plump, roasted cherry tomatoes, some gently burst, adding pockets of bright red and juicy texture. Thinly sliced garlic is visible, subtly integrated into the sauce. Fresh basil leaves, some whole, some chiffonade, are scattered generously over the pasta, providing contrasting green color and freshness. A sprinkle of golden toasted pine nuts adds a delicate crunch. Grated Pecorino Romano cheese lightly dusts the top, offering a final savory touch. The dish has a natural, organic mound shape, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. It is presented on a simple wooden table, with a cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate, under soft, natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss cherry tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly blistered.
While tomatoes roast, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add orecchiette and cook according to package instructions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml pasta cooking water.
Meanwhile, toast pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until golden. Set aside.
In a large skillet, heat 30 ml olive oil over medium-low heat.
Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
In a food processor, combine drained sun-dried tomatoes with 15 ml olive oil and 60 ml reserved pasta water. Process until a smooth puree forms.
Add sun-dried tomato puree to the skillet with garlic. Stir to combine.
Add roasted cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Gently mash some with the back of a spoon to release juices.
Add cooked orecchiette to the skillet. Toss to coat evenly with the sauce.
Add remaining 60 ml pasta water, a little at a time, if needed, to achieve desired sauce consistency.
Stir in half of the fresh basil, torn. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish with remaining fresh basil, toasted pine nuts, and grated Pecorino Romano.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard-Crusted Beef with Taleggio Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick-cut beef sirloin steak, pan-seared to a perfect medium-rare, rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The steak boasts a rich, golden-brown crust from the mustard, showcasing a crisp, savory exterior. Beside it, a generous pool of creamy, pale orange Taleggio sauce, smooth and luxurious, flows naturally, partially embracing the base of the steak. The sauce's subtle warmth contrasts with the steak's robust appearance. A delicate scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant green accent, enhancing the dish's color palette. The presentation is clean and inviting, with appropriate negative space around the elements, conveying a refined yet approachable restaurant style. The entire plate is visible, set on a simple wooden surface with a folded cotton napkin and standard European flatware, under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side of roasted potatoes or a fresh green salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat beef steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides. Spread Dijon mustard evenly over one side of each steak.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place steaks mustard-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes until a deep golden-brown crust forms. Flip steaks. Sear for another 3-4 minutes for medium-rare, or longer for desired doneness.
Remove steaks from pan. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5-7 minutes.
While steaks rest, reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add finely diced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let wine reduce by half, about 2 minutes.

Stir in double cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add Taleggio cheese, cut into small cubes. Stir continuously until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth and creamy. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Chop fresh parsley finely.
Serve each steak with a generous spoon of Taleggio cream sauce. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: For food safety, ensure beef reaches desired internal temperature. A medium-rare steak is typically 55-60°C (130-140°F), medium 60-65°C (140-150°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Vegan Strawberry Dark Chocolate Pecan Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single Vegan Strawberry Dark Chocolate Pecan Tartlet is presented on a clean white porcelain dessert plate. The crust is a golden-brown, rustic pecan shortcrust, baked to a crisp finish and forming a neat individual tartlet shell. Inside, a smooth, glossy dark chocolate ganache fills the shell, showcasing its rich, deep brown color. Arranged artfully on top are vibrant red fresh strawberries, halved or quartered, creating a natural, slightly mounded appearance. A light dusting of powdered sugar gently covers the strawberries and the edges of the tartlet. A small, fresh green mint sprig is placed subtly beside the tartlet for a pop of color. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting, highlighting the dessert as the sole focus.
instructions: Prepare Crust: In a food processor, pulse pecans, flour, and 50g sugar until fine. Add cold vegan butter. Pulse until pea-sized crumbs form. Add ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, pulsing until dough just comes together. Do not overmix.
Chill Dough: Form dough into a disc. Wrap in plastic. Chill 30 minutes.

Form Tartlets: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Roll dough on a floured surface to 3mm thickness. Cut out four circles to fit 10cm tartlet pans. Press dough into pans. Trim edges. Prick bottoms with a fork.

Blind Bake: Line each shell with parchment paper. Fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake 5-7 more minutes until golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.

Make Ganache: Place chopped dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat coconut milk in a small saucepan until simmering. Pour hot coconut milk over chocolate. Let sit 5 minutes. Stir until smooth. Stir in agave nectar if using.
Fill Tartlets: Pour ganache into cooled tartlet shells. Refrigerate at least 2 hours, or until ganache is set.
Prepare Strawberries: Halve or quarter strawberries depending on size. In a small bowl, gently toss strawberries with 20g sugar and lemon juice. Let sit 10 minutes.
Assemble and Serve: Arrange macerated strawberries on top of the set ganache in each tartlet. Dust lightly with powdered sugar. Garnish with a fresh mint sprig if desired. Serve chilled.
notes: Ensure coconut milk is full-fat for best ganache consistency.
Do not overmix crust dough to keep it tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple Crisp with Rosemary Maple
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a sustainable, minimalistic dessert is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The composition is clean and focused, honoring natural textures and colors. At the center, a modest mound of naturally fermented apple cubes, cut into irregular 2 cm chunks, showcases a pale, slightly opaque off-white hue, reflecting their gentle fermentation. Each apple piece retains its original shape, offering a soft, yielding texture. Scattered over and around the apples are clusters of golden-brown buckwheat crisp. The crisp offers a pronounced, irregular texture, ranging from small individual groats to larger, craggier formations, providing a visual contrast to the apples. A thin, glistening trail of amber rosemary-infused maple syrup is artfully drizzled over the top, catching the light and adding a subtle sheen. The plate is largely empty, emphasizing negative space and the purity of the ingredients. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a light-colored, natural wood surface providing a subtle texture. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the food's natural beauty. A folded, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly placed to the side.
instructions: Wash apples. Do not peel. Core and cut into 2 cm cubes.
Dissolve 10 g sea salt in 500 ml filtered water to make a brine.
Place apple cubes in a clean glass jar. Pour brine over apples, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Ferment at room temperature (18-22°C) for 3-5 days, or until apples are tangy and slightly bubbly. Taste daily. Once desired tanginess is reached, refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Combine buckwheat groats, 30 ml maple syrup, melted coconut oil, and a pinch of sea salt in a bowl. Mix well.
Spread mixture in a single layer on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and crispy. Let cool completely on the baking sheet; it will crisp further. Break into small clusters.
In a small saucepan, gently heat 60 ml maple syrup with the rosemary sprig over low heat for 5 minutes. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Let steep for 10 minutes. Remove rosemary sprig.
Drain fermented apple cubes.
Divide fermented apples among four small dessert plates.
Sprinkle buckwheat crisp generously over the apples.
Drizzle with rosemary maple syrup. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Corn and Tomato Salad with Fermented Chili Dressing
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream or light beige tone, reflecting natural pottery. Roasted cherry tomatoes, vibrant red and yellow bell pepper pieces, and golden corn kernels are artfully arranged, showcasing their natural colors and slightly charred textures. Interspersed among them are crisp, golden-brown sourdough croutons, torn into irregular, organic shapes, and delicate, thinly sliced pink quick-pickled red onions. A generous drizzle of the orange-hued fermented chili dressing lightly coats the ingredients, adding a subtle sheen without pooling. The composition is clean and minimalistic, with ample white space on the plate, emphasizing the pure beauty of each ingredient. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone, and soft, diffused natural lighting. The background is clean and unobtrusive, with hints of natural greenery or a simple plant, maintaining an eco-conscious and serene aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Remove corn kernels from cobs. Deseed red bell pepper and cut into 2cm pieces. Cut half of the red onion into 2cm wedges. Thinly slice the remaining half of the red onion.

On a large baking sheet, toss halved cherry tomatoes, corn kernels, bell pepper pieces, and red onion wedges with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and slightly charred.

While vegetables roast, tear stale sourdough bread into 2-3cm pieces. Spread on a separate baking sheet. Lightly drizzle with a small amount of olive oil. Toast in the oven alongside vegetables for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy.
Place thinly sliced red onion in a small bowl. Pour over just enough apple cider vinegar to cover, add a pinch of salt. Let sit for at least 10 minutes. Drain before using.

For the Fermented Chili Dressing: Mince garlic. In a small bowl, whisk together fermented chili paste, minced garlic, 60ml extra virgin olive oil, 30ml apple cider vinegar, and optional maple syrup. Season with a pinch of salt. Whisk until well combined.
In a large bowl, combine roasted vegetables, drained quick-pickled red onion, and crispy sourdough croutons.
Drizzle generously with the prepared Fermented Chili Dressing. Gently toss to coat all ingredients.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Linguine with Seared King Prawns, Sun-Dried Tomato Pesto, and Burst Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of linguine is neatly twirled and centered in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta glistens with a rich, vibrant sun-dried tomato and cherry tomato sauce, showcasing shades of deep red and bright orange. Four plump, golden-brown seared king prawns are arranged elegantly on top of the pasta, their natural curl adding visual interest. Halved, burst cherry tomatoes and finely minced garlic are interspersed throughout the sauce, adding pops of color and texture. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered artfully, providing a fresh contrast. A light dusting of grated Parmigiano Reggiano and a sprinkle of bright yellow lemon zest complete the dish. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's fresh, inviting appearance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Pair with a light, crisp white wine such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio
instructions: Prepare sun-dried tomato pesto. Combine drained sun-dried tomatoes, pine nuts, 2 minced garlic cloves, half the fresh basil, 50g Parmigiano Reggiano, and 80ml olive oil in a food processor. Process until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add linguine. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water before draining. Drain pasta and set aside.
While pasta cooks, pat king prawns dry with paper towels. Season prawns with salt and black pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add seasoned prawns in a single layer. Sear 1-2 minutes per side until opaque and pink. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove prawns from skillet and set aside.

In the same skillet, add remaining 5ml olive oil and 15g butter. Add halved cherry tomatoes and remaining minced garlic. Sauté 3-4 minutes until tomatoes soften and burst. Add red pepper flakes if using.
Add the prepared sun-dried tomato pesto to the skillet with the tomatoes. Stir to combine.
Add drained linguine and 125ml reserved pasta water to the skillet. Toss vigorously to coat pasta in sauce. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Return seared prawns to the skillet. Gently toss to combine and heat through.
Stir in fresh lemon juice and lemon zest.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil leaves and extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: Ensure pasta is cooked al dente for best texture.
Do not overcook the prawns; they cook quickly.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Heart and Celery Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Beef Heart and Celery Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features tender, slow-simmered beef heart chunks (approx. 2.5 cm cubes), diced celery, carrots, and onions, all suspended in a rich, thick, savory brown gravy. The vegetables are softened from braising, their natural colors muted but still distinct. A light scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a touch of color. The stew fills the bowl naturally, with components overlapping. A simple, off-white cloth napkin and basic stainless steel flatware are casually arranged beside the bowl. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve over mashed potatoes or egg noodles
instructions: Trim beef heart of sinew and fat. Cut into 2.5 cm cubes.
Season beef heart cubes with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown beef heart in batches until well-sealed on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion, celery, and carrots to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Gradually whisk in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef heart to the pot. Add bay leaves and dried thyme.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until beef heart is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: French Green Lentil and Mushroom Ragout
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of French Green Lentil and Mushroom Ragout is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The ragout forms an earthy, deep brown-green base, rich with visible tender green lentils, sautéed mushroom pieces, and softened diced carrots and onions. Its texture is thick yet moist, inviting and hearty. Arranged elegantly atop the ragout are vibrant elements: bright green, tender-crisp green bean batons (4-5 cm long) and glistening, tender-crisp glazed carrot batons (4-5 cm long). These vegetables provide a beautiful color contrast and textural variation. A delicate sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a final touch of fresh green and aromatic brightness to the dish. The overall plating is clean, balanced, and professional, leaving moderate negative space around the food. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware, and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting in a soft-focus bistro-style background, honoring the dish's French heritage with contemporary simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette for dipping into the rich ragout.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (approx. 150g) cut into batons for glazing

instructions: Rinse lentils thoroughly under cold water.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion and diced carrots. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 7-8 minutes until mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze. Reduce liquid by half.
Add rinsed lentils, 750 ml vegetable broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf to the pot. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Stir occasionally. Add more broth if ragout becomes too dry.

While ragout simmers, prepare glazed carrots. Melt butter in a small pan. Add carrot batons and 60 ml water. Season with a pinch of salt. Cover the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until carrots are tender-crisp.
Uncover the pan. Increase heat. Cook until water evaporates and carrots are lightly glazed.
Blanch green bean batons: Bring a separate pot of salted water to a boil. Add green bean batons. Cook for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Plunge blanched green beans into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf from the lentil ragout. Season ragout with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Ladle a generous portion of the lentil and mushroom ragout onto each plate. Artfully arrange glazed carrots and blanched green beans on top of the ragout.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Green lentils are preferred for this recipe as they hold their shape well during cooking, contributing to the ragout's texture.
Adjust the amount of vegetable broth to achieve your desired ragout consistency; add more for a looser ragout, or simmer longer for a thicker one.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Shrimp and Sun-Dried Tomato Penne
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of spicy shrimp and sun-dried tomato penne rigate is artfully plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The al dente penne is coated in a vibrant, rustic red sauce, showcasing halved bright red cherry tomatoes, plump pink seared shrimp, and small, creamy white bocconcini mozzarella balls. Finely minced garlic and visible red pepper flakes add textural interest and a hint of heat. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered generously over the top, providing a fresh aromatic contrast. The dish is arranged organically, allowing some negative space around the edges. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table. A classic silver fork rests beside the plate on a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, inviting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer freshly grated Pecorino Romano or Parmigiano Reggiano cheese at the table for individual preference.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook penne rigate according to package directions until al dente.

While pasta cooks, heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season shrimp with salt and pepper. Add shrimp to skillet. Sear 2 minutes per side, until pink and cooked through. Remove shrimp from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped sun-dried tomatoes and halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 3-4 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
If using, pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Cook 1 minute until liquid reduces.
Drain cooked pasta, reserving 120 ml of pasta water. Add pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Add seared shrimp.
Add halved mozzarella bocconcini and torn fresh basil. Toss to combine. Add a splash of reserved pasta water as needed to create a light sauce. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.
Use high-quality oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken & Root Vegetable Grain Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, natural-toned ceramic plate, possibly cream or beige, with ample white space. At the center, a bed of earthy brown rice provides a textural base. Alongside, golden-brown roasted potato chunks, irregularly shaped, are arranged organically. Sliced, seared chicken pieces, cooked to a rich brown, are nestled nearby. They are not fanned but presented as whole, substantial cuts. A vibrant heap of pale green, quick lacto-fermented shredded cabbage offers a contrasting tangy element. Thinly sliced bright red radishes and orange carrot ribbons are artfully scattered, adding fresh color and crispness. A few delicate, crispy potato skins or carrot peel crisps are placed sparingly for texture and a zero-waste touch. The overall composition is clean, unforced, and highlights the natural colors and textures of each ingredient. The plate sits on a light, textured bamboo or reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the purity and simplicity of the ingredients. A minimalist background, possibly with a hint of green plant life, maintains focus on the dish. A single individual portion is shown.

ingredients.name: fresh herbs (e.g., parsley, dill, or chives)

instructions: Prepare Quick Lacto-Fermented Cabbage: In a clean jar, combine shredded cabbage, 5g salt, and 100 ml filtered water. Ensure cabbage is submerged. Seal loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours until slightly tangy. Refrigerate.

Cook Brown Rice: Rinse brown rice. Combine 200g rice, 500 ml water, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare Potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash 400g potatoes thoroughly. If using larger potatoes, cut into 2-3 cm chunks. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.

Prepare Chicken: Pat 600g chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, toss chicken with 50 ml lacto-fermented vegetable brine, salt, and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest for 5 minutes, then slice into 1.5 cm thick pieces.

Prepare Zero-Waste Crisps (Optional): If using potato skins, wash thoroughly. Toss with a tiny bit of olive oil and salt. Bake alongside potatoes or separately at 200°C until crispy, about 10-15 minutes. If using carrot peels, toss with olive oil and salt, bake until crispy.
Prepare Seasonal Vegetables: Thinly slice 100g radishes. For 150g carrots, either slice thinly or use a peeler to create ribbons.

Assemble Bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among four shallow bowls. Arrange roasted potato chunks and sliced chicken alongside the rice. Add a generous portion of quick lacto-fermented cabbage. Arrange fresh radish slices and carrot ribbons. Garnish with potato skin or carrot peel crisps and fresh herbs, if using.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Dijonnaise
recipes.visual_description: A single, seared golden-brown chicken thigh, presented whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, creamy, pale yellow Dijon sauce generously pools around the base of the chicken, showcasing small, vibrant red diced tomato pieces and soft translucent diced onion within. The chicken skin is taut and caramelized, contrasting with the smooth, glossy sauce. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley adds a pop of bright green. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside it. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's textures. The background is a soft, blurred restaurant setting, suggesting a casual yet refined atmosphere. The overall presentation is clean and professional.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with classic accompaniments such as creamy mashed potatoes or steamed green beans.
Offer crusty baguette for soaking up the rich sauce.
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside and keep warm.
Add butter to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium.
Add finely diced onion to the pan. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened and translucent.
Stir in diced tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Whisk in Dijon mustard until the sauce is smooth.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, allowing chicken to absorb flavors.
Remove chicken again. Stir heavy cream into the sauce. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve each chicken thigh with a generous spoon of the creamy Dijon sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Artichoke & Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Fermented Artichoke & Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta is presented on a handcrafted, natural ceramic plate in a light cream tone. The short pasta, coated in a light, glossy sauce, forms a natural mound in the center of the plate, leaving ample white space around the edges. Vibrant red bell pepper batons, deep red sun-dried tomato slices, and quartered fermented artichoke hearts are visibly interspersed throughout the pasta, offering distinct shapes and colors. Wilted green spinach leaves provide a soft textural contrast. A light scattering of golden, toasted sourdough breadcrumbs crowns the dish, adding a rustic texture. A few fresh oregano leaves are gently placed on top as a simple, natural garnish. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing the natural colors and textures. A clean, minimalist background with a subtle, blurred green plant suggests an eco-conscious environment, focusing entirely on the pure beauty and simplicity of the ingredients.
instructions: Prepare breadcrumbs: Tear stale sourdough bread into small pieces. Process in a food processor until fine crumbs form. Toast crumbs in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and crisp. Set aside.

Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta cooking water before draining. Drain pasta and set aside.

Sauté vegetables: Heat olive oil and reserved sun-dried tomato oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add bell pepper batons and cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Add sliced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Build sauce: Stir in thinly sliced sun-dried tomatoes, quartered fermented artichoke hearts, and chopped fresh oregano. Pour in vegetable stock and 60ml of the reserved artichoke brine. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.

Combine: Add cooked pasta to the pan with the sauce. Add chopped spinach and nutritional yeast. Toss well to combine, ensuring spinach wilts. If the sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Season: Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Add a squeeze of lemon juice if desired for brightness.
Serve: Divide pasta among four plates. Garnish each serving with a sprinkle of toasted sourdough breadcrumbs and a few fresh oregano leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Lentil Coconut Dahl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, creamy Red Lentil Coconut Dahl is presented in a deep, rustic earthenware bowl. The dahl has a warm, inviting orange-yellow hue, with a visibly smooth yet hearty texture from the cooked red lentils. A delicate swirl of lighter coconut milk sits on the surface. Fresh, vibrant green chopped coriander leaves are scattered across the top as a functional garnish. Next to the bowl, on a well-used, warm wooden dining table, rests a piece of fluffy naan bread or a small mound of steamed basmati rice, ready for scooping. A small ceramic bowl holds a side of bright green mint chutney or a dark red pickle. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen light, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere. The table shows natural imperfections; a casually placed cloth napkin completes the authentic family dining setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed basmati rice
Serve with warm naan bread or roti
Offer a side of raita (yogurt dip)
Include Indian pickles or chutneys
instructions: Rinse red lentils until water runs clear.
Combine lentils and 700ml water in a large pot. Bring to a boil. Skim any foam.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer 15-20 minutes until lentils are tender. Stir occasionally.
Add diced tomato, turmeric powder, cumin powder, and coriander powder to the lentils. Mix well.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir. Simmer 5-7 minutes more. Season with salt.
Heat oil or ghee in a small pan for tempering (tadka). Add mustard seeds. Let them splutter.
Add cumin seeds and curry leaves. Fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour the tempered spices (tadka) into the simmering dahl. Stir immediately.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust water quantity to achieve desired dahl consistency; add more if you prefer a thinner dahl.
For extra heat, add a slit green chili to the dahl while simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Tomatoes and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef with Tomatoes and Herbs is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thick, irregular chunks of dark brown, fall-apart tender braised beef are nestled within a rich, glossy reddish-brown tomato and herb sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top, providing a pop of color. The beef chunks are prominently displayed. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the dish. A small, rustic white bowl with fluffy rice pilaf is placed to the side, completing the Mediterranean casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with rice pilaf or crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a side of Greek yogurt or feta cheese.
instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Return beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, beef broth, dried oregano, and bay leaves.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. Add a splash of water or broth if sauce becomes too thick.
Remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Paneer and Curry Leaf Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of rich, creamy Paneer and Curry Leaf Curry is presented on a rustic, everyday ceramic plate. The curry has a warm, inviting yellow-orange hue, with visible white cubes of paneer nestled within the sauce. A few fresh, vibrant green curry leaves are casually scattered on top as a garnish. The dish is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. A simple metal spoon rests beside the plate. The lighting is warm and cozy, emanating from kitchen fixtures, highlighting the comforting appeal of the dish. Portions are modest and natural, with the curry filling the plate adequately without overcrowding, allowing some negative space. The paneer is cut into thick, uniform cubes.
